a_rows_sample.anchor: The Annotated Bilattice Kernel (ABK-1) extends First-Degree Entailment (FDE / Belnap-Dunn 4-valued logic) to eliminate the structural distinction collapses identified in prior kernel evaluations ... ABK-1 resolves these deficiencies by embedding the standard 4-valued truth space BF_4 into an Annotated Bilattice Frame B_ABK. Each proposition is represented as an annotated truth tuple that pairs an FDE valuation with a justification graph, a temporal validity window, and modal/scope metadata.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces ABK-1: an architecture that embeds standard 4-valued FDE (BF_4) into an Annotated Bilattice Frame, pairing each proposition's FDE valuation with a justification graph, temporal validity window, and modal/scope metadata, explicitly targeting the lineage/temporal/underdetermined collapses previously measured against bare FDE (this batch's r-req-fde-kernel-test-vectors-result).

a_rows_sample.anchor: State(phi) = <nu(phi), J(phi), tau(phi), mu(phi)> ... FDE Truth Valuation nu in BF_4 ... Justification Graph J = <V_J, E_J, m> ... Temporal Validity Window tau = <t_start, t_end, v_D, TTL> ... Modal and Boundary Metadata mu = <Type, Modality, ScopeMask>
a_rows_sample.statement: Formal definition of the ABK-1 state 4-tuple State(phi)=<nu,J,tau,mu>: nu is the FDE truth valuation in the powerset of {T,F}; J=<V_J,E_J,m> is a justification DAG (premise nodes, derivation edges, justification mode in {Evidenced,Inferred,Reported,Assumed}); tau=<t_start,t_end,v_D,TTL> is a temporal validity window with a dependency version vector; mu=<Type,Modality,ScopeMask> carries Analytic/Synthetic, Necessary/Contingent, and a scope bitmask.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Order (<=_k): S1 <=_k S2 iff (nu1 subseteq nu2) and (J1 sqsubseteq_DAG J2) ... Truth Order (<=_t): S1 <=_t S2 iff (T in nu1 implies T in nu2) and (F in nu2 implies F in nu1) ... Conjunction (x_t) ... Disjunction (+_t) ... combining FDE valuation, justification-DAG union, temporal intersection, and metadata AND (mu1 (dot) mu2).
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines ABK-1's algebraic lattice structure over B_ABK = BF_4 x J x T x M: a Knowledge Order (<=_k, comparing valuation-subset and DAG-substructure) and a Truth Order (<=_t, standard FDE truth ordering), plus lattice conjunction and disjunction operators that combine FDE valuations via standard FDE meet/join, union justification DAGs, intersect temporal validity windows, and combine modal metadata via a metadata-AND operator.

type_signature.codomain: boolean order relations, or a combined ABK-1 state

a_rows_sample.anchor: export class ABKState { public val: FDEValue; public justification: JustificationGraph; public temporal: TemporalWindow; public metadata: ModalMetadata; ... resolveKnowledgeStatus(currentTime, upstreamVersions): KnowledgeStatus { if (this.resolveCurrency(...) === 'Expired') return 'NotAssessed'; switch(this.val) { case 'B': return 'Contradictory'; ... case 'N': { if (this.justification.nodes.length > 0) return 'Underdetermined'; return 'Unknown'; } } }
a_rows_sample.statement: Provides a full TypeScript reference implementation of ABK-1: an ABKState class carrying val/justification/temporal/metadata fields with resolveKnowledgeStatus (currency-checks first, then value-switches, distinguishing Underdetermined from Unknown by non-empty justification nodes), resolveCurrency (Expired if past tEnd, Stale if any dependency version has advanced, else Current), and resolveJustificationMode methods; and an ABKAlgebra class with a hard-coded FDE conjunction truth table and a meet() operation merging justification DAGs (node/edge union), temporal windows (intersection), and metadata (conjunctive AND, scope-mask bitwise AND).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Architectural Specification: ABK-1 / Contr Bridge Interface (ABK-CONTR-INT-v1) ... The Contr Isolation Module operates directly on top of the Annotated Bilattice Kernel (ABK-1) to handle non-explosion, contradiction trap frames, and resolution state tracking for paraconsistent evaluations. ... When an inbound assertion or lattice operation produces a contradictory valuation (nu(phi)=B), the ABK-1 engine delegates contradiction containment to ABKContrBridge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a bridge architecture (SPEC-ABK-CONTR-2026-V1) between ABK-1 and a Contr contradiction-isolation engine: whenever an ABK-1 lattice operation produces a contradictory valuation (nu=B), the engine delegates containment to an ABKContrBridge that traps the state in a local frame, sets ResolutionStatus=Unresolved, and initializes an evidential polarity edge graph, ensuring downstream inference cannot propagate the contradiction beyond a bounded contextual scope.

a_rows_sample.anchor: export interface IABKContrBridge { shouldIsolate(state): boolean; isolateContradiction(...): ContrIsolationPayload; updateResolutionStatus(...): ContradictionTrapFrame; evaluateResolution(frameId): ABKState; } ... evaluateResolution ... if (totalWeight > 0.5) { resolvedVal='T'; resolution='Resolved'; } else if (totalWeight < -0.5) { resolvedVal='F'; resolution='Resolved'; } else { resolvedVal='B'; resolution='Irresolvable'; }
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the IABKContrBridge TypeScript interface (shouldIsolate, isolateContradiction, updateResolutionStatus, evaluateResolution) and its ABKContrBridge implementation: contradiction resolution sums signed evidential-polarity weights across conflicting sources and resolves to True (Resolved) if the sum exceeds +0.5, False (Resolved) if below -0.5, or remains contradictory (Irresolvable) if the weights are near-balanced -- a simple threshold-based weighted-voting resolution rule for the contradiction lifecycle.

type_signature.domain: a contradiction trap frame with polarity-weighted evidence edges
type_signature.codomain: a resolved (or still-contradictory) ABKState plus a ResolutionStatus

a_rows_sample.anchor: describe('ABK-1 / Contr Bridge Integration Suite' ... it('should detect contradictory valuations (B) and trigger isolation' ... it('should mark frame as Irresolvable when evidence weights cancel out' ...
a_rows_sample.statement: Provides a runnable Jest end-to-end integration test suite (abk-contr-integration.test.ts) covering contradiction detection and trap-frame creation, non-explosion verification (an isolated contradictory proposition does not pollute an unrelated proposition's algebra), and resolution-lifecycle management (transition through InProgress/Resolved, resolving to True when positive evidence dominates, and remaining Irresolvable when weights cancel).

a_rows_sample.anchor: There is one additional missing bridge ... Adequacy -> Executability ... we need one more formal relation: ExecutableAdequacy. b_rows_sample.anchor: Test Vector 1: Knowledge Status (D-1.1) ... queryStatus(P_3) | N = empty | Underdetermined | FAIL (Collapsed) ... Root Cause: Standard 4-valued FDE maps both unassessed propositions (P_2) and rule evaluations with missing antecedents (P_3) to the same logical value N (empty). FDE fails to separate Unknown from Underdetermined without an explicit operational/metadata wrapper.
b_rows_sample.statement: Test Vector 1 (Knowledge Status): a standard 4-valued FDE kernel correctly separates Contradictory (B={T,F}) and passes non-explosion, but maps both an unassessed proposition (P_2) and a rule evaluation with a missing antecedent binding (P_3) to the same value N=empty -- collapsing Unknown and Underdetermined into one value. Overall PARTIAL FAIL: FDE cannot separate these two without an explicit operational/metadata wrapper.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Test Vector 2: Justification Mode (D-1.2) ... Root Cause: Truth valuations alone in FDE contain no structural lineage. v(B)={T} in both states. A pure FDE kernel collapses Inferred and Assumed unless extended into a Justification-Annotated Bilattice or Labeled Deductive System.
b_rows_sample.statement: Test Vector 2 (Justification Mode): bare FDE truth valuations carry no structural lineage -- an Inferred proposition (derived A->B) and an Assumed proposition (axiomatic default) both evaluate to v(B)={T}, so bare FDE collapses Inferred and Assumed (FAIL). Only an FDE state annotated with a derivation tree/justification graph passes (state hashes differ). Overall FAIL for pure FDE logic.

type_signature.codomain: FDE value {T} plus optional justification annotation

b_rows_sample.anchor: Test Vector 3: Currency & Validity State (D-2.1) ... Root Cause: Temporal mechanics are orthogonal to static FDE truth values. Standard FDE does not natively track state staleness or temporal validity without an integrated frame time projection.
b_rows_sample.statement: Test Vector 3 (Currency): a Stale proposition (dependency Y updated after X was computed) and an Expired proposition (TTL exceeded) both evaluate as {T} under pure FDE, collapsing to Current in both cases (FAIL). Temporal mechanics are orthogonal to static FDE truth values; FDE does not natively track staleness or expiry without an integrated frame-time projection.

type_signature.domain: proposition with temporal metadata (last_computed/last_updated or valid_until/current_time)
type_signature.codomain: FDE value {T} vs target currency state

b_rows_sample.anchor: Test Vector 4: Absence of Evidence vs. Evidence of Absence (D-3.2) ... Result: PASS ... Root Cause: FDE naturally distinguishes non-observation (N=empty) from explicit negative observation (F={F}). This is one of FDE's primary structural strengths over classical logic.
b_rows_sample.statement: Test Vector 4 (Absence of Evidence vs Evidence of Absence): pure FDE correctly maps a no-observations state to N=empty (Unknown) and an explicit negative-sensor-result state to F={F} (KnownFalse), with distinct state hashes -- full PASS. Recorded as one of FDE's primary structural strengths over classical logic.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Overall Suite Result: FAIL (Unaugmented FDE) ... Pure 4-valued First-Degree Entailment (FDE) is necessary but insufficient as a standalone KnowledgeOS kernel ... Required Architectural Enhancement: To qualify as an R_req-compliant kernel, FDE must be wrapped in a Annotated/Graded Labeled Frame Space that pairs FDE truth values with explicit justification graphs and temporal validity intervals.
b_rows_sample.statement: Overall compliance verdict across the four Tier-P1 test vectors: unaugmented FDE FAILs the R_req P1 suite (PARTIAL/FAIL/FAIL/PASS). Pure 4-valued FDE is judged necessary but insufficient as a standalone KnowledgeOS kernel: it perfectly handles Contradictory and Absence-of-Evidence-vs-Evidence-of-Absence, but collapses Underdetermined into Unknown, carries no justification lineage, and lacks temporal validity tracking. Proposes wrapping FDE in an Annotated/Graded Labeled Frame Space combining FDE truth values with justification graphs and temporal validity intervals to become R_req-compliant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Loss_req(pi,Q,Gamma) = R_req(Q,Gamma) intersect Collapsed(pi). Then: Loss_req = empty is a very strong adequacy condition. This is far more useful than a generic 'information loss' metric. ... FDE preserves some distinctions but collapses others. The relevant question is not 'Does FDE have four values?' It is: Does FDE preserve every distinction in R_req(Q,Gamma)? Our previous experiments already showed that it does not.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Loss_req(pi,Q,Gamma) = R_req(Q,Gamma) intersect Collapsed(pi) as a required-information-loss metric, with Loss_req=empty as a strong adequacy condition, judged more useful than a generic information-loss measure; reframes the earlier FDE-insufficiency finding not as 'does FDE have four values' but as 'does FDE preserve every distinction in R_req(Q,Gamma)', concluding it does not (per prior experiments) -- positioning R_req as the formal language for STATING why a representation is inadequate rather than a prescription of which representation must be used.

The transition itself is held valid (the human act genuinely authorized the appointment, which AST-018 treats as the activation authority) but the prose is self-contradictory; per append-only discipline this is not rewritten, only corrected via this new record.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AST-018 appoint collapses appointment and activation
a_rows_sample.statement: Finding O-6: one human act produces REGISTER+HANDOFF+START with no appoint-without-activate path through AST-018 appoint, and the same --human-act string serves as both the appointment authority and the START authority; judged not a defect but documented business intent (the tool's purpose is to remove UUID/REGISTER/HANDOFF/START mechanics from the human), yet worth recording because a person authorizing an appointment thereby also authorizes the start, and the estate's own vocabulary/prompts had treated these as two separate gates -- 'the vocabulary and the mechanisms disagree.' Contrast: AST-019 activate also fuses REGISTER->HANDOFF->START. Status: RECORDED - NOT PROMOTED - NOT DECIDED (ES-006.1, first clean occurrence, methodology frozen), explicitly not a proposal to change AST-018 and not in REPAIR-001's scope.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The FAIL verdict is ACCEPTED
a_rows_sample.statement: PO/ARB accepts an independent verification's FAIL verdict on AST-019 as authoritative and final (not reopened, re-run, or rewritten); F-1 (a reachable correctness defect on the production write path) is confirmed independently at source: analyze() at lines 377-385 returns no fold key, so writeActivation() at lines 401-402 forces $owner to null, mis-deriving both REGISTER.predecessor and HANDOFF.from.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTINUATION recorded (seq 5)
a_rows_sample.statement: A CONTINUATION transition (requiring a registered session) reactivates the original verifier's lane solely as a handoff predecessor so the repair lane can receive its HANDOFF -- identical in shape to the parent item's seq-10 precedent where a STOPped verification lane was reactivated only to hand off to its successor; explicitly reopens the work item, not the verification/verdict/report, and the verifier performs no further work.

a_rows_sample.anchor: That advice is misleading in this state
a_rows_sample.statement: Observation O-4 (reporting imprecision, not a defect claim): after the CONTINUATION, AST-018 next-actor reports 'LANE ACTIVE ... no new actor is needed', which is misleading in this state since the lane is ACTIVE only as a mechanical consequence of the continuation, not because the verifier has further work; the fold itself is correct, only the advisory interpretation is wrong; verified harmless to the plan since appointReviewer() has no active-lane refusal (unlike AST-019's GO-13 gate). Status: RECORDED, NOT PROMOTED (ES-006.1, single occurrence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: REPAIR-001 AUTHORIZED (grant G-REPAIR-001)
a_rows_sample.statement: Grant G-REPAIR-001 authorizes a narrowly scoped repair covering four findings and one test gap on a single file plus its contract test: F-1 (blocking: analyze() omits fold, forcing null mutationOwner and mis-deriving predecessor/from), F-3 (failure path returns the refusal() shape lacking the ok key the caller tests), F-4 (transitionWritten hard-coded true when nothing was written), F-2 (PHP warnings on STDOUT break the --json contract, closing only when BOTH F-1 and F-3 are fixed -- not a corollary of F-1 alone), and O-1 (a RED-first contract test with a live non-null mutationOwner asserting REGISTER.predecessor and HANDOFF.from both equal owner, failing on today's code before any fix). Touchable scope: activate-commissioned-fresh-session.php and its contract test only.

a_rows_sample.anchor: F-5 is HELD OUTSIDE this repair
a_rows_sample.statement: F-5 (whether KOS_MECHANISM_PATH may redirect the 'sole writer', and why AST-017/AST-018 use hard constants while AST-019 does not) is explicitly held outside REPAIR-001 pending a separate Architecture decision -- must not be fixed, mitigated, or documented away inside the repair, since a correctness slice silently settling an architecture question is a category slippage the estate forbids; ASD-001 is preserved as a recorded sequencing defect (not reopened/remedied/erased), found to be the same defect class as F-1 from opposite directions (O-3); verification history (seq 1-4) stays untouched; the adopted parent layers L1+L2+L3's byte-integrity is stated as an acceptance criterion of REPAIR-001, not an assumption.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Independence requirements differ by role -- kept separate deliberately
a_rows_sample.statement: Independence bars differ by role and are kept separate deliberately: the REPAIR-001 implementer is barred only from being the verifier (must not repair what it verified, R-34/EP-02) or the governance process that scoped the slice, while the original AST-019 producer is explicitly NOT categorically barred from implementing (repairing one's own code is ordinary engineering); re-verification afterwards bars the first verifier, the producer, the scoping governance process, AND whoever implements REPAIR-001, since independence from the work under check is what makes the check worth anything -- collapsing verification-role bars onto implementation-role bars would shrink the eligible pool for no governed reason.

a_rows_sample.anchor: declaration-only prompt. This is NOT the repair commission.
a_rows_sample.statement: A two-phase actor-onboarding pattern is used: Phase 1 is a declaration-only prompt in which a candidate determines its own process identity from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and discloses independence before reading any subject material; Phase 2 (the actual repair commission) issues only after appointment, human START, and an approved EP-01 plan -- explicitly designed so a declaration arriving with a plan attached is judged to have already broken the boundary the prompt exists to protect.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the actual test is PARTICIPATION, not identity
a_rows_sample.statement: A different runtime session UUID is necessary but not sufficient evidence of independence, since a restarted process can report a new CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID while retaining the same working context (observation O-5); the actual eligibility test is participation ('have I authored, scoped, reviewed, verified, analysed, or advised on this work item or subject in this conversation or any context I carry'), to be disclosed in full even if it makes the candidate ineligible, with the identifier list treated only as a non-exhaustive aid.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Two statements, both true
a_rows_sample.statement: The original AST-019 producer is kept distinct on two levels: the general rule is that it is NOT categorically barred from implementing its own repair (ordinary engineering, no rule bars it), while the PO/ARB has separately excluded it for this specific slice as 'not the cleanest separation for this defect'; a candidate matching that identity must report NOT ELIGIBLE citing the PO/ARB decision, not a rule, and is also barred from the later re-verification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 84c0f6f6 was handed the full commission at first start and, following it in order, read ~120 lines of the subject before declaring
a_rows_sample.statement: The declaration-only prompt design (step 0 'declare before you orient' placed first) is a direct correction of an earlier failure mode: a prior candidate (84c0f6f6), handed the full commission at first start, read approximately 120 lines of the subject before declaring, traced to prompt selection (structuring) rather than process error; the AMENDMENT-001 changelog also records bars becoming participation-first (UUIDs demoted to a non-exhaustive aid), a new barred id (e40f3fd0) added after the scoping process itself restarted under a new runtime id, and the return format extended with REQUESTED ROLE/REPAIR GRANT/NON-ACTIONS/explicit STOP fields.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the implementation STOP is unrecorded
a_rows_sample.statement: Governance determination that the actual next governed act precedes any re-verifier: the repair (commit d8a5ee93, +22/-5 plus a 293-line contract test) exists in git but the authoritative workflow record never recorded the implementation lane's STOP (lane 84e5c1f7 still ACTIVE); consequence if skipped: appoint would still mechanically work but the implementer's IMPLEMENTED report and evidence would never enter the record, existing only as a git commit -- exactly the fact/record separation the estate protects. Canonical chain: implementation STOP (reports IMPLEMENTED, never VERIFIED) -> item becomes STOPPED -> human CONTINUATION -> AST-018 appoint the re-verifier.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Is independent re-verification binding? YES
a_rows_sample.statement: Determination that independent re-verification of the repaired code is binding, grounded primarily in a quoted PO/ARB authorization clause ('keep AST-019/AMENDMENT-001 not adopted and not authorized pending independent verification') that has never been lifted; reasoning that a verification of superseded (pre-repair) code cannot be the verification of the code that replaced it, so a prior FAIL verdict does not discharge the condition -- the repair is what makes the condition answerable. Substantive reason: defect F-1 was invisible to the entire prior 25-test contract suite, and the new tests certifying the fix (GO-26..GO-30) were written by the same process that wrote the fix, so the only present evidence of a cure comes from the party being certified -- explicitly NOT generalized into a rule that every implementation requires fresh verification, resting on this one named condition attached to this one named asset plus a blocking FAIL whose defect the existing suite could not see.

a_rows_sample.anchor: fresh runtime UUID ≠ absence of prior participation
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates and applies the accumulated independence-detection findings (a subagent reports its parent's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, so collision with a barred identity disqualifies; CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1 is non-discriminating per O-5, disclosed but neither disqualifying nor certifying; prior participation established from primary evidence searches, not UUID novelty) to bar four named identities (the REPAIR-001 implementer, the first verifier, the AST-019 producer, and the scoping governance process) from re-verification, each for a stated reason rather than by reflex.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A previous candidate was handed the full commission at first start ... and read ~120 lines of the subject before declaring
a_rows_sample.statement: A second declaration-only Phase-1 prompt (for the re-verifier role) reapplies the 'declare before you orient' pattern established for the implementer (S0413), explicitly citing the same prior ordering-deviation incident as its rationale; requires the candidate to search for its own id via git grep/log and directory scans before reading any authoritative state, and to report identity/independence/prior-participation/eligibility/work-item-state/authorization in a fixed six-field format before stopping.

a_rows_sample.anchor: recordedBy: governance, deliberately not implementation
a_rows_sample.statement: Governance closes the implementation lane's STOP itself, but by TRANSCRIBING the lane's own already-existing completion report (commit d8a5ee93, its message, the EP-01 plan, developer guide, session log) rather than speaking in the lane's voice, per INV-ATTR-1/2; explicitly asserts only that the completion report exists and is cited, not that the repair is correct (auditing correctness would be Governance performing the verification it is commissioning); status recorded as IMPLEMENTED -- explicitly NOT VERIFIED, NOT ADOPTED, NOT AUTHORIZED.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Single admission gate MUST EXIST; Contract-conformance enforcement MUST EXIST; Identity assignment MUST EXIST; Evidence admission MUST EXIST; Justification preservation + sufficiency evaluation MUST EXIST; History recording MUST EXIST; Representation-agnostic intake MUST EXIST; Epistemic-state determination MUST EXIST; Confidence assignment inside boundary MUST EXIST
b_rows_sample.statement: Prior F-1..F-5 work is reported to have confirmed capabilities already present in existing law (not invented new ones), yielding a concrete 9-row MUST-EXIST domain capability map used to argue the Kernel-as-pure-admissibility-function formulation is too small — the domain already has authoritative responsibilities around identity assignment, evidence admission, justification preservation/sufficiency, epistemic-state determination, confidence, and history.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Kernel is probably not 'the constitutional validator' ... The Kernel is the authoritative admission boundary of KnowledgeCore. Its constitutional admissibility responsibility exists inside that boundary, but it is not the whole definition.
b_rows_sample.statement: The Kernel's identity is reframed a third time in this batch: not a god-Kernel, not merely DeepSeek's constitutional-validator/pure-function, but 'the authoritative admission boundary of KnowledgeCore,' inside which constitutional admissibility is one responsibility among identity assignment, epistemic state, evidence/justification/confidence, and history.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The KnowledgeCore accepts any representable submission. Natural language is therefore just one possible surface representation. The candidate shape is invariant; the surface representation isn't.
b_rows_sample.statement: F-3's result that KnowledgeCore accepts any representable submission gives the Sanskrit/FST/compiler research a clean architectural home outside the Kernel: natural language, structured data, and formal notation all reduce to the same canonical candidate shape before admission, validating the earlier candidate-set insight (AH-6) while explicitly removing it from the Kernel.

b_rows_sample.anchor: F-4 explicitly prohibits the tempting architecture: candidate → candidate database → Kernel later. Non-admitted candidates are not KnowledgeOS domain state. ... There is no hidden semantic aggregate.
b_rows_sample.statement: F-4 forbids a candidate-persistence architecture ('store candidates now, decide admissibility later'): a non-admitted candidate is never KnowledgeOS domain state — it is either recorded in History as part of an already-admitted transition, or lives entirely mechanism/infrastructure-side — a strong anti-god-Kernel constraint against a hidden semantic aggregate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: research_required: NO; research_track_opened: NO; kernel_designed: NO; kernel_implemented: NO; domain_model_changed: NO; aggregate_changed: NO; invariants_changed: NO ... So I would not ask DeepSeek for more research now.
b_rows_sample.statement: F-1..F-5's own concluding YAML block records that it opened no new research track, designed and implemented no Kernel, and changed no domain model/aggregate/invariants, explicitly returning control to the HPA; the reviewing voice concludes no further research round is warranted and proposes instead a single, code-free, thirteen-part DDD consolidation question as the final step before deciding what the Kernel actually is.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Single admission gate MUST EXIST; Contract-conformance enforcement MUST EXIST; Identity assignment MUST EXIST; Evidence admission MUST EXIST; Justification preservation + sufficiency evaluation MUST EXIST; History recording MUST EXIST; Representation-agnostic intake MUST EXIST; Epistemic-state determination MUST EXIST; Confidence assignment inside boundary MUST EXIST
b_rows_sample.statement: Verbatim restatement (in a separately-timestamped file) of the 9-row F-1..F-5 MUST-EXIST domain capability map and the conclusion that DeepSeek's Kernel-as-pure-function formulation is too small; content is identical to the corresponding section of S0361 and adds no new claim beyond it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: F-4 explicitly prohibits the tempting architecture: candidate → candidate database → Kernel later. Non-admitted candidates are not KnowledgeOS domain state.
b_rows_sample.statement: Duplicate restatement of F-4's anti-candidate-persistence constraint (no hidden semantic aggregate; non-admitted candidates are never domain state), identical in substance to the corresponding S0361 contribution.

b_rows_sample.anchor: they did not invent new domain capabilities. They confirmed capabilities already present in the existing law and made their boundaries explicit.
b_rows_sample.statement: Nine domain capabilities claimed as existing-law, all MUST EXIST: single admission gate, contract-conformance enforcement, identity assignment, evidence admission, justification preservation + sufficiency evaluation, history recording, representation-agnostic intake, epistemic-state determination, confidence assignment inside boundary. Used to argue a minimal rule-evaluator Kernel ('(command, state, rules, evidence) -> admissibility verdict') is too small, since the domain already holds authoritative responsibility for these nine. A specific ownership split is quoted: the domain owns the admitted JustificationPath and its sufficiency evaluation, while the reasoning mechanism owns only production.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Not one item F008 wants to keep appears on F007's exclusion list.
b_rows_sample.statement: Running the contradiction test on S1-F007's exclusion set (NL interpretation, rule engine, evidence weighting, self-audit) against S1-F008's inclusion set (admission gate, contract conformance, identity assignment, evidence admission, justification preservation, representation-agnostic intake, epistemic-state determination, confidence assignment, history recording) finds zero overlap -- F007 removes mechanisms, F008 retains domain responsibilities, one principle (mechanisms out, domain responsibilities in) applied to two disjoint sets, not opposed magnitudes on one axis. The residual genuine tension is narrower: F007's Adjudication!=Execution distinction versus F008's map containing both adjudication (the gate) and execution (assigning identity, recording history).

b_rows_sample.anchor: The map — no... The warning — yes, and it is the artifact's real deliverable.
b_rows_sample.statement: Implementation-relevance verdict: the nine-capability map itself yields no implementation work (every item is claimed to already exist as law; six of nine are found present in v1.1's own coverage comparison), but the anti-minimalist warning that 'the Kernel cannot simply be a generic rule evaluator' is preserved as a standing review question at boundary decisions -- a failure mode invisible to conformance testing (each rule can pass while identity assignment migrates into a mechanism) and visible only to the question 'does anything the domain must own now happen somewhere else?'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Must own (7): identity assignment · constitutional evaluation · epistemic state determination · evidence reference preservation · justification preservation · history recording · contradiction detection. Must not own (8): semantic interpretation · evidence content · reasoning · workflow · projection · rule definition · Confidence (if derivable) · Supersession/contestation (if separate lifecycle).
b_rows_sample.statement: Records a member-list model: 'The Kernel is the Admission Boundary of the KnowledgeAggregate,' with 7 must-own responsibilities (identity assignment, constitutional evaluation, epistemic state determination, evidence reference preservation, justification preservation, history recording, contradiction detection) and 8 must-not-own responsibilities (semantic interpretation, evidence content, reasoning, workflow, projection, rule definition, Confidence-if-derivable, Supersession/contestation-if-separate-lifecycle); two exclusions are explicitly conditional on open questions (Confidence's derivability, and the lifecycle-ownership question), making this the first list to state its own dependencies. Contradiction detection appears as a must-own item for the first time across five lists; projection is excluded for the fourth time without argument; evidence-reference (not content) is retained, consistent with S1-F014's reference/content split and S1-F018's Entity/VO question. Maximum bound stated: 'The Kernel must not own any responsibility that is not essential to protecting the aggregate invariant.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Extent = which aggregates, and which gate. That is the K-1 structure: KnowledgeAggregate + ConflictRecord, Verification Port as sole inbound gate. ... Contents = which members, states, events, and port obligations sit inside that extent.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the extent-vs-contents distinction: Extent = which aggregates and which gate (the K-1 structure: KnowledgeAggregate + ConflictRecord, Verification Port as sole inbound gate — reported as formal-track state, not a research candidate); Contents = which members, states, events, and port obligations sit inside that extent; identified as the most clarifying single distinction extracted from the corpus so far, arriving from the formal governance track rather than the research corpus's own reasoning.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The same evidence should not automatically serve as both construction evidence and independent validation evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Records a constraint new to the corpus: the same evidence item must not automatically serve as both construction evidence and independent validation evidence — the evidential analogue of the producer≠verifier separation (S1-F002), now stated about evidence roles rather than actors; bears on unruled item on evidence-reference resolvability (an evidence reference may need to carry its role, not just its identity); adds a new cost to S1-F018's shareable-Entity horn, since a shareable Entity could otherwise be reused across construction and validation, which this constraint forbids.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The acquisition procedure itself determines whether an observation can function as evidence. ... two identical observations can differ in evidential standing.
b_rows_sample.statement: Records the strongest claim in the corpus about evidence: the acquisition procedure itself constitutes whether an observation can function as evidence, so two identical observations can differ in evidential standing depending on how they were obtained; this makes acquisition provenance a precondition of admissibility rather than a desirable attribute, a different and finer requirement than source-type retention or a justification-path obligation; intersects S1-F029's role constraint (role and acquisition together determine what an evidence reference must carry) and adds a further cost to S1-F018's shareable-Entity horn (one acquisition history may qualify an Entity for one use and not another).

b_rows_sample.anchor: A justified claim. More precisely: a proposition that is asserted, supported by evidence, and constitutionally evaluated. ... If a claim is part of KnowledgeOS, it must be justifiable—there must exist evidence, a reasoning chain, and a constitutional determination that it belongs in the system.
b_rows_sample.statement: Concludes the smallest domain fact whose integrity must be protected is 'a justified claim' (asserted, evidence-supported, constitutionally evaluated), with justifiability as the sole retained invariant; explicitly excludes Identity ('an administrative concern'), Epistemic State ('a projection of events'), Confidence ('an assessment'), and History ('an audit record') from the required invariant — the most reductive result in the corpus, demoting four of the six components every other member list treats as core, including Identity, which a separate ledger treats as the core domain and S1-F015 said never changes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Identity + Evidence References | Strong: identity is the anchor | WEAK — Evidence can exist without identity; identity can exist without evidence (if contested) | Does NOT require co-location.
b_rows_sample.statement: Records five pairwise atomicity-test verdicts, all negative: Identity+Evidence References (relatedness Strong, atomicity WEAK, does not require co-location); Identity+Justification (Strong/WEAK, does not require co-location — justification can be assessed by a separate context); Identity+Epistemic State (Moderate/WEAK — state can be a projection); Identity+Confidence (WEAK, assessed separately); Identity+History (WEAK, history stored separately) — the corpus's leading hypothesis (aggregate as smallest consistency boundary, stated 9 minutes earlier) does not survive its own test.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'F-1..F-5'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Customer_Sales and Customer_Billing refer to the same real-world organization. It does not follow that Customer_Sales=Customer_Billing ... How can knowledge cross a bounded-context boundary without corrupting meaning?
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses the bounded-context-translation problem, distinguishing it from entity-identity questions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: x_C. Its meaning is Meaning(x|C). Meaning(x|C_1) != Meaning(x|C_2) is perfectly legitimate
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes context-relative concept meaning.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ref(x_C1)=r and Ref(x_C2)=r. SameRealWorldReferent does not imply SameDomainConcept. This is one of the most important principles in the entire architecture
a_rows_sample.statement: States one of the architecture's most important principles: shared real-world referent does not imply shared domain concept.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Customer_Sales: customerNumber, salesStatus, salesRegion, accountManager. Customer_Billing: debtorNumber, creditLimit, paymentStatus, invoiceAddress. The two models overlap. But they do not have the same semantics
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked Customer_Sales vs Customer_Billing example of overlapping but non-identical bounded-context models.

a_rows_sample.anchor: T_{A->B}: K_A -> K_B where K_A and K_B are knowledge structures within bounded contexts
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines the translation function between bounded-context knowledge structures.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Customer_Sales -> Customer_Billing may discard salesRegion. T_{B->A}(T_{A->B}(x)) != x. Translation != bijection
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked counterexample showing translation is generally non-invertible/non-bijective.

a_rows_sample.anchor: TranslationType in {Lossless, Lossy, Approximate, Partial, Invalid}. This classification should be explicit
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a five-way translation-type taxonomy that must be made explicit.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If T(x) preserves all relevant semantics under the target context: Meaning(T(x)|B)=Meaning(x|A) for the relevant semantic dimensions. Then translation is effectively lossless for that purpose
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines purpose-relative lossless translation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A={a1,a2,a3,a4} but target context only supports {b1,b2}. Then T(A) must discard information. That is acceptable if explicitly represented
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example of acceptable lossy translation conditional on explicit representation of the loss.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If T drops information, KnowledgeOS should preserve Loss(T). Otherwise a downstream consumer may incorrectly believe the translated object contains the complete original semantics
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires explicit tracking of translation loss to prevent downstream misinterpretation of completeness.

a_rows_sample.anchor: M_{A,B} as a mapping between concepts. OrderStatus_A -> BillingStatus_B. But the mapping must describe the relationship: Equivalent, Broader, Narrower, Overlapping, Derived, Approximate
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines semantic mapping between concepts requiring a typed relationship description.

a_rows_sample.anchor: OrderStatus_A: Created, Confirmed, Shipped, Delivered, Cancelled. BillingStatus_B: Open, Paid, Overdue, Cancelled. There is no simple equality. Shipped might imply Open but not Shipped=Open
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked order-status/billing-status example showing implication without equivalence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R_semantic in {SameMeaning, EquivalentUnderContext, Implies, CompatibleWith, MapsTo, Refines, Abstracts, ConflictsWith}
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines an eight-value typed semantic-mapping relation taxonomy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A=>B, that does not mean A<=>B. This sounds elementary, but AI systems frequently collapse these distinctions. KnowledgeOS must not
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns against collapsing implication into equivalence, a distinction AI systems frequently violate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Concept_B is more detailed than Concept_A. Then B may refine A. Approved may be refined into ApprovedByManager and ApprovedByBoard
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines semantic refinement, worked with an Approved-refinement example.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A may abstract several concepts B_1,B_2,B_3. OperationalFailure may abstract network failure; storage failure; process failure
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines semantic abstraction as the converse of refinement, worked with an OperationalFailure example.

a_rows_sample.anchor: B preceq A meaning B is more specific than A. This can form a semantic lattice or partial order. But we must not assume every domain naturally forms a complete lattice
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a cautious semantic partial-order/lattice structure, explicitly not assumed universal.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A partial order requires reflexivity, antisymmetry, transitivity. Some domain relations satisfy these properties. Others do not. KnowledgeOS should represent the actual relation rather than force mathematical structure where none exists
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns against forcing partial-order structure onto relations that do not actually satisfy its axioms.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Contract(T). SourceContext, TargetContext, SourceConcept, TargetConcept, MappingRule, LossCharacteristics, Assumptions, ValidityPeriod
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a translation-contract schema with eight required fields.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SalesEvidence -> SalesClaim -> Translation -> BillingClaim. Otherwise the target claim looks as though it originated directly from Billing
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires translation provenance preserving the full source-to-target lineage.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If identity is wrong, then almost everything we built before can become wrong ... reasoning about the wrong object ... When are two references actually referring to the same real-world entity?
b_rows_sample.statement: Opens by arguing identity errors can corrupt the entire downstream chain (Evidence->Assertion->Knowledge->Model->Decision) since the system may reason about the wrong object, framing the fundamental identity question.

b_rows_sample.anchor: "nexus3.dgverlag.de", "10.61.133.85", "the Nexus server" ... Reference\neq Entity
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Reference ≠ Entity: multiple distinct strings/identifiers can all refer to one entity, but the strings themselves are not the entity — a reference merely claims to refer to an entity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SameEntity(r_1,r_2\mid C,E,M) ... Resolution(r_1,r_2)\in\{Same,Different,PossibleSame,Unknown\}
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes SameEntity(r1,r2|C,E,M) parameterized by context/evidence/identity-model, and defines a four-value Resolution outcome {Same,Different,PossibleSame,Unknown}, rejecting binary resolution as 'much safer.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: nexus3 appears in two documents ... one says production, another says development ... Identity=Unknown. This should block automatic merging
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example showing an ambiguous shared name across two documents legitimately yields Identity=Unknown, which must block automatic merging.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SameAs(x,x)=True ... SameAs(x,y)\Rightarrow SameAs(y,x) ... transitivity ... SameAs should behave like an equivalence relation
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines SameAs(x,y) as ideally reflexive, symmetric, and transitive — 'SameAs should behave like an equivalence relation' if it truly denotes strict entity identity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence(A,B) and Evidence(B,C) ... not sufficient to establish A=C ... SameAs from EvidenceForSameAs ... another example of Assertion\neq Evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: Notes evidence for pairwise SameAs relations is not automatically transitive (Evidence(A,B) and Evidence(B,C) don't establish A=C), requiring SameAs to be distinguished from EvidenceForSameAs — 'another example of Assertion ≠ Evidence.'

b_rows_sample.anchor:
DevelopmentServer
eq ProductionServer ... KnownDifferent from NotKnownSame ... 
eg SameAs(x,y)
eq DistinctFrom(x,y) unless the domain explicitly uses a closed-world identity rule
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines DistinctFrom(x,y) as distinct from simple ¬SameAs(x,y): KnownDifferent ≠ NotKnownSame unless the domain explicitly adopts a closed-world identity rule.

b_rows_sample.anchor: IdentityRelation(x,y)\in\{Same,Distinct,Uncertain\} ... I prefer retaining the richer evidence state Same/Distinct/PossibleSame/Unknown ... preserves epistemic uncertainty
b_rows_sample.statement: Prefers a richer four-value internal identity-evidence state (Same/Distinct/PossibleSame/Unknown) over a coarser three-value simplification, to preserve epistemic uncertainty.

b_rows_sample.anchor: globally unique identifier; database primary key; certificate identity; authoritative registry; ... temporal continuity; cryptographic identity ... should have different evidential strength
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists nine types of identity evidence (UUID, primary key, certificate, registry, system relationship, network identity, human confirmation, temporal continuity, cryptographic identity), each with differing evidential strength.

b_rows_sample.anchor: UUID_A=UUID_B ... SameAs(A,B) can be strongly established ... fundamentally different from Name_A=Name_B
b_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts strong identity evidence (a guaranteed-globally-unique UUID match, strongly establishing SameAs) with weak name-based matching.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Name=nexus3 for both records ... P(Same|NameMatch) may be high or low depending on the domain ... IdentityEvidence is context-dependent
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: a bare name match's evidential strength for identity depends heavily on namespace context (strong in a small controlled namespace, nearly useless globally) — 'IdentityEvidence is context-dependent.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: IdentityKey=(Organization,Environment,Hostname,SystemID) ... EntityIdentity=ContextualTuple rather than simply a display name
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines composite EntityIdentity as a contextual tuple (Organization,Environment,Hostname,SystemID), showing shared hostname with differing environment yields different entities — EntityIdentity = ContextualTuple, not a display name.

b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects and sharpens D-0's earlier finding: the models ARE separable in isolation, but one unrelated U anywhere in the epistemic state masks the difference completely in any bucket, because Zero_weak/Zero_kleene are existential quantifiers that absorb at U; with 5 of 8 Sat_c classes non-executable, this masking saturation is the normal regime, not an edge case -- the sixth instance of the recurring projection-vs-structure diagnosis, and the first found in the readings rather than a value or metric.

Validates the Zero Lens claim UNKNOWN≠ABSENT with a concrete formal witness: if Contr(p) and NoAssessment(p) both map to U, the representation has collapsed two semantically distinct situations, and this Representation_Collapse(Contr,Unknown) is now measurable.

Gives the precise masking-mechanism table: models are separable (2 distinct reading profiles) when zero other requirements are at U, but become inseparable (1 profile) as soon as even one other requirement is at U, regardless of its bucket -- caused by Zero_weak/Zero_kleene being existential quantifiers over the state (absorbing at the first U encountered), which Zero_reasoned inherits through Zero_weak; since 5 of 8 Sat classes are non-executable, saturation is the normal regime, not the edge case, meaning the contradiction-model choice is unobservable in exactly the regime KnowledgeOS actually occupies.

b_rows_sample.statement: Per-domain confidence after falsification (R16 Strong/Medium/Weak scale): D-1 Strong->STRONG; D-2 Strong->MEDIUM; D-3 Strong->WEAK; D-6a (Evidence Protocol) new->MEDIUM; D-6b (Product Evidence) new->STRONG; D-5 (Engineering Capability, not a context) Medium->MEDIUM (unchanged, H-CAT-1 stands); D-4 (Workflow, rejected) ->STRONG as a rejection; D-7 (PKS, a context type) new->WEAK. Distinction drawn: falsified is worse than unevidenced — D-3 and D-7 carry contradicting evidence (falsified); D-6a carries no evidence (unevidenced).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 2. CANDIDATE — supported by evidence, awaiting ruling or more evidence (K-1..K-15)
b_rows_sample.statement: Fifteen candidate concerns, each citing its supporting commission and what it waits on: K-1 dimensional-with-archetypes meta-model; K-2 the archetype set (strong: DOMAIN/PROCESS/CAPABILITY/KNOWLEDGE/ARTIFACT/RUNTIME ASSET/PROJECTION; weaker: CONTAINER; weakest: PURPOSE); K-3 the four partial orders (authority, production, realization, containment); K-4 11 invariant relationships vs 8 implementation choices; K-5 DP-n as capability anchor; K-6 Knowledge Space = declared boundary+owner+constitution; K-7 authority = provenance x standing, four progression kinds; K-8 the strategic domain set PD-1/2/3/5; K-9 viewpoints as presentation; K-10 decision-readiness as the platform's product; K-11 FREEZE/RETIRE as insufficiency evidence; K-12 PKS extends context-engineering with governance; K-13 the canon-track reference artifacts themselves; K-14 the mission is enacted via 8 artifacts; K-15 ownership splits (candidate-unowned=ladder working, operating-unowned=defect, sole instance Runtime Adapter).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 3. HYPOTHESIS — plausible, insufficient evidence (H-1..H-9)
b_rows_sample.statement: Nine hypotheses with evidence state: H-1 the space map is the platform's real ownership/context map (n=1, downgraded); H-2 GOVERNANCE as a fifth viewpoint (asset found, framing undecided); H-3 PURPOSE more fundamental than CONTAINER (n=0); H-4 KnowledgeOS as a 'Knowledge Architecture Platform' (n=1); H-5 'generates -> PKS', the loop's head edge and the platform's distinctive bet (n=0 inside and outside); H-6 capability may read across a space boundary, never own (n=1 capability); H-7 space nesting (unevidenced); H-8 DOMAIN's decision-silence is dormant not permanent (untestable at n=1); H-9 EVIDENCE-STATUS/OPERATIONAL-STATE as meta-model dimensions (proposed, undocketed).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 5. REJECTED — falsified, with the falsifying pass cited (R-1..R-12)
b_rows_sample.statement: Twelve rejected/falsified claims listed with falsifying pass: R-1 the flat A-G category list as a meta-model; R-2 Governance/Product as kinds, Knowledge Asset as one thing; R-3 Domains own Capabilities; R-4 the single-stack hierarchy (Purpose->...->Artifact); R-5 KnowledgeOS is the Core Domain/the real product; R-6 the MVK 15-file extraction boundary; R-7 'two missions'/'mission layer vacant'/the INTENDED evidence grade; R-8 '0 of 11 responsibilities enforcing'; R-9 '0 traversals' of the evidence back-edge as a generalization; R-10 I-4 as falsified, and LG-1; R-11 a second Engineering Decision Model; R-12 'one owner => one context' as stated.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The six concepts ... MISSION · ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE · ENGINEERING CAPABILITY · ENGINEERING ARTIFACT · PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE SPACE · PRODUCT
b_rows_sample.statement: Six concepts defined by responsibility/lifecycle/owner/dependencies, none defined by a folder: MISSION (why the platform exists; enacted->candidate->ratified, currently enacted-unratified; owner: sponsor; depends on nothing, the root); ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE (rules/methods/decisions that transfer between products; ES-006.1 ladder; owner DA for policy, sponsor+ARB for method; depends on MISSION); ENGINEERING CAPABILITY (protect exactly one invariant; observed->...->promoted; shape frozen under PGP-01..05; depends on MISSION+KNOWLEDGE); ENGINEERING ARTIFACT (carry knowledge in a representation, never the knowledge itself; statuses.yaml 8 states lint-enforced; owner field; depends on KNOWLEDGE); PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE SPACE (hold one product's concepts/language/contexts/bindings; authored today, generated as hypothesis n=0; owner product team; depends on KNOWLEDGE method + PRODUCT subject); PRODUCT (deliver business value; own delivery lifecycle; owner product team; depends on PKS + CAPABILITY).

a_rows_sample.anchor: causal inference compares outcomes in the same population under different interventions, whereas association compares different subsets of the population based on what actually happened.
a_rows_sample.statement: Observational Knowledge (X correlated with Y) and Causal Knowledge (intervention on X changes Y) must never have the same epistemic status; 'Teams using architecture reviews had fewer production incidents' is not equivalent to 'Introducing architecture reviews reduces production incidents', the latter requiring causal assumptions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: an effect requires specifying the outcome, the actions being compared and the population. ... CausalQuestion: population, intervention, comparator, outcome, time horizon, estimand
a_rows_sample.statement: CausalQuestion object formalized with population/intervention/comparator/outcome/time_horizon/estimand fields, replacing an unconstrained 'Does X affect Y?' question, illustrated with an example (projects using KnowledgeOS; mandatory architecture review vs none; architecture-related production defects; 12 months; average causal risk difference); called 'an epistemic schema', not merely a statistical method.

a_rows_sample.anchor: individual causal effect through the difference between Y1 = outcome if intervention happens and Y0 = outcome if intervention does not happen ... normally only one of these outcomes is observed for each individual.
a_rows_sample.statement: Counterfactual Lens: KnowledgeOS should represent causal claims as counterfactual claims (observed evidence + counterfactual estimand + identifying assumptions), not ordinary observations, since the counterfactual outcome (what defect rate a project would have had without an intervention) is never directly observed; proposed for first-class representation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: causal diagrams to identify common causes/confounding, conditioning on common effects/selection bias, measurement bias, effect modification ... KnowledgeOS should distinguish semantic relationships from causal relationships.
a_rows_sample.statement: Causal Graph Lens: a causal graph (directed edges with confounding/selection/measurement structure) differs fundamentally from an ordinary semantic knowledge-graph 'related_to' edge; proposes a distinct CausalGraph construct with explicit edge semantics rather than adding a bare 'causes' edge to the existing graph.

a_rows_sample.anchor: confounding as arising when treatment and outcome share common causes. ... CAUSAL CLAIM REVIEW ... Exchangeability: NOT ESTABLISHED ... Causal conclusion: ABSTAIN
a_rows_sample.statement: Confounding Lens as a first-class anti-false-inference mechanism, illustrated by 'experienced teams' confounding an architecture-review-vs-quality relationship; a CAUSAL CLAIM REVIEW output lists observed association, potential confounders (team maturity, project size, engineering leadership), exchangeability status, and a resulting ABSTAIN conclusion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: conditioning on common effects can produce selection bias, and even randomization does not protect against selection bias occurring after randomization. ... Why are these observations present in the evidence set?
a_rows_sample.statement: Selection-Bias Lens: selecting evidence (e.g. only successful projects) before inference can bias conclusions ('Architecture practice X works') even without explicit randomization failure; KnowledgeOS should ask why observations are present in the evidence set at all.

a_rows_sample.anchor: measurement error can make the observed association differ from the causal effect ... The observation mechanism itself becomes part of the evidence model.
a_rows_sample.statement: Measurement-Bias Lens maps to observation provenance: Reality -> Observation mechanism -> Stored evidence -> Statistical inference, with the observation mechanism itself becoming part of the evidence model, since exchangeability/positivity/consistency alone are insufficient when variables are measured incorrectly.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the relevant combinations of treatment and covariates actually occur in the population. ... Claim scope = ALL teams / Evidence support = narrow population -> POSITIVITY / GENERALISABILITY WARNING
a_rows_sample.statement: Positivity/Coverage Lens becomes an Evidence Coverage Check: a claim's scope (e.g. 'all teams') must be checked against actual evidence coverage (e.g. only large Java teams), producing a positivity/generalisability warning when scope exceeds coverage.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the observed outcome under the treatment actually received corresponds to the relevant counterfactual outcome. ... If 'treatment X' has multiple uncontrolled versions, the causal question itself may be ill-defined.
a_rows_sample.statement: Consistency Lens: the intervention must be sufficiently well-defined that 'X happened' has a single meaning (contrast vague 'AI governance' with a precisely versioned 'AI governance policy v1.3 + mandatory architecture review + defined approval workflow + defined enforcement mechanism'), connecting causal consistency to ubiquitous-language/bounded-semantics concerns.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Intervention: DO(X) ... OBSERVE -> HYPOTHESIZE -> INTERVENE -> OBSERVE OUTCOME -> UPDATE CAUSAL EVIDENCE ... KnowledgeOS becomes capable of supporting organizational learning, not merely document retrieval.
a_rows_sample.statement: Intervention Lens: represent claims as do(X) interventions with expected outcome and counterfactual, enabling an OBSERVE->HYPOTHESIZE->INTERVENE->OBSERVE OUTCOME->UPDATE CAUSAL EVIDENCE loop that supports organizational learning rather than mere document retrieval.

a_rows_sample.anchor: time-varying treatments, time-varying confounders, treatment-confounder feedback ... treatment-confounder feedback can make traditional adjustment methods biased even when the relevant confounders are measured.
a_rows_sample.statement: Time-Varying Knowledge Lens: KnowledgeOS is inherently longitudinal (X0->Y0->X1->Y1->X2->Y2, earlier decisions affecting later evidence), so a naive single-step X->Y model is often insufficient, echoing the book's warning that treatment-confounder feedback can bias traditional adjustment even with measured confounders.

a_rows_sample.anchor: variable selection for causal inference is difficult and recommend multiple sensitivity analyses rather than pretending there is one universally correct selection procedure. ... ROBUST CAUSAL CONCLUSION or CAUSAL CONCLUSION SENSITIVE TO ASSUMPTIONS
a_rows_sample.statement: Sensitivity/Triangulation Lens (called 'one of the strongest principles in the entire book'): run multiple methods/alternative assumptions/alternative causal graphs over the same evidence and check convergence, yielding either a ROBUST CAUSAL CONCLUSION or a CAUSAL CONCLUSION SENSITIVE TO ASSUMPTIONS, rather than a single model producing a single answer.

a_rows_sample.anchor: predictive ML variable selection is not equivalent to causal variable selection ... ML can be combined with causal inference through doubly robust estimators, but ML does not magically solve confounding or uncertainty.
a_rows_sample.statement: Machine Learning Lens correction: 'Prediction != causal inference' proposed as a KnowledgeOS architectural invariant, because predicting treatment well is not the same as including variables necessary for exchangeability, and unnecessary variables can increase variance or create positivity problems.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS SHALL NOT promote an associational finding to a causal claim without an explicit causal question, identified intervention and comparator, declared causal assumptions, an identifiability assessment, and an appropriate uncertainty/sensitivity assessment. ... KnowledgeOS SHALL preserve the distinction between predictive validity and causal validity.
a_rows_sample.statement: Two proposed KnowledgeOS constitutional principles synthesizing both books: (1) no promotion of an associational finding to a causal claim without explicit causal question/intervention/comparator/assumptions/identifiability assessment/uncertainty-sensitivity assessment; (2) preserve the distinction between predictive validity and causal validity, since predictive and causal models serve different purposes and predictive variable selection can be inappropriate for causal inference.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Before choosing a statistical method, determine what question you are actually trying to answer and whether that question is identifiable from the available evidence under explicit assumptions. ... KnowledgeOS needs a formal taxonomy of claim types and corresponding inference obligations.
a_rows_sample.statement: Synthesizes both source books into a single QUESTION -> {Descriptive|Associational|Causal} -> (for Causal) Identification -> {Estimation|Abstain} -> Uncertainty -> Robustness -> Sensitivity Analysis -> Epistemic Status decision hierarchy; concludes KnowledgeOS should become an 'Evidence Reasoning System with explicit statistical and causal epistemics' rather than a generic AI/ML analytics engine, and flags a formal taxonomy of claim types with corresponding inference obligations as the next architectural research step.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not automatically turn every noun into a domain object. ... conceptual richness does not prove a software bounded context.
a_rows_sample.statement: DDD warning applied to the causal vocabulary extracted from the book (Causal Question, Intervention, Comparator, Outcome, Population, Time Zero, Counterfactual, Causal Effect, Assumption, Exchangeability, Positivity, Consistency, Confounder, Mediator, Collider, Selection, Measurement, Estimand, Identification, Estimation, Sensitivity, Evidence): ownership, lifecycle, invariants, decisions, consistency boundaries, language and dependencies must be discovered before any noun becomes a domain object.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Book of Evidence tells us HOW observations become evidence ... Causal Inference tells us HOW evidence supports causal claims ... Statistical methods tell us HOW evidence is quantified ... DDD tells us HOW to model the domain ... Wisdom tells us HOW to determine what evidence is needed.
a_rows_sample.statement: Combines all four books+lenses into one epistemic operating loop: Decision -> Evidence Need -> Evidence Question -> Acquisition Design -> {Selection Procedure, Measurement Procedure, Context Conditions} -> Observation -> Acquisition Audit -> Candidate Evidence -> Evidence Assessment -> Statistical Analysis -> Causal Assessment -> Knowledge -> Wisdom -> Decision, described as 'starting to look like the actual KnowledgeOS epistemic operating loop.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: We should not conclude: 'Everything in KnowledgeOS should be Bayesian.' ... Also: Bayesian ≠ causal. ... They interact ... But they are not the same thing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit scope limits: Bayesian updating complements but does not replace deduction/causal inference/statistical estimation/formal verification/empirical testing/domain rules/logical constraints/governance/human judgment; and Bayesian belief-updating ('how should belief change given evidence?') is distinct from causal inference ('what would happen under intervention?') even though they interact in a chain Evidence->Bayesian update->belief in causal model->causal inference->decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Correlation between action and outcome does not establish causation (transition to Step 43)
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a missing dimension beyond State/Evidence/Decision/Action/Outcome: correlation between action and outcome does not establish causation. If KnowledgeOS observes Action=A followed by Outcome=B, it cannot automatically conclude A->B -- especially important if KnowledgeOS is expected to learn from its own decisions. Opens Step 43 (Causal Reasoning, Intervention, Counterfactuals and Learning from Outcomes) with the central principle that an outcome following an action does not prove the action caused the outcome, framed as essential for KnowledgeOS to 'learn from engineering decisions rather than merely record them'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(Y|A) is not generally equal to P(Y|do(A))
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces the causal layer by formalizing the central distinction between Correlation and Causation as P(Y|A) not generally equal to P(Y|do(A)) -- called one of the most important mathematical foundations for an intelligent KnowledgeOS. Motivated by the premise that observing Action=A followed by Outcome=Y does not license concluding A->Y ('temporal sequence and correlation are not sufficient to establish causation').

b_rows_sample.anchor: Decision -> StateChange -> NewBehavior -> NewState -> NewDecision; S_{t+1}=F(S_t,A_t,U_t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Motivates dynamic causal reasoning: an action changes system state, the new state changes future behavior, changing the conditions of later decisions (Decision -> StateChange -> NewBehavior -> NewState -> NewDecision). Formalizes S_{t+1} = F(S_t, A_t, U_t) (U_t = external disturbances) as the dynamic generalization of the static causal model A->B, connecting Step 16 (temporal state), Step 41 (decision sufficiency), Step 42 (invariants) and Step 43 (causality).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Dynamic causal model D=(S,A,F,O); deterministic F versus stochastic P(S_{t+1}|S_t,A_t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a dynamic causal model D=(S,A,F,O): state space S, action/intervention space A, transition function F, observation function O. Distinguishes deterministic transition S_{t+1}=F(S_t,A_t) from stochastic transition P(S_{t+1}|S_t,A_t), and states the architecture should preserve both, using F where deterministic rules are appropriate and the probabilistic form when uncertainty is intrinsic.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Action changes the future action space; state-dependent decision policy A_{t+1}=pi(S_{t+1},K_{t+1})
b_rows_sample.statement: Example: an architectural migration decision A_t changes S_t to S_{t+1}, and the new architecture changes which actions are possible later (Action_t -> FutureActionSpace), 'a crucial second-order effect'. The next decision becomes A_{t+1}=pi(S_{t+1},K_{t+1}) for decision policy pi, giving Policy + State + Knowledge -> Action.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Dynamic Bayesian state update; hidden state and belief state; state estimate != state fact
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes dynamic Bayesian updating P(S_t|K_t) -> P(S_{t+1}|K_{t+1}) after observing O_{t+1}. When the true state S_t cannot be directly observed, only O_t is observed, and P(S_t|O_1:t) represents belief about the state -- example: a service's true reliability (Healthy/Degraded) is inferred from logs/metrics/traces/alerts as P(Degraded|Observations). This gives Observation -> StateEstimate, with StateEstimate != StateFact -- uncertainty remains attached. The dynamic decision problem then uses BeliefState_t rather than State_t, with policy A_t=pi(BeliefState_t) (conceptually a partially observable decision process); KnowledgeOS's decisions should depend on KnowledgeState, never pretending KnowledgeState=Reality.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Information stability, complexity debt, and reasoning-complexity metrics
b_rows_sample.statement: A well-designed feedback loop can reduce uncertainty (H(S_{t+1}|K_{t+1}) < H(S_t|K_t)) but can also increase it if the system becomes more complex; defines Delta H = H_after - H_before, where Delta H>0 means the system became harder to understand. Introduces KnowledgeComplexity/complexity debt: an architecture change may reduce runtime risk while increasing epistemic complexity (e.g. MicroserviceCount up may increase CausalPathComplexity); proposes candidate reasoning-complexity metrics (GraphDepth, DependencyCount, CausalPathCount, ModelUncertainty, ConflictCount), explicitly not universal measures of architectural quality but indicators of reasoning complexity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Twelve falsification experiments for Step 44 dynamic-causal model (all PASS)
b_rows_sample.statement: Runs twelve falsification tests, all PASS: (1) an action changes state and future available actions => future action space recomputed; (2) a feedback loop amplifies errors => potential instability detected; (3) a feedback loop dampens errors => stabilizing behavior recognized; (4) an action has a delayed effect => causal model preserves the delay; (5) a causal cascade contains multiple paths => direct/indirect effects remain distinguishable; (6) two failures share a common cause => not treated as independent failures; (7) an action is safe immediately but unsafe over a longer horizon => safety evaluation depends on horizon; (8) an action creates an unsafe reachable state => decision gate blocks it under the relevant safety policy; (9) an intervention produces an unexpected second-order effect => outcome recorded and causal model updated, original history unchanged; (10) a hidden state is inferred from observations => state estimate retains uncertainty; (11) two causal models produce different long-term predictions => model uncertainty remains explicit; (12) a delayed feedback controller repeatedly overreacts => oscillation/instability detected as a system-level phenomenon rather than attributed to isolated decisions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 44 verdict and seven core principles
b_rows_sample.statement: Declares STEP 44 -- PASS ('extended KnowledgeOS from static to dynamic causal reasoning') and restates seven core principles: a decision changes the future state space; feedback can amplify or dampen errors; causal cascades must preserve direct, indirect, and interacting effects; common causes destroy naive independence; safety is often horizon-dependent; delayed effects are part of causality; an observed outcome must feed back into knowledge, not rewrite the historical decision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: New formal object DynamicCausalModel DCM=(S,A,F,O,tau,M)
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces DynamicCausalModel DCM=(S,A,F,O,tau,M): S=state, A=actions/interventions, F=transition mechanism, O=observations, tau=delays, M=competing models/uncertainty -- consolidating the step's dynamic, delayed, and model-uncertain causal machinery into one tuple.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Approaching a mathematical freeze; opens Step 45 on adaptive learning without corrupting historical knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: States the theoretical architecture is 'getting close to the point where it can be frozen', with remaining major questions concerning Learning, Adaptation, Model revision, Formal invariants, Computability, Complexity, Approximation, and ultimately whether a finite, executable, verifiable KnowledgeOS can be constructed from the model. Opens Step 45 (Adaptive Learning, Model Revision, Concept Drift and Knowledge Evolution) with the central question: how should KnowledgeOS change its models when reality changes without corrupting historical knowledge -- to formalize Learning, ModelUpdate, ConceptDrift, StructuralDrift, ParameterDrift, KnowledgeRevision, and the difference between learning from experience and rewriting history, framed as determining whether KnowledgeOS can be 'a continuously improving software system rather than a static knowledge repository'.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'dynamic-causal-system-model' POSSIBLY relates to 'causal-reasoning-assurance-layer' (batch B0023). Note: Step 44's dynamic-systems extension of the static causal layer: state-transition function F, deterministic/stochastic variants, belief-state/hidden-state estimation, information-stability (delta H) and complexity-debt metrics, culminating in the DCM=(S,A,F,O,tau,M) tuple; builds on but is distinct from the static causal-reasoning-assurance-layer of Step 43.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D-1 · Hook count wrong: Phase A says 8, actual is 10 ... the total was eyeballed rather than computed
a_rows_sample.statement: D-1: Phase A's high-confidence Observed claim of 8 wired hooks is wrong; the actual count via a JSON-parsing method is 10 (PreToolUse 5, PostToolUse 2, SessionStart 1, Stop 2), the original figure having been eyeballed rather than computed, with settings.json unchanged since the baseline commit ruling out temporal drift.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D-2 · 'Four of seven components have no executable substance' — false, and self-contradicting ... Phase A's own §3.1 table already says this
a_rows_sample.statement: D-2: the claim that four of seven components have no executable substance is false (the actual figure is two of eight zero-asset components) and self-contradicting, since Phase A's own detail table already correctly marks two other components PARTIAL rather than NONE.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A wrong observation is worse than an acknowledged unknown.
a_rows_sample.statement: The producer states a governing principle for its own self-review: a high-confidence Observed measurement that is wrong is worse than an honestly acknowledged unknown.

a_rows_sample.anchor: each Phase-A claim was re-derived using a different measurement method than the original, deliberately seeking falsification.
a_rows_sample.statement: The self-review method is stated as deliberate falsification-seeking: re-deriving each original claim using a measurement method different from the one originally used.

a_rows_sample.anchor: V-A · Phase A §6's own diagram sums to 10 while its caption says 8 ... it upgrades D-1 from miscount to internal inconsistency
a_rows_sample.statement: V-A (new finding): the same document's own §6 diagram already sums to 10 hooks while its caption says 8, a same-page self-contradiction of D-2's exact shape, showing the correct number was already present inside the document.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Method: every checked claim re-derived by a method different from both the original and (where known) the producer's self-review method. Falsification attempted on the load-bearing claims
a_rows_sample.statement: The verification method deliberately uses a third, independently different measurement method than both the original and the producer's self-review, and attempts falsification on load-bearing claims rather than confirming formatting.

a_rows_sample.anchor: N-1 (MODERATE) — same class as the defects repaired ... Line 1 is still v1.0 ... line 6 declares v1.1
a_rows_sample.statement: N-1 (new defect): the corrected document's own title line still says v1.0 while its version banner says v1.1, exactly the same self-contradiction shape the correction round was convened to repair, though it changes no conclusion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'Non-canonical keys anywhere in the estate: 0' is wrong; there are 20 ... the falsified measurement in fact strengthens T-1b.
a_rows_sample.statement: Verification #2 falsifies one of the refinement's own high-confidence Observed measurements (claimed 0 non-canonical keys; actual 20, e.g. `note` on 16 COMPLETE transitions the mechanism never reads), while judging the correction strengthens rather than weakens the T-1b invariant it was meant to support.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Correction 1 ... 20 instances ... Correction 2 ... DP-6 replacement instruction completed to all three cells ... Correction 3 ... OQ-10 extended
a_rows_sample.statement: Three mechanical corrections are delivered against Verification #2's R-1/R-2/R-3: the false non-canonical-key measurement is replaced with a dated 20-instance census, the DP-6 replacement instruction is completed to all three table cells, and OQ-10 is extended to record the recordedBy-referent ambiguity as a question only.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EXECUTIVE VERDICT — VERIFIED WITH NOTES ... All three corrections (R-1, R-2, R-3) are accurate
a_rows_sample.statement: Verification #3 confirms all three of the correction's own repairs (R-1/R-2/R-3) as accurate and re-derived from primary evidence, and that the change boundary held (all hunks fall inside the four declared sites, nothing reaches BC-7 ownership, the aggregate, ADR-AIP-03, or CAP-14).

a_rows_sample.anchor: F-1 ... the delivery note's own diff metric ('5 removed · 14 added') disagrees with git, which reports 16 insertions / 5 deletions.
a_rows_sample.statement: F-1 (minor): the correction's own delivery note miscounts its diff (claims 5 removed/14 added; git shows 16 insertions/5 deletions), traced to a grep-based method silently dropping two added blank lines; measured as LOW impact with no concealed semantic change.

a_rows_sample.anchor: F-2 ... R-3's '6 of 37 STARTs' is not independently reproducible. ... a plain reading gives 14 of 38.
a_rows_sample.statement: F-2 (minor): the correction's cited '6 of 37 STARTs' figure for the recordedBy-referent ambiguity cannot be independently reproduced (a plain reading yields 14 of 38), its selection rule being unstated, though the underlying conclusion is unaffected because it rests on separately confirmed facts.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Third recurrence of the method-dependent-count defect (V-D → R-1 → F-1/F-2). Repairing instances one at a time has not stopped it
a_rows_sample.statement: A recurring defect class (a measured number stated without its selection method) is named as having now recurred three times across two work items, recommended as a candidate standing rule for future KES/Governance work: a census must state its selection rule and measurement point or it is not evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Accept BC-7 correction. 2. Record F-1 and F-2 as knowledge integrity findings. 3. Do not reopen architecture model. 4. Route measurement provenance issue to future KES governance work. 5. Keep independence limitation recorded.
a_rows_sample.statement: The PO/ARB accepts Verification #3 (VERIFIED WITH NOTES) via five explicit acts: accept the correction, classify F-1/F-2 as knowledge-integrity (not architecture) findings, decline to reopen the architecture model, route the recurring measurement-provenance defect to future KES governance work, and keep the independence limitation on permanent record.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Three corrections applied under G-KOS-ARCHBASE3-CORRECT ... implementing Verification #2's R-1/R-2/R-3 and nothing else
a_rows_sample.statement: The refinement document's own banner records that it was subsequently corrected under a separate grant to apply exactly Verification #2's R-1/R-2/R-3 findings and nothing else, with the correcting pen disclosed as the same process that authored Verification #2 itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The four members and provenance: (1) Step 121 corpus audit... (2) CON-06 freeze practice... (3) F-1 (3B, synthesis); (4) CF-003 (3C, repository...) Family membership is NOT retrospective
a_rows_sample.statement: B-3: substantiates the chapter's 'fourth sighting' census of a recurring governance-gap failure family (Step 121 audit, CON-06 freeze practice, F-1, CF-003) as contemporaneously recorded, not retrospectively assembled, cross-checked against archaeology finding AF-008 confirming sightings 1-2 historically independent of 3-4.
