DeepSeek's verdict: 'Diagnostics must not mutate authoritative state — ESTABLISHED.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Domain services — class A (as functions, not services) ... foldSessions() ... assertTransitionAllowed() ... All are static/pure functions. There is no service registry, container, or injection anywhere in EKS except constructor injection inside the assurance library.
a_rows_sample.statement: EKS's domain services (foldSessions, assertTransitionAllowed, RecommendationEngine::evaluate, AssessmentService::evaluate, RecommendationInbox::classify, AnalyseCohesion::observe, plus the assurance library's four Validate* application services) are all static/pure functions; there is no service registry, container, or dependency-injection mechanism anywhere in EKS except constructor injection inside the assurance library.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Concurrency: none. workflow-state.php performs read → fold → check → append → write with no lock, no lease, no compare-and-swap, and no re-read. Two concurrent appends silently lose one.
a_rows_sample.statement: No concurrency control exists in the workflow record's write path: read -> fold -> check -> append -> write, with no lock, no lease, no compare-and-swap, and no re-read; two concurrent appends silently lose one. Explicitly deliberate per tier-1 source ('Increment 2 is not authorized'), recorded as class D, accepted debt.

a_rows_sample.anchor: E-1 erratum (applied 2026-08-22 — smallest scope, see §25.2): ... In the concurrent-append experiment, 23 / 30 trials silently lost a transition; the losing process exited 0 and reported {"ok":true,"seq":2}; every survivor was dense and monotonic. DENSITY IS NOT A COMPLETENESS PROOF.
a_rows_sample.statement: Erratum E-1: the earlier mitigation claim ('a lost transition is mechanically detectable as a gap because seq is dense/monotonic') is contradicted by a fully-read concurrent-append experiment in a different document: 23/30 trials silently lost a transition, the losing process exited 0 reporting success, and every surviving record remained dense and monotonic -- 'density is preserved BY the loss, because the clobbering writer reuses the sequence number the lost writer took.' A lost transition is therefore NOT mechanically detectable as a gap; the original sentence is preserved verbatim and this erratum is the correction, never a silent rewrite.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What is persisted vs derived ... A clean and unusually disciplined separation. The record holds facts; every interpretation is recomputed on demand. It is the strongest single design property in EKS, and it is what makes the fold trustworthy.
a_rows_sample.statement: Persisted-vs-derived separation: persisted are schema/workItem/workflow/roles[], transitions[] (verbatim, append-only, seq-stamped), grants[] (verbatim, append-only), and every JSONL row; derived-never-stored are sessions{}, each session's state, mutationOwner, workItemState, handoffsTo{}, authorizationLinkage, the authorized boolean, every resolver verdict/reason/authorizationFact, and all lint/check/dashboard output. Framed as 'the strongest single design property in EKS, and it is what makes the fold trustworthy.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Governance discipline that is genuinely enforced by construction ... refusal, ambiguity, and 'I cannot know' are first-class, tested, non-error outcomes. Very few systems get this right.
a_rows_sample.statement: Eight governance disciplines are made structural, not merely promised: lifecycle ≠ authority (two arrays never merged); absence ≠ permission ('no record = ungoverned = free' is explicitly forbidden reasoning in code); recommendation ≠ decision; observation ≠ verdict (three verdicts are structurally unemittable by machine); discovery ≠ activation (the resolver is write-free by construction, pinned by test T-11); one interpretation authority (the resolver subprocesses fold rather than parsing records itself, T-13); ambiguity is an answer (AMBIGUOUS lists all candidates, chooses none, exits 0); producer ≠ acceptor (the durability ADR binds its own producing process out of approving it). 'Refusal, ambiguity, and "I cannot know" are first-class, tested, non-error outcomes. Very few systems get this right.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: proc_open('php', <script>, 'fold') — the resolver → engine delegation ... the only inter-component protocol in EKS ... No network integration. No API. No serialization contract between components other than the JSON that fold prints on stdout.
a_rows_sample.statement: EKS's only inter-component protocol is a subprocess call (session-resolve.php spawns workflow-state.php fold via proc_open); nine integration mechanisms total are catalogued (filesystem, git CLI, the subprocess delegation, shell_exec/require_once between scripts, Composer autoload, AI-harness hooks, GitHub Actions, the KOS_MECHANISM_PATH env var, and prose cross-references resolved only by humans); there is no network integration, no API, and no serialization contract between components other than the JSON that `fold` prints to stdout.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Grant | SPLIT — the hypothesis needed correction. BC-7 owns the grant record ... It does not own the grant's authority content
b_rows_sample.statement: Testing the commission's owned-language hypotheses against evidence, Grant ownership is refined (split into record-schema ownership by BC-7 vs authority-content ownership by Governance) rather than confirmed as fully owned.

b_rows_sample.anchor: GrantScope is an opaque string ... Giving it structure ... would import governance semantics into BC-7
b_rows_sample.statement: A tactical modelling rule for the BC-7-Governance boundary: GrantScope must remain an opaque string compared only by equality; giving it structure or grammar would let the model start interpreting authority, violating the accepted boundary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: identity reads both parts of the aggregate in one call — and neither input document raises it. ... a work-item-scoped value presented inside a session-scoped answer
b_rows_sample.statement: N-1 (new observation): the `identity` query is found to read both the lifecycle and authority parts of the aggregate in a single call, presenting a work-item-scoped authorizationLinkage value inside a session-scoped answer -- a second, stronger cross-part read than F-1's, confirming rather than reopening the one-aggregate conclusion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: OQ-12 | Should invariants carry an explicit enforcement class — refused · overwritten · not-consulted · writer obligation? ... OQ-13 | Is authorizationLinkage a modelling element or a query convenience?
b_rows_sample.statement: Two new open questions are raised without proposed solutions: whether invariants should carry an explicit enforcement class distinguishing refused/overwritten/not-consulted/writer-obligation (OQ-12), and whether the identity query's authorizationLinkage is a modelling element or mere query convenience (OQ-13).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge/evidence/assessment may inform authority, but it does not create authority. ... EKS: transitions[] ≠ grants[] ... PKS: Knowledge → Assessment/Review → Recommendation → Authority Act ... AIP: produced record ≠ owned authority
b_rows_sample.statement: Strongest cross-system finding: all three systems (EKS, PKS, AIP) independently converge on 'knowledge/evidence/assessment may inform authority, but it does not create authority' -- EKS via transitions[] ≠ grants[] and Assessment never granting authority; PKS via AP-1/promotion as an explicit authority act; AIP via produced-record ≠ owned-authority; DeepSeek classifies this as ESTABLISHED in EKS/PKS, PARTIALLY ESTABLISHED in AIP -- described as 'already observable architecture', not merely a liked principle.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The governance mechanism records authority; it does not grant it, and it cannot enforce it. ... 'An illegal write is a REFUSED transition (exit 65, nothing appended) — the fold refuses; nothing is physically prevented' (workflow-state.php:11–13, tier 1).
b_rows_sample.statement: Second most important finding: the governance mechanism RECORDS authority, it does not GRANT it, and cannot ENFORCE it -- an illegal write to the record is a refused transition (exit 65, nothing appended); authority is a recorded reference to a human act, and the record refuses malformed writes to itself while preventing no engineering action whatsoever.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The only role with write authority over the Authority State. Enforced in code: if ($writer !== 'governance') { refuse(...) } ... ⚠️ '--writer-role' is a command-line argument. Anything that can run the CLI can pass --writer-role=governance. The single-writer rule is a recorded constraint, not an authenticated one
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance is the only role enforced (in code) to have write authority over the Authority State (workflow-state.php:333-335, contract test R5a); measured 126/126 grants carry registeredBy:governance (assigned by the mechanism itself, not the caller). However, --writer-role is a plain CLI argument -- anything that can run the CLI can pass --writer-role=governance -- so the single-writer rule is a recorded constraint, not an authenticated one (class D, proposition P-7).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Grant (measured over 126): exactly six fields, on all 126 ... status PROPOSED, CONSUMED, CLOSED are declared in code and never used ... authority ~90 distinct prose values ... scope min 65 · median 2,337 · max 6,037 characters ... humanActRef 63/126 are prose only ... grantId 1 duplicate across the estate
b_rows_sample.statement: Measured over all 126 grants: exactly six fields exist on every one (grantId, status, authority, humanActRef, scope, registeredBy), no seventh field ever appears. status is AUTHORIZED(125)/REVOKED(1) -- PROPOSED/CONSUMED/CLOSED are declared but never used (the grant lifecycle is not exercised). authority has ~90 distinct prose values across 126 grants (only 12/126 a bare token). scope ranges 65-6037 characters (median 2337). humanActRef is resolvable (sha or doc path) for at most 63/126; 63/126 are prose only. grantId is not enforced unique (1 duplicate, G-KOS-GOVGAPS-VERIFY, measured across the estate).

b_rows_sample.anchor: the authorized query is implemented as: if (($g['status'] ?? '') === 'AUTHORIZED' && ($g['scope'] ?? null) === $scope) ... string equality on scope. ... 'scope' is not a scope. It is a commission narrative stored in a field named 'scope.'
b_rows_sample.statement: The authority-scope finding (first-hand to this baseline, class D): the `authorized` query is implemented as raw string equality on grant `scope` (workflow-state.php:429-431); since scope has a median length of 2,337 characters (max 6,037; only 2/126 under 200 chars), asking 'is this session authorized for scope X?' requires reproducing a multi-thousand-character prose paragraph byte-for-byte -- the query is structurally implemented (class A) yet practically unanswerable (class D): 'scope is not a scope. It is a commission narrative stored in a field named scope.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Delegation — OBSERVED BEHAVIOUR, SEMANTIC INTERPRETATION UNKNOWN ... 0/126 grants carry a delegation, delegator, delegatee, parent-grant, validity, or expiry field. The narrowing is visible in prose scope text only, and prose is not a model.
b_rows_sample.statement: Grants on a work item are observed to frequently narrow over time (e.g. one item carries 23 grants, many successive amendment-scoped acts), but the business concept 'Delegation' is explicitly NOT established as existing in the current EKS model: 0/126 grants carry any delegation, delegator, delegatee, parent-grant, validity, or expiry field; the narrowing is visible only in prose scope text, and 'prose is not a model.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: The system RECORDS authority. It does not GRANT authority. Verbatim in tier-1 source: 'a grant registers a recorded human act by reference — the record never manufactures authority (G-2/R5b).'
b_rows_sample.statement: The system RECORDS authority, it does not GRANT authority: a grant registers a recorded human act by reference; the record never manufactures authority. Corroborated by measurement: 126/126 grants carry a humanActRef and 0/126 carry anything the mechanism could have generated as authority itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: U-13 | Evidence addressing partially mutable — 7/20 observed grants reference artifacts descriptively rather than immutably; evidence provenance can drift ... An honest UNKNOWN is valid; an artificial UNKNOWN is a defect.
b_rows_sample.statement: UNKNOWN register entry U-13: evidence addressing is partially mutable -- a measured 7/20 sampled grants reference artifacts descriptively rather than immutably (e.g. by path rather than by content hash/commit), so evidence provenance can drift; the register's governing rule throughout is 'an honest UNKNOWN is valid; an artificial UNKNOWN is a defect' -- no gap is filled to make the reconstruction coherent.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Exactly one mutation owner per work item is a mechanically enforced invariant (I-1)
b_rows_sample.statement: Grants: a grant without a humanActRef is refused by the engine ('the record never manufactures authority -- G-2/R5b'). Exactly one mutation owner per work item is mechanically enforced (I-1). Closure is a governance act (G-1): COMPLETE refuses any writer but governance/human. Producer != acceptor (R-34, INV-ATTR-2): a process cannot verify/accept its own work; separation is declared, not attestable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Family 3 -- AUTHORITY (Who/What may authorize?)
b_rows_sample.statement: Family 3 (AUTHORITY) table: INV-003 Assessment != Authority (ESTABLISHED, forbids Assessment->Authority; an instance of Relation-001); Authority-as-Recorded-Reference (C-1, STRONG landscape row -- EKS grant 126/126 humanActRef, PKS Charter G-17, AIP grant G-2/R5b -- 'the record references a human act; it never manufactures authority'; forbids Record->Authority; whether this landscape row is SAME or RELATED to the register's authority rows across systems is UNKNOWN, U-02).

b_rows_sample.anchor: CORRECTION TO MY OWN PRIOR PASS: canonical-construction/21 stated: "INNOVATION is required in exactly one place: a typed AuthorityAct (0 corpus occurrences)." That was wrong. I searched for the string AuthorityAct and concluded the concept was absent. The concept exists, is named Grant, is corpus-de
b_rows_sample.statement: Self-correction: an earlier pass (canonical-construction/21) claimed a typed AuthorityAct required pure innovation because a literal string search for 'AuthorityAct' found zero corpus occurrences; this was a lexical error -- the concept exists under the name Grant ('Grant = recorded reference to human act', architecture/Epistemic-Architecture-Investigation.md:265), is corpus-defined, and is implemented with fields grantId/status/authority/humanActRef/registeredBy/scope across 132/132 measured work items -- the same Grant entity the B0002 object 'grant-record' already identifies (BC-7 owns the grant record schema but not the authority content it refers to).

a_rows_sample.anchor: A philosophical-interpretation study run alongside KR-REP-REDUCTION-AUDIT-2026-09. Nothing here is adopted; nothing may become a primitive. The layer ban is in force: a reading may yield a question, a lens or a corroboration -- never an entity.
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames this as a philosophical-interpretation study run alongside the executing KR-REP-REDUCTION-AUDIT-2026-09, explicitly under the project's layer ban: a scriptural reading may yield only a question, a lens, or a corroboration, never a promoted entity, with Theory v1.2 as the frozen baseline.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The audit's decisive finding was not a computational error. It was an assumption two parties held and neither tested -- that desc = (n+1) - asc. I asserted it; review restated it in better vocabulary; the tie-break falsified it, 21 369 times.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports the first concrete finding of the actually-executed KR-REP-REDUCTION-AUDIT-2026-09: the decisive problem was not a computational error but a shared, never-tested assumption that the descending rank equals (n+1) minus the ascending rank (desc=(n+1)-asc), which the tie-breaking mechanics falsified 21,369 times -- an assumption asserted by one party and merely restated in better vocabulary by a reviewing party, caught only because the audit protocol required 'formally prove' rather than 'state'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Krsna's first substantive line is not a correction of Arjuna's conclusion. It is the observation that his reasoning is well-formed and his premise is not examined. prajna-vadan -- words of wisdom -- is not sarcasm; the argument is competent. The defect is upstream of the argument. ... results.md par
a_rows_sample.statement: Reads Gita 2.11 ('you grieve for those who should not be grieved for, and you speak words of wisdom') as corroborating (C-1) that a well-formed, competently-argued document (results.md section 5, reviewed and improved in wording by a second party) can rest on an unexamined premise since neither pass touched the premise -- only the audit's 'formally prove' requirement did -- while explicitly warning that this corroborates only the value of an audit step and supplies no method for identifying which premise needs examining.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Gita does not counsel living with doubt. It counsels CUTTING it -- by knowledge, decisively. ... an unexamined assumption and a live doubt are different failure modes. samsaya is doubt one has; the section 5 error was an assumption one does not know one has. ... review interrogates what is state
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts lens L-1 from Gita 4.40/4.42 ('cut the doubt with the sword of knowledge'): an unexamined assumption (one does not know one has) is a different failure mode from a live doubt (samsaya, one knowingly has), with the text addressing only the latter and being silent on the former; frames this as the whole difference between review (interrogates what is stated) and audit (interrogates what is assumed).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The audit was run knowing it might destroy the experiment's headline result. It did. ... the verse's structure is exactly the methodological commitment: execute the check; do not select it by its expected outcome. A checklist run only where one expects to pass is not a checklist. [EXT] only. The pro
a_rows_sample.statement: Reads Gita 2.47 ('your right is to the work, never to its fruits') as the most apt corroboration (C-2) of running the audit knowing it might destroy the experiment's headline result -- which it did -- framing the verse's structure as exactly the methodological commitment to execute a check independent of its expected outcome, while marking this as [EXT] only, since the programme already reached this discipline from its own prior failures (the vacuity guard, the paired-design correction, the positive control); the verse agrees but did not teach it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A tempting reading: at the end, set the framework aside and trust the synthesis. REFUSED. This is the most dangerous verse in the text for a research programme, because it licenses exactly what the governance freeze forbids: a shortcut from evidence to conviction. ... it is the second time this stra
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly refuses reading Gita 18.66 ('abandoning all duties, take refuge in Me alone') as license to set the analytical framework aside at the end and trust the synthesis, judging it the most dangerous verse in the text for a research programme because it would license exactly the evidence-to-conviction shortcut the governance freeze forbids (EXPERIMENT -> AUDIT -> ADJUDICATION -> THEORY v1.3, no shortcut), noting this is the second time this study strand has had to refuse its own most quotable verse, after 2.50 ('skill in action') in the prior study.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a well-formed argument can rest on an unexamined premise: 2.11 corroborates. execute the check regardless of expected outcome: 2.47 corroborates. unexamined assumption != live doubt: 4.40-42 lens only. which premise to examine: nothing -- and this is the gap that matters. shortcut from evidence to t
a_rows_sample.statement: Produces an eight-row corroboration map cross-referencing each audit element (well-formed-argument-on-unexamined-premise, execute-check-regardless-of-outcome, assumption-vs-doubt, the tie-break entanglement, bootstrap bias, N_viol as bias-free check, which-premise-to-examine, evidence-to-theory shortcut) against its Gita locus and relation, finding four of eight audit elements -- including every technical finding -- get nothing from the text, which speaks only to the posture of auditing, never its content.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-15: a well-formed argument may rest on an unexamined premise; competence is not verification. lens [PROP] already operationalized by the audit protocol. G-16: unexamined assumption != live doubt -- review interrogates what is stated, audit what is assumed. lens [PROP] the sharper of the two. G-17:
a_rows_sample.statement: Registers four candidates from this study: G-15 (lens, [PROP], already operationalized by the audit protocol) -- a well-formed argument may rest on an unexamined premise, competence is not verification; G-16 (lens, [PROP], the sharper of the two) -- unexamined assumption differs from live doubt, review interrogates what is stated while audit interrogates what is assumed; G-17 (corroboration, [EXT]) -- execute the check independently of its expected outcome, established internally rather than learned from the text; and G-18 (REFUSED, [NEG]) -- setting the framework aside for the synthesis, which contradicts the governance freeze; records three explicit refusals (samsaya as an audit state, jnana-asi as an operator, 18.66 as a methodological warrant).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sixth consecutive time. ... C-1 binds (no mechanism enters the kernel merely because KnowledgeOS can use it) ... the layer ban forbids the derivation chain ... the governance freeze forbids any kernel modification before adjudication ... the programme's record is unbroken -- the Gita has yielded que
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports zero kernel candidates for the sixth consecutive Gita study, reaffirming that the C-1 binding rule (no mechanism enters the kernel merely because KnowledgeOS can use it), the layer ban (forbidding the derivation chain from reading to kernel entity), and the governance freeze (forbidding kernel modification before adjudication) together keep the kernel NOT SELECTABLE, with the study programme's record unbroken across six studies.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Not that the Gita anticipated audit methodology. It supplies posture, not protocol -- and the gap it leaves (which premise to examine) is exactly the gap the checklist filled. Not that corroboration strengthens the audit. The 21 369 violations are exactly as decisive before and after this document.
a_rows_sample.statement: States three things that must not be concluded from this study: that the Gita anticipated audit methodology (it supplies posture, not protocol, and never fills the gap of which premise to examine -- only the checklist does that); that corroboration strengthens the audit finding (the 21,369 rank-tie violations are exactly as decisive with or without this document); and that two refusals across two studies mean the text is unproductive (a source that never requires refusal is not being read critically).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The strongest statement made must never exceed the strength of the available evidence. This study's yield is two lenses, one corroboration, and one refusal. The refusal -- of the text's most famous verse, because it would license the one shortcut the programme forbids -- is again the most useful of
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the governing principle that the strongest statement made must never exceed the strength of available evidence, summarizing this study's total yield as two lenses (G-15, G-16), one corroboration (G-17), and one refusal (G-18), judging the refusal of the text's most famous verse -- because it would license the one shortcut the programme forbids -- to be again the most useful of the four.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An attractive interpretation must yield to an audit finding. ... the representation-reduction audit found: the bootstrap confidence interval procedure was invalid for the sparse conditional-entropy estimator; the rank invertibility claim failed because of tie handling. Those failures did not invalid
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports that the representation-reduction audit found two specific problems -- the bootstrap confidence-interval procedure was invalid for the sparse conditional-entropy estimator, and the rank-invertibility claim failed due to tie handling (matching the desc=(n+1)-asc falsification) -- neither of which invalidated the main structural conclusions (which rested on exact violation counts and train/test agreement), but both of which forced withdrawal of the affected claims, establishing the principle that an attractive interpretation must yield to an audit finding, essential if KnowledgeOS is to govern AI-generated knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'Ascending and descending rank are merely invertible recodings.' The audit showed that deterministic tie-breaking makes this claim false in the implemented experiment.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally records the rejection of the claim that ascending and descending rank encodings are merely invertible recodings, since the audit showed deterministic tie-breaking makes this false in the implemented experiment -- the theory-level record of the desc=(n+1)-asc falsification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: desc != (n+1)-asc [for D with ties, e.g. D=[23000,46000,46000]] ... The implemented ascending/descending rank transformations were not proven to be simple invertible recodings. ... A representational convention can carry operational consequences. But the pure 'decoder-only effect' attribution was to
a_rows_sample.statement: Records the formal audit correction that the ascending/descending rank transformations were not proven to be simple invertible recodings, since deterministic tie-breaking on data with repeated values (e.g. D=[23000,46000,46000]) makes desc != (n+1)-asc; the broader lesson survives (a representational convention can carry operational consequences) but the pure 'decoder-only effect' attribution was too strong and had to be corrected after audit.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The audit's findings -- 1,395 verified, 0/33,840, 40.2% class contamination -- are exactly as strong before and after this document.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports three concrete figures from the executed KR-REP-REDUCTION corpus audit as of 2026-09-03: 1,395 verified cases, a 0/33,840 result (a zero-count structural check over 33,840 items, consistent in scale with the subsets.jsonl-derived pairwise counts discussed elsewhere in the thread), and a 40.2% class-contamination finding -- all stated to be unaffected in strength by the philosophical corroboration study itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is the 5 digits -> 2 digits trap in Sanskrit dress. ... A reading that treats compactness as a virtue would import exactly the error the mandate forbids.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly refuses the most tempting available reading -- that Gita 2.50 ('yoga is skill in action') licenses treating representational compactness as inherently virtuous -- citing the master handoff's section 25 warning that digit count is not itself a representation-capacity measure and that a two-digit representation may carry MORE information capacity than a five-digit one depending on encoding, recording the refusal as the study's most useful yield.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Trust(A_t, K_supreme) = Surrender + Non-attachment + Engagement
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a three-term additive formalization of the Knower-to-Source trust relation, offered as solving 'the relationship between the Knower (Arjuna) and the Supreme Knowledge (Krishna)', with no stated units, domain, or way to evaluate the sum.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Epistemic Trust > Pure Abstraction … Trust enables transformation; abstraction alone does not
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues, from Krishna's statement that the personal-devotion path is easier than the abstract-formless path, that 'epistemic trust' is architecturally superior to 'pure abstraction' for KnowledgeOS, without defining either term against the ratified architecture's actual vocabulary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Manas \neq Buddhi ... Mind → where attention is directed ... Buddhi → discrimination, determination, intelligence.
b_rows_sample.statement: From Gita 12.8 (fix mind on the Lord, engage intelligence in Him): Mind = attention/orientation, Buddhi = discrimination/intelligence; these must not be collapsed (Manas != Buddhi). KnowledgeOS Kernel decomposes into a Mind branch (maintains orientation/attention) and a Buddhi branch (discriminates/evaluates); formalized as M_t = current epistemic orientation, B_t = current discrimination capability, with (M_t,B_t,K_t) hypothesized as more informative than K_t alone -- explicitly not yet a proposed new state model, a hypothesis to test against the eight primitives and Sigma.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel should have degraded/fallback modes
b_rows_sample.statement: Chapter 12's fallback hierarchy (fixed mind -> practice -> dedicated action -> renunciation of results -> stable state, when steady fixation is difficult) suggests a Kernel design principle: the Kernel should have degraded/fallback modes since not every epistemic operation is fully resolvable (Direct Determination -> failure -> Controlled Practice -> failure -> Defined Action -> failure -> Result Detachment -> Stable State). Connects directly to the unresolved Qualify/G1 operation: proposes Qualify(x) not as 'prove everything about x' but as 'determine the strongest justified epistemic disposition available', tentatively over a set like {Confirmed, Supported, Uncertain, Unknown, Rejected, Deferred} -- explicitly not proposed as canonical values. Builds on the Step 286 Cavell hypothesis that qualification may legitimately terminate rather than being infinitely justified.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Epistemic status should depend on evidence/criteria, not emotional or outcome preference. ... Truth evaluation \perp outcome preference
b_rows_sample.statement: From Chapter 12's equanimity verses (fixed and free from disturbance amid happiness/distress, honor/dishonor, friend/enemy, praise/criticism): Evaluation != Reaction -- a Kernel should not change a proposition's epistemic status merely because it is praised, attacked, desirable or undesirable. Proposed invariant: epistemic status should depend on evidence/criteria, not emotional or outcome preference; formalized as Truth evaluation _|_ (independent of) outcome preference, warning against a weak-system failure mode where a desired outcome C causes evidence A to be reinterpreted as supporting C. Also proposes a Perturbation Resistance property: given external disturbance epsilon on K_t, a robust Kernel should route through Buddhi to evaluate epsilon rather than blindly computing K_{t+1}=f(K_t,epsilon).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Stable orientation \neq fixed conclusions
b_rows_sample.statement: From verse 12.14's drdha-niscayah (fixed determination): raises the tension Stability vs Revisability -- when should determination persist vs. yield to new evidence (connecting to contradiction, supersession, state transition, evidence, provenance, equality, knowledge revision). Preliminary Kernel invariant: Stable orientation != fixed conclusions; the Kernel can remain oriented toward its governing epistemic purpose while changing conclusions as evidence changes: Goal_t=Goal_{t+1} does not imply K_t=K_{t+1} (Goal stable AND Knowledge revisable). Concluding synthesis: 'Kernel stability != Knowledge-state stability', proposed as potentially one of the foundational ideas of KnowledgeOS.

Ten labeled H12 hypotheses (research findings, not canonical architecture): H12-1 Kernel has an orientation/attention aspect analogous to Mind (Candidate); H12-2 Kernel has a discrimination capability analogous to Buddhi (Strong candidate); H12-3 Mind and Buddhi should not be collapsed into one function (Candidate); H12-4 Stable orientation can coexist with changing knowledge state (Strong candidate); H12-5 Epistemic evaluation should be independent of desired outcome (Strong candidate); H12-6 Kernel should be robust against external disturbance (Candidate); H12-7 Failure of direct determination should permit controlled fallback (Strong candidate); H12-8 Qualification may represent a legitimate epistemic endpoint rather than an infinite proof obligation (Candidate; connects to G1); H12-9 Knowledge-state revision should not imply loss of Kernel identity (Candidate); H12-10 Kernel requires a governing orientation, but its KnowledgeOS equivalent is unresolved (OPEN).

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would NOT yet add any new primitive ... Mind/Buddhi \rightarrow candidate\ Kernel\ capabilities
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit refusal to add Mind, Buddhi, Practice, Devotion, Determination, or Peace as new primitives; the ratified KnowledgeOS primitive set remains {Entity, State, Event, Observation, Proposition, Relation, Policy, Action}. Chapter 12 has not demonstrated Mind or Buddhi must be a new primitive; the better interpretation is Mind/Buddhi -> candidate Kernel capabilities, not new primitives. Also warns against translating Krishna -> Authority directly (would violate methodology); instead proposes 'a Kernel requires an orientation target' and poses the open question of the KnowledgeOS equivalent of the Kernel's governing objective (candidates: Truth, Epistemic validity, Governed knowledge, Purpose-defined correctness), to be derived independently, noting this is where Governance becomes relevant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Can the existing KnowledgeOS eight primitives and the five-axis \Sigma=(A,S,R,V,C) express the proposed Mind–Buddhi–Kernel behavior without introducing a new primitive?
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes pausing philosophical interpretation after Chapter 12 to test mathematically: can the existing eight primitives and five-axis Sigma=(A,S,R,V,C) express the proposed Mind-Buddhi-Kernel behavior without a new primitive? Specifically test whether Buddhi = an operation over existing primitives, Mind = a state/orientation over existing primitives, and Kernel = (K_t, operations, invariants, transition rules) -- framed as the first real mathematical/DDD test of the 'KnowledgeOS Kernel = Mind' interpretation.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'hpa-gita-chapter12-mind-buddhi-orientation-stability' POSSIBLY relates to 'gita-bhakti-epistemic-trust-model' (batch B0054). Note: A second, distinct hpa reading of Gita Chapter 12 (Bhakti-yoga), oriented around 12.8 (fix mind, engage intelligence) rather than the existing trust/relationship (Sraddha/devotion) reading. Proposes Mind=orientation/attention, Buddhi=discrimination, tests Kernel != passive container, a degraded/fallback-mode hierarchy connecting to the unresolved Qualify/G1 operation, a Perturbation Resistance property, the Evaluation != Reaction invariant, and ten H12 hypotheses, explicitly declining to add Mind/Buddhi as new primitives beyond the ratified eight.

a_rows_sample.anchor: "deployment succeeded." ... Zero detects the missing dimension ... Unknown\neq False
a_rows_sample.statement: Concrete worked example testing the accumulated kernel model: kernel receives assertion 'the production deployment has succeeded' with no runtime evidence (E=empty-set); runs Observe->Discriminate->Qualify(P,E,C,T,Pi); Zero detects Z(K_t)=missing evidence; the kernel does NOT conclude P=false, reconfirming Unknown != False as one of the strongest results of the Gita+Zero interpretation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: o_t = \Omega_{G_t} \left( B_t,K_t,Z_t \right)
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the guna mode as selecting an operator POLICY, not merely a descriptive label: o_t = Omega_{G_t}(B_t,K_t,Z_t), giving Tamas mode o=Ignore; Rajas mode o=Search->Act->Search; Sattva mode o=Discriminate->Qualify->(Act or Stop) -- illustrated on identical K_t and O_t across modes, giving 'different modes of mind -> different operators/behaviour' a formal shape.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \operatorname{Stop}(K_t) ... No further qualification is presently justified.
a_rows_sample.statement: Discovers a missing operator through simulation: when Buddhi cannot determine sufficiency, the kernel needs Escalate or SeekQualification -- the kernel must know when NOT to decide. Proposes Stop(K_t) as a legitimate kernel operation: a disciplined kernel can say 'no further qualification is presently justified', which is an epistemic decision, not a failure -- contrasted with a bad kernel's uncertainty->more computation->more computation loop. Gives Qualify(x) codomain {Qualified,Rejected,Suspended,Escalated,bot}, with bot meaning the kernel has reached a legitimate epistemic terminus, connecting to the Cavell insight.

a_rows_sample.anchor: J_t = w_A A_t+ w_S S_t+ w_R R_t+ w_V V_t+ w_C C_t - \lambda Z_t - \mu U_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes, explicitly non-canonical/for research purposes only, a candidate kernel objective function J_t = w_A A_t + w_S S_t + w_R R_t + w_V V_t + w_C C_t - lambda Z_t - mu U_t (weighted five Sigma axes minus unresolved-gap term Z minus unjustified-commitment term U), with purification meaning J_{t+1}>J_t -- explicitly not adopted because the measurement scales and per-axis ordering remain unresolved (per Step 287). Proposes Moksha as the limiting condition where repeated purification cycles reach Delta J -> 0 (the kernel can no longer improve the state under the available epistemic horizon) -- a philosophical hypothesis, not an architecture decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P1 — Kernel is active ... P7 — Kernel mode affects operation selection
a_rows_sample.statement: Seven candidate principles from the simulation: P1 Kernel != Knowledge Store (active epistemic processor); P2 Buddhi=discrimination, B:state+observation+context->epistemic discrimination; P3 Knowledge is dynamic, K_t!=K_{t+1}; P4 Zero is epistemically constructive, Zero(K_t)=representation of detected absence/obstruction; P5 Purification is quality transformation, Purify(K_t) not-equiv AddKnowledge(K_t); P6 Outcome is independent from epistemic validity, valid reasoning != successful outcome; P7 Kernel mode affects operation selection, G_t -> Omega_{G_t} -- assessed as the potential mathematical foundation for the Sattva/Rajas/Tamas model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel = the smallest persistent epistemic mechanism capable of representing a knowledge state, discriminating over it, and producing a governed transformation of that state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Concludes the smallest meaningful kernel cannot be merely a data structure; needs at least Represent + Discriminate + Transform, with Zero/Purification/Action/Guna/provenance understood around this core. Candidate research definition (explicitly not ratified canonical): KnowledgeOS Kernel = the smallest persistent epistemic mechanism capable of representing a knowledge state, discriminating over it, and producing a governed transformation of that state -- explicitly noting Steps 285-287 deliberately leave canonicalization, equality, Qualify, and governance unresolved.

a_rows_sample.anchor: input \rightarrow precondition \rightarrow Buddhi decision \rightarrow state transformation \rightarrow postcondition \rightarrow Zero effect \rightarrow provenance
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes the concluding research step 'Define the Kernel Algebra': stop adding Gita chapters and take the simulated kernel through a formal operator analysis of {Observe,Attend,Discriminate,Qualify,Compare,Transform,Purify,Act,Expose,Stabilize,Stop,Escalate}, determining for every operator a 7-step profile: input -> precondition -> Buddhi decision -> state transformation -> postcondition -> Zero effect -> provenance, then testing composition, idempotence, commutativity, associativity, reversibility, monotonicity, mode-dependence and purification effects -- framed as turning the philosophical interpretation into an actual mathematical research programme.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 11 fenced blocks. ALL are ```text. ZERO are code. ... it does NOT overclaim
a_rows_sample.statement: Audits S2252's kernel 'simulation' as a sixth artifact carrying a title (simulation/executable) the programme has previously found (INV-9/EV-F2) to contain no program in five prior corpus steps; this one likewise contains zero executable code (11 fenced blocks, all plain text). Unlike those five, this artifact does NOT overclaim empirical validation -- its own opening states it is a hypothetical test of internal coherence, not a claim the Gita defines KnowledgeOS. Classified as evidence class ANALYTIC-worked-scenario, not EXECUTED, correctly scoped by its own text and must never be cited as executed evidence -- recorded because the word 'simulation' in the title risks being misread as execution by a later agent who sees only the title.

a_rows_sample.anchor: (K_t,Sigma_t,G_t) -Buddhi+O_i-> (K_{t+1},Sigma_{t+1},G_{t+1}) ... K_0 -O_1-> K_1 -O_2-> K_2 -> ... -> K_n and measure Sigma_0,...,Sigma_n against the discovered invariants. Now purification becomes something we can simulate rather than merely describe.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a simulation model (K_t,Sigma_t,G_t) --Buddhi+O_i--> (K_{t+1},Sigma_{t+1},G_{t+1}), with a trajectory K_0-O1->K_1-O2->K_2->...->K_n measured against the discovered invariants via Sigma_0,...,Sigma_n -- 'purification becomes something we can simulate rather than merely describe.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Jñāna : (K_t,\;Doubt_t) \rightarrow (K_{t+1},\;Doubt_{t+1})
b_rows_sample.statement: From the closing verses (knowledge as a weapon that cuts doubt arising from ignorance): models Jnana not as a primitive/object but as a transformation operator J:(K_t,Doubt_t)->(K_{t+1},Doubt_{t+1}), with intended effect Doubt_{t+1}<Doubt_t under appropriate conditions -- reinforcing the earlier Jnana~delta interpretation over Jnana=Knowledge. Also formalizes Ajnana->Samsaya->Jnana->Buddhi->Karma as a candidate kernel cycle: ignorance->doubt->investigation->knowledge->discrimination->decision->action->new observation->updated K_t.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero \neq Doubt ... "I don't know X." -> Zero ... "I have two conflicting claims about X." -> Samsaya
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly separates five concepts previously at risk of conflation: Zero (detection of missing/absent knowledge, 'I don't know X'); Samsaya/doubt (unresolved epistemic uncertainty, 'I have two conflicting claims about X'); Ajnana (lack/absence of understanding); Jnana (knowledge/transformation that resolves or transforms uncertainty, 'evidence establishes claim A'); Buddhi (discrimination/decision capability, 'therefore accept A'). Zero != Doubt is proposed as an excellent candidate for formalization.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t=(X_t,\Sigma_t,\Pi_t,\Gamma_t,\Delta_t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes KnowledgeOS is not fundamentally a set (beyond K_t subset K): a five-component knowledge state K_t=(X_t,Sigma_t,Pi_t,Gamma_t,Delta_t) where X_t=represented knowledge content, Sigma_t=epistemic quality/state dimensions, Pi_t=provenance, Gamma_t=context/constraints, Delta_t=detected gaps/uncertainties, with kernel transitions K_{t+1}=F(K_t,O_t,B_t,A_t) -- assessed as a much richer mathematical object than K_t subset K alone.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Content equality? ... Epistemic equality? ... Provenance-sensitive equality? ... Behavioural equality?
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly connects Chapter 4's doubt/knowledge/lineage material to the Step 287 open equality problem K_1 equiv K_2, posing four distinct candidate readings: content equality (X_1=X_2); epistemic equality (Sigma_1=Sigma_2); provenance-sensitive equality ((X_1,Pi_1) cong_lambda (X_2,Pi_2)); behavioural equality (delta(K_1,o)=delta(K_2,o) for all o). States plainly that Chapter 4 gives philosophical motivation for asking this question but does not provide the mathematical answer -- Step 287's OPEN status remains correct.

Constructs a five-operator formal algebra: Omega:W->O (observe), Q:O->E (qualify), J:ExK->K' (know/transform), B:K'xC->D (discriminate), A:D->W' (act), with explicit composition K_{t+1}=J(Q(Omega(W_t)),K_t), D_t=B(K_{t+1},C_t), W_{t+1}=A(D_t,W_t). Proposes working kernel definition Kernel=(K_t,Omega,Q,J,B,A,Delta,Sigma,Pi) with central transition K_t --Omega,Q--> E_t --J--> K'_t --B--> D_t --A--> W_{t+1} --Omega--> K_{t+1}, explicitly non-canonical pending formal validation. Frames Chapter 4's strongest contribution as a theory of what the kernel DOES with knowledge (Knowledge->discrimination->decision->action->new state), not another primitive.

b_rows_sample.anchor: freeze a KERNEL-CANDIDATE-v1 consisting of only \{K_t,\;Zero,\;Sa\d{m}śaya,\;Jñāna,\;Buddhi,\;Decision,\;Action\}
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommends, before simulating the whole Gita-KnowledgeOS system, freezing a minimal KERNEL-CANDIDATE-v1 = {K_t, Zero, Samsaya, Jnana, Buddhi, Decision, Action} and mathematically testing operators J, B, A, Omega, Q for closure, typing, identity, composition, reversibility, monotonicity, and information loss -- explicit caution that the source's religious claims must not be converted into technical claims by analogy alone; the strongest candidates are those independently derivable from KnowledgeOS per Step 286. Chapter 4 generates and corroborates hypotheses; it does not ratify the kernel.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'hpa-gita-chapter4-doubt-jnana-transformation-operator' POSSIBLY relates to 'gita-kernel-simulation-deployment-example-coherence-test' (batch B0054). Note: Rereads Gita Chapter 4 (Jnana Yoga, doubt destroyed by knowledge) against the completed Chapters 5-18 model, adding the missing layer of how the kernel transforms knowledge and resolves doubt. Proposes the pipeline Ajnana(ignorance)->Samsaya(doubt)->Jnana(investigation/knowledge)->Buddhi(discrimination)->Karma(action), models Jnana as a TRANSFORMATION OPERATOR J:(K_t,Doubt_t)->(K_{t+1},Doubt_{t+1}) with intended Doubt_{t+1}<Doubt_t (not merely a primitive/object), and explicitly separates Zero (missing/absent knowledge) from Samsaya/doubt (unresolved uncertainty between conflicting claims) in a five-row table (Zero/Samsaya/Ajnana/Jnana/Buddhi). Proposes a five-component knowledge state K_t=(X_t,Sigma_t,Pi_t,Gamma_t,Delta_t) [content, epistemic quality, provenance, context, detected gaps]. Poses four distinct candidate readings of K_1 equiv K_2 (content equality, epistemic equality, provenance-sensitive cong_lambda, behavioural equality via delta) as motivated but NOT solved by Chapter 4, explicitly preserving Step 287's OPEN status. Gives Knowledge != Action but Knowledge -> better-qualified action, reinforcing Command != Transformation. Proposes a five-operator formal algebra Omega(observe),Q(qualify),J(know/transform),B(discriminate),A(act) with explicit composition K_{t+1}=J(Q(Omega(W_t)),K_t), D_t=B(K_{t+1},C_t), W_{t+1}=A(D_t,W_t). Closes by proposing to freeze a KERNEL-CANDIDATE-v1={K_t,Zero,Samsaya,Jnana,Buddhi,Decision,Action} and mathematically test operators J,B,A,Omega,Q for closure/typing/identity/composition/reversibility/monotonicity/information-loss before continuing to add Gita terminology.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 3 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: Human first has/conceives an Ideal State ... IDEAL STATE -> EXPECTATIONS/CRITERIA -> OBSERVATION -> COMPARISON -> DETERMINATION -> FACT/KNOWLEDGE. That is a substantially different model from the one I was using before.
a_rows_sample.statement: Major reorientation: humans do not build up an ideal state from arbitrary observations; instead a human first has/conceives an Ideal State and then evaluates reality against it, giving the pipeline IDEAL STATE -> EXPECTATIONS/CRITERIA -> OBSERVATION -> COMPARISON -> DETERMINATION -> FACT/KNOWLEDGE, substantially reversing the previously-used observation-first model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ideal state ... The complete state of what is supposed to be known/true/valid for the thing at that point in time. ... all applicable rules; all required participants; ... I_t = Ideal Knowledge State at t ... O_t -- comparison with I_t --> K_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the ideal state I_t broadly as the complete state of what is supposed to be known/true/valid for a thing at time t; for an election system this would include all applicable rules, required participants, required conditions, valid relationships, required evidence, expected states, constraints, applicable laws, and known principles; every new piece of observed information O_t is evaluated against I_t, giving the extraction problem O_t --comparison with I_t--> K_t.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Information that correctly describes some aspect of the ideal state is Knowledge. ... K_t subset I_t ... The ideal state itself may be unknown to us. ... I_t -- the theoretical ideal state, and hat-I_t -- our current extracted/estimated representation of it. Then: hat-I_t != I_t in general. That may actually explain your earlier statement: "We try our best but never achieve the best."
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines 'information on the ideal state is knowledge' to 'information that correctly describes some aspect of the ideal state is Knowledge', giving K_t subset-or-equal I_t as the established/identified portion of the ideal state -- but the ideal state I_t itself may be unknown to us, so we must distinguish the theoretical ideal state I_t from our current extracted/estimated representation hat-I_t, with hat-I_t != I_t in general, explaining 'we try our best but never achieve the best'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(x|O_{<=t},I_t^known) ... Probability is involved in extracting the ideal state from imperfect observations. Not: Knowledge=Probability. Instead: Probability models the uncertainty of our extraction of the ideal state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Locates probability's role: for an ideal-state element x, given incomplete and overlapping observations O_1..O_n we estimate P(x|O_{<=t},I_t^known); probability is involved in extracting the ideal state from imperfect observations, not in defining Knowledge -- probability models the uncertainty of our extraction of the ideal state, not Knowledge itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: System must have backup capability ... backup configuration exists ... If the applicable reasoning rules determine that the observation satisfies the criterion, we establish: F_t: "System has backup capability." ... the fact is not produced merely from the observation. It is produced by: Observation + Ideal State + Comparison Criteria + Reasoning.
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example of fact production: ideal state I_t requires 'system must have backup capability', observation O_t is 'backup configuration exists'; comparing O_t against I_t via applicable reasoning rules establishes fact F_t='System has backup capability' -- a fact is produced not merely from observation but from Observation + Ideal State + Comparison Criteria + Reasoning together.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Logic = mechanism for comparing/deriving consequences from the ideal state and observed state. ... I_t: A and B and C. Observed: O_t: A,B,not-C. Logic gives: O_t does not entail I_t. Therefore the determination might be: F_t: "Current state does not satisfy the ideal state."
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines logic's role as the mechanism for comparing/deriving consequences from the ideal state and observed state: given ideal state I_t=(A and B and C) and observed O_t=(A,B,not-C), logic determines O_t does not entail I_t, yielding determination F_t='Current state does not satisfy the ideal state'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(A)=1, P(B)=0.9, P(C)=0.6, P(D)=0.2. Then our extracted representation of the ideal/current relationship is uncertain. The probability is therefore attached to the extraction/determination, not necessarily to the underlying ideal state itself. That gives: I_t -> hat-I_t where hat-I_t is probabilistically estimated from available information.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explains the origin of graded 0-to-1 values: if the ideal state requires A,B,C,D but observations only partially resolve them (P(A)=1,P(B)=0.9,P(C)=0.6,P(D)=0.2), the extracted representation of the ideal/current relationship is uncertain -- this probability attaches to the extraction/determination I_t -> hat-I_t, not to the underlying ideal state itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Where does the Ideal State come from? ... A. Given by reality I_t=Reality_t B. Given by human knowledge I_t=HumanModel_t C. Given by rules/laws/principles I_t=NormativeModel_t D. Given by the domain model I_t=DomainModel_t E. An ideal mathematical state I_t=I* F. Some combination I_t=f(Reality,Rules,Principles,Domain,HumanKnowledge). We should not assume which one it is.
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses 'Where does the Ideal State come from?' as, in the author's opinion, the most important unresolved problem, with six unassumed candidate sources: given by reality (I_t=Reality_t), given by human knowledge (I_t=HumanModel_t), given by rules/laws/principles (I_t=NormativeModel_t), given by the domain model (I_t=DomainModel_t), an ideal mathematical state (I_t=I*), or some combination I_t=f(Reality,Rules,Principles,Domain,HumanKnowledge) -- explicitly: we should not assume which one it is.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge = identified elements/relationships of an ideal state. And the current Knowledge state is K_t while the ideal state is I_t. The goal of knowledge extraction could therefore be: K_t -> I_t or more realistically: K_t approx I_t with the difference I_t - K_t representing what remains unknown, uncertain, or unextracted.
a_rows_sample.statement: Resolves 'is Knowledge a collection of facts?' into a richer formulation: Knowledge = identified elements/relationships of an ideal state; with current knowledge state K_t and ideal state I_t, knowledge extraction aims at K_t -> I_t or more realistically K_t approx I_t, with the residual I_t - K_t representing what remains unknown, uncertain, or unextracted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: "Every information on the ideal state of anything is knowledge." I would change "every information" to "every correctly determined proposition about the ideal state". ... "I believe the ideal state contains X." That is information about someone's belief, not necessarily Knowledge about the ideal state. ... "The document says X." ... Information about an ideal state != Knowledge of the ideal state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Challenges the overbroad claim 'every information on the ideal state of anything is knowledge', proposing instead 'every correctly determined proposition about the ideal state'; example: 'I believe the ideal state contains X' is information about someone's belief, not Knowledge about the ideal state, and 'the document says X' is knowledge that the document says X, not knowledge that X is true. Preserves the distinction: Information about an ideal state != Knowledge of the ideal state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: IDEAL STATE -> (defines expected/relevant structure) -> OBSERVED REALITY -> INFORMATION -> EXTRACTION -> (evidence/uncertainty) -> COMPARISON (ideal <-> observed) -> LOGIC -> DETERMINATION -> FACTS -> KNOWLEDGE STATE -> update over time. ... Probability primarily helps with the extraction from imperfect information, while Logic helps determine consequences and relationships.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives the full revised pipeline diagram: IDEAL STATE (defines expected/relevant structure) -> OBSERVED REALITY -> INFORMATION -> EXTRACTION (branching into evidence and uncertainty) -> COMPARISON (ideal<->observed) -> LOGIC -> DETERMINATION -> FACTS -> KNOWLEDGE STATE -> update over time; probability primarily helps with extraction from imperfect information, logic helps determine consequences and relationships.

a_rows_sample.anchor: before determination, we now need to investigate: What is the Ideal State? Because determination is: D_t = Compare(Observed_t, Ideal_t) and if we don't understand Ideal_t, we don't fully understand D_t. ... IDEAL STATE -> OBSERVATION -> EXTRACTION -> COMPARISON -> DETERMINATION -> FACT -> KNOWLEDGE
a_rows_sample.statement: Revises the research direction: before determination can be understood, 'What is the Ideal State?' must be investigated, since determination is formalized as D_t=Compare(Observed_t,Ideal_t) and understanding D_t requires understanding Ideal_t; sets the research sequence as IDEAL STATE -> OBSERVATION -> EXTRACTION -> COMPARISON -> DETERMINATION -> FACT -> KNOWLEDGE, with Probability->uncertain extraction and Logic->comparison and consequence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the fundamental question for KnowledgeOS is not "How do we store Knowledge?" and not even "How do we extract Knowledge?" It may be: "How is an ideal state of Knowledge defined, and how does a system continuously determine its current relationship to that ideal state?" ... Knowledge becomes the currently justified representation of the relationship between them. I would now research Ideal State / normative state / complete state / target state / possible-world state / domain model / epistemic idealization across mathematics, epistemology, AI, systems theory, DDD, and philosophy before we touch the Kernel again.
a_rows_sample.statement: States what may be 'the biggest discovery so far': the fundamental KnowledgeOS question may be neither 'how do we store Knowledge' nor 'how do we extract Knowledge' but 'how is an ideal state of Knowledge defined, and how does a system continuously determine its current relationship to that ideal state?'; Knowledge becomes the currently justified representation of the relationship between Ideal State and Observed State. Proposes researching Ideal State / normative state / complete state / target state / possible-world state / domain model / epistemic idealization across mathematics, epistemology, AI, systems theory, DDD, and philosophy before returning to Kernel definition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: "Every information" you mean all possible information about the thing, not merely "some information." So your proposition is: I_t = the totality of all possible information about the object/domain at time t. And I_t may be infinite.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reinterprets 'every information' as meaning ALL possible information about a thing, not merely some information: I_t is redefined as the totality of all possible information about the object/domain at time t, and I_t may be infinite -- a much stronger interpretation than given previously.

a_rows_sample.anchor: O_t subset I_t or, more realistically, imperfect projections of I_t. The extraction process is therefore: I_t -> observable information -> extracted knowledge, with the extraction being imperfect because the underlying elements can overlap and the observation process cannot completely distinguish them.
a_rows_sample.statement: A human/system cannot access all of the (possibly infinite) I_t, only observations O_t subset I_t or imperfect projections of it; extraction is I_t -> observable information -> extracted knowledge, imperfect because underlying elements can overlap and observation cannot completely distinguish them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K = the space of all possible information/knowledge elements ... I_t subset K is the complete/ideal information state relevant at that time. Then an observer A has only an extracted state: K_t^A subset I_t ... K_t^A != I_t in general.
a_rows_sample.statement: Sharpens 'Knowledge is a state and subset of elements of the infinite Knowledge Space' into: K-script (the space of all possible information/knowledge elements), with I_t subset K-script being the complete/ideal information state relevant at time t; an observer A has only an extracted state K_t^A subset I_t (or a representation/projection of it), and because extraction is imperfect, K_t^A != I_t in general.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(x in I_t | O_{<=t}^A). So probability describes the extraction uncertainty. ... Knowledge itself is not probability. Rather: Probability can describe the imperfect extraction of Knowledge from the ideal information state.
a_rows_sample.statement: For an ideal-state element x in I_t that an observer cannot directly verify, the observer estimates P(x in I_t | O_{<=t}^A) given its observations -- probability describes extraction uncertainty, consistent with 'the elements overlap and only probability can extract them as separately as possible' (still to be tested as the right mathematical mechanism, but a coherent hypothesis). Knowledge itself is not probability; probability describes the imperfect extraction of Knowledge from the ideal information state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If I_t means all possible information, then we need to distinguish: possible information from true information and knowable information. ... whether your I_t means: 1. all logically possible information, or 2. all information that is actually true about the thing at t, or 3. all information that could in principle be known about the thing at t. I think this distinction is now the next critical question.
a_rows_sample.statement: Raises the next critical question: since not every possible description of a system is true, I_t must be disambiguated among three readings -- (1) all logically possible information, (2) all information that is actually true about the thing at t, or (3) all information that could in principle be known about the thing at t; this distinction will determine the meaning of the 'infinite Knowledge Space' and what KnowledgeOS is trying to extract from it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I_t = the potentially infinite space of all relevant states/propositions/relationships at time t ... K_t (script) = Infinite Knowledge Space at t and I_t subset K_t (script) could represent an ideal state/configuration of the domain. But even I_t may itself be infinite. ... K_t = Pi_t(I_t) where Pi_t is the extraction/projection available to the observer.
a_rows_sample.statement: If I_t can be infinite, it should not be modeled as a finite list of facts but as the potentially infinite space of all relevant states/propositions/relationships at t; introduces K-script_t (infinite Knowledge Space at t) with I_t subset K-script_t as an ideal state/configuration of the domain (itself possibly infinite), and the observer's actual accessible/extracted knowledge as K_t subset I_t or, more generally, K_t=Pi_t(I_t) where Pi_t is the observer's extraction/projection function.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I_t={x_1,x_2,x_3,...}. We cannot observe all of them. ... construct an estimate hat-I_t from the observations. For an element x: P(x in I_t | O_{<=t},C_t) can express our uncertainty ... probability is increasingly looking like a mathematics of extraction from an incompletely observable/infinite state, rather than a definition of Knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: With an infinite ideal state I_t={x_1,x_2,...} that cannot be fully observed, an estimate hat-I_t is constructed from observations O_{<=t}, and for an element x, P(x in I_t | O_{<=t},C_t) expresses uncertainty about membership; probability is increasingly a mathematics of extraction from an incompletely observable/infinite state, not a definition of Knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Theory is the formal theory ... to answer: How can a system represent, transform, evaluate, preserve, revise, and act upon knowledge without confusing reality, information, evidence, truth, determination, decision, and action? It is not yet a finished universal 'Knowledge Algebra.' The strongest current form is a theory of epistemic state, representation, evidence, inquiry, propositions, and transformations, with some parts still explicitly research-stage.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the central question KnowledgeOS Theory answers and its current honest scope: a theory of epistemic state/representation/evidence/inquiry/propositions/transformations, explicitly not yet a finished universal Knowledge Algebra.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reality -> Observation -> Information -> Representation -> Proposition -> Evidence -> Warrant/Reasoning -> KnowledgeState -> Determination -> Decision -> Authorization -> Action -> Outcome -> NewEvidence. Evidence is not Truth. Observation is not Evidence. Representation is not Ontology. Determination is not Truth unless a soundness bridge has been established. Decision is not Determination. Decision is not Action. Unknown is not False. Correlation is not Causation. A graph is not automatically a Knowledge State. A path is not automatically an inference. Hash equality is not semantic identity. These distinctions prevent the system from making epistemic category errors.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the fourteen-stage conceptual chain from Reality to NewEvidence and eleven protective non-identities (Evidence!=Truth, Observation!=Evidence, Representation!=Ontology, Determination!=Truth without a soundness bridge, Decision!=Determination, Decision!=Action, Unknown!=False, Correlation!=Causation, graph!=KnowledgeState, path!=inference, hash-equality!=semantic-identity), framed as preventing epistemic category errors.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t = (Content,Support,Uncertainty,Model,Alternatives,History,Identity,Context,Inquiry,Status), but this is currently treated as a semantic decomposition, not necessarily a mandatory implementation tuple. Knowledge State != Representation. Different representations may potentially represent the same semantic state. But the theory is deliberately cautious: semantic equivalence of arbitrary representations has not been universally established.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the K_t semantic decomposition (explicitly non-mandatory) and the Knowledge State != Representation principle, cautioning that semantic equivalence of arbitrary representations is not universally established -- directly consistent with this same batch's F4 audit findings on equiv_sem.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [[s]]_Gamma = p where s is a representation/sentence and p is the proposition interpreted under context Gamma. Truth(p,w,Gamma,t) in {0,1}. This allows the theory to distinguish assertion != determination != truth.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the proposition-interpretation formalization [[s]]_Gamma=p and truth evaluation Truth(p,w,Gamma,t), supporting the three-way distinction assertion != determination != truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ev(e,p,Gamma,t) meaning that evidence e bears upon proposition p under context Gamma at time t. Evidence != Truth and Evidence != Knowledge. two pieces of evidence != two independent pieces of evidence. Two documents may simply copy the same original source. path != independent evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates evidence as a relational predicate Ev(e,p,Gamma,t) rather than a property of an object, deriving Evidence!=Truth, Evidence!=Knowledge, and the independence warning that multiple evidence items copying the same source do not constitute independent corroboration, nor does a mere graph path constitute independent evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: q=<X,Y,Gamma,tau,Pi,Lambda> and more fundamentally an inquiry can be understood as an answer-producing function q:W->Y. This leads to the concept of inquiry-relative adequacy. A representation does not have to preserve everything. It has to preserve what is necessary to answer the inquiry correctly.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the inquiry formalization as a six-tuple and as an answer-producing function q:W->Y, grounding the concept of inquiry-relative adequacy (a representation need only preserve what answers the inquiry correctly, not everything).

b_rows_sample.anchor: T:X->X' transforms a representation. Q=g o T where Q is the inquiry-relevant observable. The preservation condition can be expressed as Pi o T = Pi o T o E_S for an appropriate elimination/reduction structure. This provides the foundation for reasoning about reduction, elimination, equivalence, sufficient representations, preservation, semantic invariants, and Zero.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the transformation and preservation formalization (T:X->X', Q=g∘T, the preservation condition Pi∘T=Pi∘T∘E_S), naming it the foundation for the whole reduction/elimination/equivalence/Zero research family already covered extensively in this batch's kr-rep-reduction-related documents.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero is not simply the number 0. A Knowledge Gap can be represented as a set of unsatisfied requirements: Delta_t = {r in R_t: not Sat(K_t,r)}. Then Delta_t=empty means that there is no remaining requirement gap under the relevant satisfaction semantics. Zero equiv empty gap rather than merely numerical zero. This connects your algebraic work with the epistemic theory.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates Zero as structurally equivalent to an empty requirement gap (Delta_t=empty) rather than numerical zero, explicitly connecting the algebraic Zero research line to the epistemic Delta_t/Sat theory just extensively audited in this same batch.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_{t+1} = T(K_t,E_{t+1},Q_t,C_t,EC_t,A_t). H_{t+1}=H_t union {transition_t}. current candidate operation nucleus includes ASSERT, LINK, REVISE, RETRACT, ISOLATE. But importantly, these are not all canonically frozen as the final minimal operation set. Operation minimality remains an open research problem.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the state-evolution transition formula and history-append formula, listing a five-operation candidate nucleus (ASSERT/LINK/REVISE/RETRACT/ISOLATE) while explicitly flagging operation minimality as an open research problem, not a frozen final set.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS does not adopt the simplistic rule P, not-P => everything. Instead, contradiction is represented and isolated. real knowledge systems routinely contain conflicting observations, competing hypotheses, outdated information, incompatible sources, different contextual truths. So contradiction is an epistemic state to manage, not a reason to destroy the entire knowledge state.
b_rows_sample.statement: States KnowledgeOS's explicit rejection of classical explosion (P, not-P => everything) in favor of representing and isolating contradiction as a manageable epistemic state, motivated by five named real-world sources of conflicting information.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Status table (15 rows): K_t as epistemic state RESOLVED/RATIFIED; Reality!=knowledge state ESTABLISHED; Evidence!=truth ESTABLISHED; Truth!=determination!=decision ADOPTED/FOUNDATIONAL; Contradiction/non-explosion RESOLVED/ADOPTED; Representation theory SUBSTANTIALLY DEVELOPED; Inquiry semantics DEVELOPED; Proposition semantics DEVELOPED; Evidence semantics DEVELOPED; Transformation theory SUBSTANTIALLY DEVELOPED; Universal Knowledge Algebra NOT ESTABLISHED; Canonical minimal operations OPEN RESEARCH; Complete F4 Sat(K_t,r) semantics NOT ESTABLISHED; Universal semantic equivalence r1 equiv_sem r2 NOT ESTABLISHED; F3<->F4 semantic bridge OPEN.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives a comprehensive fifteen-item status table for the whole theory, distinguishing resolved/established/adopted foundations from explicitly open items (universal Knowledge Algebra, canonical minimal operations, complete F4 Sat semantics, universal equiv_sem, F3<->F4 bridge), the last three matching exactly the open items just extensively audited in this same batch's F4/Model-B series.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The existence and role of Sat are present in the historical corpus, but a fully operational, corpus-native definition of Sat(K_t,r) has not yet been recovered. The later Sat* construction is therefore a candidate construction, not proof that the corpus already contained that exact semantics.
b_rows_sample.statement: Directly cross-references and restates the same-day F4/Model-B audit series' central finding (S2888-S2897): Sat's existence/role are corpus-present but its full operational semantics are not recovered, and Sat* remains a candidate construction rather than recovered corpus semantics.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not design what the corpus has not established. Where the corpus is insufficient, the correct result is NOT ESTABLISHED / RESEARCH REQUIRED, not an invented definition.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the closing methodological rule underlying the whole KnowledgeOS research programme: never design what the corpus has not established; an insufficient corpus should yield the honest classification NOT ESTABLISHED/RESEARCH REQUIRED rather than an invented definition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Delta_t = {r in R_t | Sat(K_t,r)=0}. Therefore Delta_t=empty is the KnowledgeOS notion of Zero Gap. Zero means that there are no unsatisfied requirements remaining within the defined requirement set and satisfaction semantics.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the core Zero-Gap definition as Delta_t=empty over the requirement set R_t and satisfaction predicate Sat(K_t,r), consistent with the F4/Model-B and kr-rep-reduction lines already covered in this batch.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 0 != empty in general. Numerical zero means a quantity has value zero. KnowledgeOS Zero is closer to: empty residual requirement set.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes numerical zero from KnowledgeOS Zero (an empty residual requirement set), a set-theoretic rather than quantitative notion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero is always relative to the defined requirement/inquiry scope. ... Zero Gap != Complete Knowledge. It means only: There is no remaining gap with respect to the requirements currently being evaluated.
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against conflating Zero Gap with Complete Knowledge or Complete Reality: satisfying all requirements in a scoped requirement set says nothing about knowledge outside that scope.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the same K_t can be Zero relative to R_t while simultaneously being Non-zero relative to a larger R'_t. This makes Zero inquiry- and contract-relative, rather than absolute.
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example showing the identical knowledge state K_t can simultaneously be Zero (empty gap) relative to a smaller requirement set and non-Zero relative to a larger superset, establishing Zero as inherently inquiry- and contract-relative rather than an absolute property of K_t.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If a transformation T removes irrelevant information while preserving everything needed to answer the inquiry, then the resulting representation may still have the same gap: Delta(T(K_t))=Delta(K_t). If the gap was already empty, then a valid inquiry-preserving transformation can maintain Delta(T(K_t))=empty. So Zero can function as a preserved semantic condition, not merely as a terminal numerical value.
b_rows_sample.statement: Connects Zero to the transformation/preservation theory: an inquiry-preserving transformation T maintains the gap Delta(T(K_t))=Delta(K_t), so an already-empty gap remains empty under valid transformations, framing Zero as a preserved semantic condition across the reduction/elimination research family.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero_{R,C}(K_t) iff Delta_{R,C}(K_t)=empty, where the subscript reminds us that Zero depends on the relevant requirements R and contract/context C. This is much stronger and safer than saying 'Zero means absence.' It means: There is no unresolved requirement in the specified epistemic task.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the strongest current formulation Zero_{R,C}(K_t) iff Delta_{R,C}(K_t)=empty, explicitly parameterized by requirements R and contract/context C, as a safer and stronger statement than an unparameterized 'Zero means absence.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: the full operational semantics of Sat(K_t,r) is not yet completely established, especially in the historical F4/Model-B work we just discussed. Therefore Delta_t=empty is theoretically meaningful, but we cannot yet claim that every real KnowledgeOS implementation can compute Zero correctly. Zero definition != Zero computation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Self-applies the same day's F4/Model-B audit finding (Sat(K_t,r)'s operational semantics not yet established) to the Zero-Gap concept itself, distinguishing Zero definition (theoretically meaningful) from Zero computation (not currently guaranteed correct in any real implementation).
