a_rows_sample.anchor: The platform cannot attest a specified session execution. identity binding must NOT be placed inside C-10's authoritative state, because C-10 cannot establish it. It is C-5-shaped
a_rows_sample.statement: The sharpest finding in the D3 prep: a C-10 receipt's binding to a specific session execution can never be stronger than what INV-ATTR-1/INV-ATTR-2 permit (self-declared, not attested), so identity binding cannot be placed inside C-10's authoritative state -- it is C-5-shaped, and C-5 owns no attestation record either.

a_rows_sample.anchor: M4 must be classified NOT ATTESTED -- never MISSING. ... Calling it MISSING asserts "no receipt", which the evidence does not support. Calling it present asserts a binding the platform cannot make.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extension of the NOT-ATTESTED-never-PASS discipline to condition classification: a receipt that exists but cannot be bound to its executing session (M4) must be classified NOT ATTESTED, since calling it MISSING or VALID would each assert something the platform cannot establish.

a_rows_sample.anchor: two residues no selection resolves ... knowledge versions K ... all three new propositions are silent on it ... S is unattestable. INV-ATTR-1 -- no gate reads identity ... E2 must mark the session-execution reference RECORDED, NOT ATTESTED.
a_rows_sample.statement: Two residues survive any D1 selection unresolved: whether 'knowledge versions K' remains a required receipt property (silently dropped by all three new propositions), and that the session-execution reference S must be marked RECORDED-NOT-ATTESTED per INV-ATTR-1/D4.3's M4 finding, both flagged for E2 (receipt completeness) to settle.

a_rows_sample.anchor: recording session identity != attesting session identity ... recording an applicability reference != attesting correctness of applicability
a_rows_sample.statement: D3 formalises two non-equivalences carrying the decision: recording session identity is not attesting session identity, and recording an applicability reference is not attesting the correctness of applicability -- the platform cannot attest 'a specified session execution' (INV-ATTR-1/2), so identity binding is placed outside C-10's boundary entirely.

a_rows_sample.anchor: One prohibition, three surfaces: an unresolved status may never be laundered into a resolved one.
a_rows_sample.statement: A single cross-cutting prohibition is observed recurring in three independent places in the estate's governance (independence classification, C-5 separation dimensions, D4.1 compensating controls, later a fourth at D4.3 M4): an unresolved epistemic status must never be laundered into a resolved one -- recorded as an observation bearing on, but distinct from, the canonical unifying-invariant candidate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: THE REVIEWER MUST BE A FRESH INDEPENDENT ARCHITECTURE PROCESS ... Satisfied on the measurement in §2.2: this is a process with no registered role in the chain.
a_rows_sample.statement: Demonstrates the independence-verification method in practice: enumerate every process occurrence across all transitions and grants in the aggregate plus a whole-repository grep, and treat zero occurrences as the only admissible basis for eligibility.

a_rows_sample.anchor: independence is not transferable: an assignment whose recorded evidence names a8ce5a39 cannot be discharged by 8a525719 without the record asserting something false about who did the work.
a_rows_sample.statement: Names a second-order independence failure distinct from personal ineligibility: a genuinely independent process cannot discharge a review under a workflow lane whose registered execution context names a different process, since INV-ATTR-1 means the engine itself would never detect the substitution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I will not adopt another process's identity in order to become operable.
a_rows_sample.statement: States a refusal principle: a process must not adopt a different, already-registered process's self-declared identity merely to satisfy a commission's addressee field and become operable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: you may self-bind identity; you may never self-choose role, scope, work item, or authority.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the governing invariant for the candidate-declaration mechanism: a process may discover and declare its own runtime identity, but may never self-select the role, scope, work item, or authority it is to hold -- those must come from the authoritative commission (AST-018 next-actor), with a MISMATCH between the prompt's claimed role and the commission's role forcing STOP (GO-08).

a_rows_sample.anchor: F-3 is disclosed as aggravating, not exculpatory: producing this record adds a further participating act by 77b85fa3 on this work item. If the PO/ARB's ruling turns on 'has this process already acted here,' this record is itself part of the evidence against it.
a_rows_sample.statement: A candidate for an independence-sensitive review role discloses that the very act of writing its own declaration record is itself a further participating act that could count against its own independence, explicitly refusing to treat its own record-production as exculpatory -- an instance of radical self-disclosure over self-serving interpretation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not decide for yourself that read-only orientation is or is not participation if the governing policy is ambiguous. Report the factual evidence. The candidate therefore returned UNDETERMINED and stopped, rather than self-certifying under reading B.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes a governance behavioral principle: when a governing policy is deliberately left as a placeholder and genuinely ambiguous, the correct response for a self-assessing process is to report factual evidence and return UNDETERMINED rather than adjudicate the ambiguity in its own favor, escalating the open question to the PO/ARB with named legitimate dispositions instead of a recommendation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: role != process identity, identity != eligibility, eligibility != appointment, appointment != activation, activation != authorization ... A process identity is DISCOVERED FROM THE RUNTIME -- never invented by the human, copied from another session, inferred from prompt text, or chosen from a human-entered UUID.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a six-link non-collapse chain of governance-identity concepts (role != process identity != eligibility != appointment != activation != authorization), each a genuinely separate step, and the rule that process identity is always discovered from the runtime, never supplied, copied, inferred, or human-chosen.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Basis: PROVENANCE ATTRIBUTION -- not self-declaration. The producer never declared this identity in any governed artifact. It is attributed here by a third party from runtime evidence. ... Every prior identity in this estate was declared by the process itself. This one is attributed by a third party from evidence the producer never confirmed. That is a new act type here.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces provenance-attributed identity as a genuinely new act type in this estate's governance model, distinct from the previously universal rule (INV-ATTR-1/2, G-2) that process identity is always self-declared and never attestable by others: here Governance attributes a producer identity to a third-party process from transcript timestamp/content evidence the producer itself never confirmed, bounded explicitly as barring-only (never enabling), evidentially grounded in operator-side transcripts outside the governed repository store, and remaining falsifiable/supersedable if contradicting evidence appears.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A previous candidate on the parent work item read the material first and declared afterwards. Its own reading then became prior participation ... Do not repeat that. Establish your identity FIRST. Check the bars FIRST. Read ONLY the authoritative state ... Declare. Then STOP.
a_rows_sample.statement: Institutionalizes a corrective procedural step ('declare before you orient') directly caused by the S0375 episode where a candidate's own pre-declaration reading became disqualifying prior participation with no policy able to resolve it; the fix reorders the candidate protocol (identity first, bars first, then only the minimal authoritative state, then declare and stop) without deciding the underlying open independence-policy question, which remains open.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The appointment names a ROLE, not a process. It deliberately contains no session identifier, and none was invented. Appointee identity: NOT DECLARED -- it comes from the runtime of the fresh session the PO/ARB starts.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reconfirms, in a concrete appointment act, that a governed appointment names only a role and never invents or pre-selects a process identity -- the appointee's identity is discovered later from the runtime of whichever fresh session the human actually starts.

a_rows_sample.anchor: process context continuity != workflow session identity continuity ... A Claude restart can produce a different CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID while retaining essentially the same working conversation and context. ... This is the temporal extension of INV-ATTR-1/2, not a new subject.
a_rows_sample.statement: States observation O-5: process context continuity is not the same as workflow session identity continuity -- a Claude restart can yield a new CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID while the same working context persists, so process identity is not only self-declared and unattestable (INV-ATTR-1/2) but also temporally unstable across restarts, and this instability is itself a temporal extension of INV-ATTR-1/2 rather than a separate subject.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Direction A -- false independence (the dangerous one; the one that actually materialised). ... Nothing malicious is required. A restart is enough. ... Direction B -- lost continuity (the tolerable one). ... The rule below deliberately errs toward Direction B. A wrongly-barred process needs one governed act to be re-established. A wrongly-admitted one cannot be repaired at all.
a_rows_sample.statement: Analyzes the O-5 instability as producing two asymmetric failure directions: (A) false independence -- a restarted process presenting a clean UUID could be wrongly admitted as independent while carrying the complete prior context of the very work it should be excluded from, destroying the independence guarantee retrospectively with a record that looks clean; (B) lost continuity -- a legitimately continuing process cannot prove it is the registered lane holder and must be re-established, a merely tolerable cost. States the governing principle that any remedy must err toward B, since a wrongly-barred process is one governed act away from repair while a wrongly-admitted one can never be repaired because its check was never actually independent.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Independence must be declared and assessed on PRIOR PARTICIPATION, not on identity difference. A different UUID is necessary but not sufficient evidence of independence. ... A restarted process is a new candidate until Governance explicitly establishes its participation.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the corollary that carries the load: independence must be assessed on disclosed prior participation, never merely on identity difference, since a different UUID is necessary but not sufficient evidence of true independence; the resulting safe rule is that a restarted process is treated as a new candidate until Governance explicitly re-establishes its participation, explicitly rejecting as dangerous the alternative of treating UUIDs as durable, permanent identities.

a_rows_sample.anchor: That process authored ASD-001, scoped REPAIR-001, recorded the CONTINUATION (seq 5) and the grant G-REPAIR-001, and wrote the candidate-declaration prompt. Appointing it would collapse the separation between Governance analysis and Implementation ... The mechanism would not have caught this. AST-018 appoint might well have accepted e40f3fd0.
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms O-5's abstract danger with a concrete live instance: the governance-recording process that scoped and authorized REPAIR-001 reappeared under a new runtime identifier (e40f3fd0) after a restart, which appears on no identity bar list, so the mechanical appointment check (AST-018 appoint) would have accepted it as independent -- the bar had to be applied manually by the PO/ARB on participation grounds since the mechanism itself would not have caught it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This process added itself to the implementer bar the moment it recorded §2-§6. Governance-recording is not a lane, but it is participation.
a_rows_sample.statement: States that a process recording a governance decision, though holding no formal workflow lane, is itself a participation act that self-bars that process from later filling an independence-sensitive role on the same matter -- governance-recording capacity is explicitly not exempt from participation-based exclusion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: INV-ATTR-2/G-2: separation is Declared, NOT attestable. No mechanism can establish who performed an act; assurance rests entirely on where the human starts the session.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding F-4: role separation between producer, verifier, and approver is Declared, not attestable (INV-ATTR-2/G-2); no mechanism in the estate can establish who actually performed an act, so assurance rests entirely on where the human starts a session -- a capability described as C-5, separation attestation, with no owner today.

b_rows_sample.anchor: this is the first recorded instance of it failing in the FALSE-BAR direction. INV-ATTR-2 anticipated that a process could wrongly claim independence; this event shows the same mechanism can make a process wrongly claim to be barred
b_rows_sample.statement: INV-ATTR-2 ('separation is declared, not attestable') is extended by observed evidence to a second failure direction: not only can a process wrongly claim independence (the failure the invariant was framed against), but the same unverified-self-declaration property can make a process wrongly claim to BE barred, harming an assignment rather than assurance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The platform cannot attest a specified session execution. identity binding must NOT be placed inside C-10's authoritative state, because C-10 cannot establish it. It is C-5-shaped
b_rows_sample.statement: The sharpest finding in the D3 prep: a C-10 receipt's binding to a specific session execution can never be stronger than what INV-ATTR-1/INV-ATTR-2 permit (self-declared, not attested), so identity binding cannot be placed inside C-10's authoritative state -- it is C-5-shaped, and C-5 owns no attestation record either.

b_rows_sample.anchor: One prohibition, three surfaces: an unresolved status may never be laundered into a resolved one.
b_rows_sample.statement: A single cross-cutting prohibition is observed recurring in three independent places in the estate's governance (independence classification, C-5 separation dimensions, D4.1 compensating controls, later a fourth at D4.3 M4): an unresolved epistemic status must never be laundered into a resolved one -- recorded as an observation bearing on, but distinct from, the canonical unifying-invariant candidate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This process is not a neutral party to this question... It has an interest in concluding that that record is worth preserving.
b_rows_sample.statement: Full process-disclosure practice: a producing process discloses its own prior participation and interest in the outcome (having authored the canonical analysis, D5, and prior governance registrations) and binds itself out of later verifying or accepting its own work (R-34/P-2).

b_rows_sample.anchor: This process is not a neutral party to this question, and the reason is specific... many of the 210 transitions and 99 grants whose durability is the subject of this ADR were recorded by this process.
b_rows_sample.statement: Full conflict-of-interest disclosure: the ADR's producer recorded many of the transitions whose durability is under analysis, has an interest in concluding the record is worth preserving, and binds itself out of approving, verifying, or accepting its own ADR.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the Governance actor was correct to refuse to decide. That refusal is actually evidence that the separation model is working.
b_rows_sample.statement: The PO/ARB's own observation, recorded as OBSERVED evidence: a producer bar held under direct pressure to breach it, twice, without an exception being requested, is evidence that the separation-of-authority model is functioning; the registering process explicitly draws no conclusion about C-5 (separation attestation) ownership from it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the S4b lane's registered executionContext names the producer as claude-code-session:5e1dd9ee. The plan 3817eb2b was produced by claude-code-session:1c8b041b.
b_rows_sample.statement: INFO-2: a provenance discrepancy exists in the governance record itself (not the plan) — the plan discloses its own producer correctly, but the lane's registered executionContext names a different process as producer; reconciling this is left as a Governance act.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-12's principle — author ≠ independent reviewer, not author ≠ every prior reviewer — would make it authoring-eligible again, and repeated authoring remains a QUALITY RISK rather than an independence failure.
b_rows_sample.statement: Clarifies an eligibility rule already precedented in the chain: the exclusion rule is 'author ≠ independent reviewer', not 'author ≠ every prior reviewer who ever touched this artifact' — a process that authored earlier amendments remains eligible to author a later, different correction, though the repetition itself is recorded as a quality risk rather than an independence failure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Independence — the seven criteria, all required ... distinct process/session identity ... is not a continuation/compaction/fork/resume lineage of a barred producer
b_rows_sample.statement: States a seven-criterion independence test (process identity, non-authorship of the artifact/prior corrections/prior verifications, non-lineage from a barred producer, non-inherited working context) with the rule that a different session ID alone is insufficient; if lineage cannot be established the classification must be NOT ATTESTED, never PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Independence is not one property ... Role independence ... Authority independence ... Access independence ... Organizational independence ... Financial independence ... Technical independence ... Temporal independence ... Cognitive independence
b_rows_sample.statement: Decomposes 'independence' into eight distinct dimensions and a six-level evidence-strength ladder (self-declaration through independent external assessment), concluding a platform can prove some dimensions (recorded identity difference, access-enforced separation) but not others (no collusion, no cognitive bias, organizational independence) from metadata alone.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A reviewer checking only the two names it was handed would have PASSED this gate and proceeded ... this is exactly why the same commission forbids hand-copied grant lists: the chat-supplied exclusion set was narrower than the governed one.
b_rows_sample.statement: Demonstrates the failure mode of trusting a prompt-supplied exclusion list rather than the governed record: the chat-supplied set of two barred names missed a fourth clause that fires on a registered grant covering the same performer under a different role in this same chain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: a REGISTERED act that is not live is a FALSE RECORD — and here it would falsely assert that an independent reviewer is at work on the gate that exists to guarantee independence.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the converse of the estate's 'a live but unregistered act still counts as missing' rule: a registered-but-not-live START is a false record, which is the worse failure direction on the one gate whose purpose is guaranteeing independence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'Fresh' is satisfied in the sense the record can test — no prior participation. It cannot mean 'no knowledge of the estate': this session read MEMORY.md and CONTEXT.md at startup via the repository's SessionStart hook, which is disclosed here rather than left to be discovered.
b_rows_sample.statement: Narrows what 'fresh' can mean under the record's own tests: no prior participation is provable; absence of any estate knowledge is not, and unavoidable bootstrap reading is disclosed rather than concealed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: independence is not transferable: an assignment whose recorded evidence names a8ce5a39 cannot be discharged by 8a525719 without the record asserting something false about who did the work.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names a second-order independence failure distinct from personal ineligibility: a genuinely independent process cannot discharge a review under a workflow lane whose registered execution context names a different process, since INV-ATTR-1 means the engine itself would never detect the substitution.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I will not adopt another process's identity in order to become operable.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a refusal principle: a process must not adopt a different, already-registered process's self-declared identity merely to satisfy a commission's addressee field and become operable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: a live but unregistered act still counts as missing ... a REGISTERED act that is not live is a FALSE RECORD.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the estate's two-directional recording rule as the reason a chat-delivered commission cannot substitute for a recorded START transition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'It is CODE provenance, never AI-process attestation: nothing here asserts who produced the artifact (EKS-07 stays unsolved; self-declared process identity is not independently attested authorship).' — scripts/lib/EngineeringKnowledge/Shared/Domain/HandoffContext.php:11–15
b_rows_sample.statement: AI processes are first-class actors (they invoke CLIs, author artifacts, and record transitions -- e.g. recordedBy:architecture on 2 HANDOFF transitions), but their identity cannot be established by any mechanism: tier-1 source states verbatim that this is code provenance, never AI-process attestation (EKS-07 unsolved); self-declared process identity, as practiced (e.g. a document declaring its producer as claude-code-session:5e1dd9ee), is explicitly marked 'self-declared and NOT attestable.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: What EKS does not do with AI processes ... No process identity ... No cross-process notification ... No agent registry ... No capability restriction. Every hook is advisory; nothing an AI process can do is prevented by EKS.
b_rows_sample.statement: EKS explicitly does not: issue/record/verify any AI-process identifier (self-declaration is the practice); notify concurrent processes of each other's actions (discovery is only by re-reading files, EKS-07); register any AI process in registry.yaml; or restrict any AI-process capability (every hook is advisory; nothing an AI process can do is prevented by EKS).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Exactly one mutation owner per work item is a mechanically enforced invariant (I-1)
b_rows_sample.statement: Grants: a grant without a humanActRef is refused by the engine ('the record never manufactures authority -- G-2/R5b'). Exactly one mutation owner per work item is mechanically enforced (I-1). Closure is a governance act (G-1): COMPLETE refuses any writer but governance/human. Producer != acceptor (R-34, INV-ATTR-2): a process cannot verify/accept its own work; separation is declared, not attestable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_min = {HoldState, TransitionLegally, RejectIllegally, Replay} ... Adeq_K(O) iff K_min subseteq Cap(O) ... O_1 != O_2 does not imply Cap(O_1) != Cap(O_2). ... O_core = canonical semantic operation CLASSES, a concrete vocabulary is a REPRESENTATION of them.
a_rows_sample.statement: Section 3: proposes formal apparatus K_min={HoldState,TransitionLegally,RejectIllegally,Replay}, Adeq_K(O) iff K_min⊆Cap(O), Necessary(o,K_min) iff ¬Adeq_K(O\{o}), and the minimal-adequate-set family M_K; a 6-way classification (Necessary/Derivable/Equivalent/Optional/Contextual/Undetermined) each candidate operation must receive; and the type correction O1≠O2 does not imply Cap(O1)≠Cap(O2), so O_core should denote canonical semantic operation CLASSES, with a concrete vocabulary merely one representation of them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: O_core = {ASSERT, LINK, REVISE, RETRACT, ISOLATE} appears in ... both are REVIEW/ASSESSMENT documents. A ratification assessment is not a ratification ... The five-element set is a candidate basis ... superset, never =.
a_rows_sample.statement: Section 4 continued: a candidate 5-element operation nucleus O_core={ASSERT,LINK,REVISE,RETRACT,ISOLATE} exists in the corpus but only within review/assessment documents (not ratification), recorded elsewhere as NOT RATIFIED; the document recommends treating it as a candidate basis using superset-not-equals notation until every additional candidate is tested against K_min; per-capability necessity questions are posed for each of the five (can new epistemic state be introduced? can standing change while history is preserved? can standing be withdrawn without destroying traceability? can contradictory branches be preserved without global explosion? can dependency/provenance/justification structure be represented?), noting ISOLATE's question is already partly constrained by the adopted non-explosion/contradiction-containment invariants.

b_rows_sample.anchor: O_core = {ASSERT, LINK, REVISE, RETRACT, ISOLATE} ... Kernel vs. Peripheral Operations: Read-only observations, administrative governance, and diagnostic explanations do not mutate representation states. They are moved to the KnowledgeOS SDK/API boundary layer. Reduced Core Set: exactly 5 primitive, state-transforming operations.
b_rows_sample.statement: Prunes the candidate operation list to exactly five state-transforming primitives (ASSERT, LINK, REVISE, RETRACT, ISOLATE), explicitly relocating read-only observation (Query, Trace, diagnostic Explain), assurance (Validate, Compare), and governance (Authorize) operations out of the state-transition kernel into a separate SDK/API boundary layer -- resolving the operation-reduction question raised repeatedly earlier in this batch.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ASSERT(p,v,src) appends new ground node with initial standing and source provenance ... LINK(n1,n2,rel) appends directed relational edge ... REVISE(p,p',reason) appends p', adds supersedes link p'->p, leaving p immutable ... RETRACT(p,scope) appends retraction tombstone node linked to p; adjusts active standing ... ISOLATE(p,boundary) constructs Epistemic Firewall F(p) blocking graph propagation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives each of the five O_core primitives a formal signature and state-transformation effect: ASSERT appends a new ground node with initial standing/provenance; LINK appends a directed relational edge; REVISE appends a new claim with a SUPERSEDES link to the old claim, which remains immutable; RETRACT appends a tombstone node and adjusts active standing rather than deleting; ISOLATE constructs an Epistemic Firewall blocking graph propagation for a proposition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Transition Axioms: 1. Strict Monotonicity of Historical Nodes: forall op, Nodes(K_t) subseteq Nodes(delta(K_t,op,Gamma).K_{t+1}) 2. Deterministic Delta Output: delta(K_t,op,Gamma)=delta(K_t,op,Gamma) 3. Frame-Qualified Composition: Context Gamma parameters govern whether Delta K applies globally or is partitioned into a frame sub-graph K|_Gamma.
b_rows_sample.statement: States three transition axioms required of every delta implementation over the reduced O_core: Strict Monotonicity of Historical Nodes (no operation shrinks the node/edge set), Deterministic Delta Output, and Frame-Qualified Composition (context Gamma parameters, such as temporal boundaries or authority levels, determine whether a state delta applies globally or only within a frame sub-graph K restricted to Gamma).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Final Kernel Reduction Matrix: With the execution of Closure Packages C1 through C4, the KnowledgeOS Kernel reduction is complete ... C1 Truth & Evidence Space ... C2 Contradiction & Scope ... C3 Operations Algebra ... C4 Equivalence & Adequacy ... PACKAGE C4 FALSIFICATION TEST: PASSED (EA and Equivalence verified)
b_rows_sample.statement: Issues the file's culminating claim: 'With the execution of Closure Packages C1 through C4, the KnowledgeOS Kernel reduction is complete', supported by a final matrix summarizing each package's formal result and a Python test (test_c4_adequacy_and_equivalence) reported PASSED for both Executable Adequacy and Semantic Equivalence on a small synthetic three-operation example; status self-declared [RATIFIED -- FINAL CLOSURE PACKAGE] for C4 specifically, versus [RATIFICATION CANDIDATE] for C2 and C3 in the same file.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Package C3 -- Operations + delta + Composition: Frame composition parameterized: Composition is context-dependent ... Key Achievement: The kernel now has exactly 5 primitives with monotonic transitions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates Package C3's achievement (5-primitive O_core, monotonic delta) but labels 'Frame composition parameterized: Composition is context-dependent' with a check-mark as an achieved/closed item in this file's Part-1 table, even though the source Package C3 spec explicitly left the composition RULE selection open/parameterized rather than resolved -- the parameterization itself (not a selected rule) is what was achieved, a distinction this summary's checkmark formatting elides.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ASSERT ... risks confusing entity/proposition identity with assertion identity ... REVISE ... What exactly is being revised? proposition? assertion? evidence? interpretation? relation? evaluation? determination? These have different identities. A generic REVISE(p,...) is therefore probably too coarse ... RETRACT ... we still need to distinguish Retracted != Superseded != Invalidated != Expired != Withdrawn ... ISOLATE ... Still depends upon Scope(Contr(p),Gamma) and Contr and Scope are not fully determined. Therefore ISOLATE cannot be considered fully closed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies an unresolved identity question for four of the five O_core primitives: ASSERT risks conflating entity/proposition identity with assertion identity when a new independent assertion arrives about an already-existing proposition; REVISE is ambiguous about which of seven candidate objects (proposition, assertion, evidence, interpretation, relation, evaluation, determination) is actually being revised, making a single generic REVISE(p,...) too coarse; RETRACT needs to distinguish five different terminal states (Retracted, Superseded, Invalidated, Expired, Withdrawn) it currently conflates; ISOLATE cannot be closed while Contr and Scope remain undetermined.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The 'monotonic delta' claim is mathematically misleading ... Nodes(K_t) subseteq Nodes(K_{t+1}) ... is not the same thing as monotonic knowledge. You have established at most: structural history monotonicity or append-preserving identity. It does not imply K_t <= K_{t+1} epistemically ... I recommend renaming Monotonic delta to History-Preserving delta or Append-Preserving State Transition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a terminology overclaim: the node-set-inclusion property (Nodes(K_t) subseteq Nodes(K_{t+1})) is structural/append-preserving history monotonicity, not epistemic monotonicity (K_t <= K_{t+1} in a knowledge-ordering sense) -- a retraction, isolation, or revision can each reduce admissibility or invalidate a conclusion even while node-set inclusion holds. Recommends renaming 'Monotonic delta' to 'History-Preserving delta' or 'Append-Preserving State Transition' to state precisely what has actually been demonstrated.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 4.1 Aggregate Boundaries: KnowledgeCore (Aggregate Root) -- Nodes (Entities), Edges (Value Objects), Firewalls (Value Objects), Audit Log (Events). 4.2 Commands: type Command = ASSERT | LINK | REVISE | RETRACT | ISOLATE, each with typed fields. 4.3 Events: type DomainEvent = {type, nodeId, timestamp, stateHash, prevStateHash}. 4.4 Queries: type Query = QUERY | TRACE | EXPLAIN, explicitly separate from Command.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a concrete DDD implementation sketch not seen elsewhere in this batch: KnowledgeCore as an Aggregate Root containing Nodes (Entities), Edges (Value Objects), Firewalls (Value Objects), and an Audit Log (Events); a TypeScript discriminated-union Command type covering exactly the five O_core primitives with typed fields; a DomainEvent type carrying command type, node id, timestamp, and pre/post state hashes; and a Query type (QUERY/TRACE/EXPLAIN) explicitly kept separate from the Command/kernel layer, operationalizing the earlier decision to move read/observation operations out of the state-transition kernel.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Invariant 2.1.1 (Structural History Preservation): For all states K_t=<V_t,E_t,F_t,H_t> and operations o in O_core, the structural node set V and history ledger H are strictly monotonic: V(K_t) subseteq V(delta(K_t,o,Gamma)) and H(K_t) subseteq H(delta(K_t,o,Gamma)). Note: Epistemic standing S(p) is NOT monotonic under retraction or revision. Only physical history H and node presence V are monotonic.
b_rows_sample.statement: Implements the demanded 'Monotonic delta' correction precisely: splits the invariant into V(K_t) subseteq V(K_{t+1}) (structural node monotonicity) and H(K_t) subseteq H(K_{t+1}) (history-ledger monotonicity), explicitly stating epistemic standing S(p) is NOT monotonic under RETRACT or REVISE -- only physical history and node presence are monotonic, precisely the distinction the earlier reviews demanded.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Contract 1: ASSERT ... Preconditions: p not-in V(K_t) OR p in V(K_t) with status RETRACTED. Postconditions: p in V(K_{t+1}) ACTIVE ... Failure Semantics: If p in V(K_t) and status is ACTIVE, returns NO_OP_DUPLICATE. Contract 2: LINK ... Failure Semantics: raises UNMAPPED_NODE_EXCEPTION; transition aborts with K_{t+1}=K_t. Contract 3: REVISE ... Failure Semantics: If p is RETRACTED, raises REVISION_ON_RETRACTED_NODE_ERROR. Contract 4: RETRACT ... S(p) standing mass becomes <0,0,1.0> ... Failure Semantics: If p not-in V(K_t), returns NO_OP_NOT_FOUND. Contract 5: ISOLATE ... Failure Semantics: If scope is empty, defaults to local node isolation scope={p}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives each of the five O_core primitives a complete precondition/postcondition/failure-semantics contract with named failure outcomes not present in earlier versions: ASSERT returns NO_OP_DUPLICATE on a redundant active node; LINK raises UNMAPPED_NODE_EXCEPTION (aborting with no state change) if either endpoint is missing; REVISE raises REVISION_ON_RETRACTED_NODE_ERROR if the target is already retracted; RETRACT sets standing to fully-ambiguous <0,0,1.0> and returns NO_OP_NOT_FOUND if the target does not exist; ISOLATE defaults to single-node scope if no explicit scope is given.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Since then the C1-C4 assessment asserts, from a [FINAL ADVISORY], 'O_core reduced to 5 primitives: ASSERT, LINK, REVISE, RETRACT, ISOLATE' -- a set matching none of the prior enumerations. It adds a member to the incompatible family rather than closing it: the recorded 19->17->6 contraction now has a 5 beside it, against 48 enumerations whose intersection is empty.
b_rows_sample.statement: Delivers this batch's single most consequential external correction: the C1-C4 assessment's self-declared O_core reduction to five primitives {ASSERT,LINK,REVISE,RETRACT,ISOLATE} matches NONE of the corpus's prior operator-count enumerations; rather than resolving the corpus's recorded operator-count contraction sequence (19 -> 17 -> 6), this batch's five-operator set is a 49th mutually incompatible enumeration added to a family of 48 whose collective intersection is empty -- meaning the batch's self-declared O_core closure did not converge the corpus's actual operator-registry debate, it extended its divergence.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
$$
\boxed{
Semantic\ Carrier
\rightarrow
Required\ Observables
\rightarrow
Semantic\ Equivalence
\rightarrow
Invariant\ Preservation

\rightarrow

a_rows_sample.statement: Requires R1≡_sem R2 to be established before comparing Complexity(R1)<Complexity(R2), otherwise different semantic objects are being compared; proposes the proper sequence Semantic Carrier -> Required Observables -> Semantic Equivalence -> Invariant Preservation -> Representation Reduction -> Minimality as more mathematically defensible than raw operator-cardinality comparisons ('13 operators > 12 operators').

a_rows_sample.anchor:
$$
Custody(I)=\{c\mid c\text{ is responsible for preserving invariant }I\}.
$$ A reduction is valid only if: $$
\forall I\in I_{required},
\quad
Custody_{before}(I)\neq\varnothing
\Rightarrow
Custody_{after}(I)\neq\varnothing.
$$
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes invariant custody as a reduction-validity criterion: Custody(I)={c | c is responsible for preserving invariant I}; a kernel reduction is valid only if, for every required invariant I, a non-empty custody before reduction implies a non-empty custody after -- proposed as a much better kernel-reduction criterion than counting operators.

a_rows_sample.anchor:

a_rows_sample.statement: A three-status admission ladder governed by an explicit policy: Candidate -> Supported -> Accepted. a_rows_sample.anchor: The boundary
a_rows_sample.statement: Committed is not a fourth epistemic status; it is a decision-boundary status attached to an Accepted item by authority, under the model's sharpest rule A6: authority determines commitment, not evidential truth. Evidence can make a claim Accepted; only an authorized act can make anyone bound to it. The falsification pass caught the earlier formulation quietly treating Committed as a rung of the same ladder; the ratified repair re-typed it, and the lived governance record enacts exactly this discipline (adoption and authorization as separate human acts).

a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a five-layer model: World state W (what exists) -> Observation O (interaction producing an observable result) -> Representation R (encoded artifact: text/JSON/db row/image/log/document/API response) -> Assertion A (proposition extracted/constructed from R) -> Knowledge object K (governed epistemic object containing A plus epistemic context).

a_rows_sample.anchor: O=Transform... Evidence is an epistemically usable representation of an observation: E=Transform(O). Observation\rightarrow Evidence but Observation\neq Evidence
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects earlier shorthand: Observation is an event O=(actor,time,method,target,result); Evidence E=Transform(O) is a representation of it. Observation -> Evidence but Observation ≠ Evidence, resolving 'what is observation?' as 'a bounded interaction/event producing an observable result,' not 'everything.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: O=(Subject,Target,Method,Time,Environment,RawResult,Actor) ... Observation has event identity
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines formal Observation as a 7-tuple (Subject,Target,Method,Time,Environment,RawResult,Actor), worked example O1=(Admin,Nexus,HTTP/API,2026-08-27T10:00,Production,3.69.0,Admin), noting the structure is domain-adaptable but 'Observation has event identity.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: h_1=Hash(R_1) ... Identity(R_1)=h_1 ... R_1\equiv R_2 under byte-level identity ... does not mean they are the same observation
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Representation identity via hashing: Identity(R)=Hash(R) gives deterministic byte-level artifact identity, but byte-identical representations (R1≡R2) do not imply the same observation.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
Same script at t_1 and t_2 ... R_1=R_2 but O_1
eq O_2 because Time(O_1)
eq Time(O_2) ... RepresentationIdentity
eq ObservationIdentity
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: identical textual output from the same script at two different times has R1=R2 but O1≠O2 (different Time), giving RepresentationIdentity ≠ ObservationIdentity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: O_1 produces text and a human records a paraphrase ... R_1\neq R_2 while SourceOf(R_1)=SourceOf(R_2)=O_1
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: a machine-produced representation and a human paraphrase of the same observation are different representations (R1≠R2) sharing the same source observation O1.

a_rows_sample.anchor: E_1 from database, E_2 from administrator both support A ... A(E_1)=A(E_2) but E_1\neq E_2 ... EvidenceIdentity\neq AssertionIdentity
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: two distinct evidence items (database record, administrator statement) supporting the same assertion have A(E1)=A(E2) but E1≠E2, giving EvidenceIdentity ≠ AssertionIdentity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A=(Subject,Predicate,Object,Context) ... A_1=(Nexus,HasVersion,3.69.0,Production) ... may normalize to the same assertion
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a canonical assertion structure A=(Subject,Predicate,Object,Context), showing multiple natural-language phrasings ('Nexus version is 3.69', 'Nexus runs version 3.69.0', 'Installed Nexus = 3.69.0') can normalize to the same canonical assertion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SemanticEquivalent(A_1,A_2,C,t) is context-dependent ... LLM-equivalence must not automatically become DeterministicIdentity
a_rows_sample.statement: 'The Nexus server is current' vs 'Nexus 3.69.0 is installed' are not necessarily equivalent since 'current' depends on a reference time and authoritative version source; SemanticEquivalent(A1,A2,C,t) is context-dependent, and LLM-proposed equivalence must not automatically become deterministic identity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Exact identity x\equiv_{exact}y ... Structural identity x\equiv_{struct}y ... Semantic equivalence x\equiv_{sem,C}y ... not interchangeable
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines three non-interchangeable identity relations: exact identity (same canonical bytes/identifier), structural identity (same normalized structure), semantic equivalence (same meaning under context C).

a_rows_sample.anchor: KID=CanonicalAssertion+Context+EpistemicState+Validity
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: K1 (assertion A, observed 2025) and K2 (same A, observed 2026) have identical propositions but distinct knowledge objects, motivating a first knowledge-identity proposal KID = CanonicalAssertion + Context + EpistemicState + Validity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AssertionIdentity separate from KnowledgeObjectIdentity ... identity of an Entity is not the same as equality of its attributes
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues two knowledge objects with the same assertion but different provenance are different knowledge records referring to the same proposition, requiring AssertionIdentity separate from KnowledgeObjectIdentity — explicitly analogized to the DDD principle that entity identity differs from attribute equality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeEntity has stable identity ... Assertion (Value Object) ... ObservationEvent (Domain Event) ... KnowledgeAggregate ... a strong DDD fit
a_rows_sample.statement: Maps the model onto DDD building blocks: Knowledge Object as Entity (KnowledgeEntity, stable identity), normalized proposition as Value Object (Assertion, compared by value), Observation as Domain Event (ObservationEvent), and a potential Aggregate (KnowledgeAggregate) managing consistency of related epistemic state — 'a strong DDD fit.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeAtma(K)=Identity(K) ... I would not yet accept this as the final definition
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes an initial Knowledge Atma formalization as 'the stable identity of a knowledge entity independent of its representations,' KnowledgeAtma(K)=Identity(K), but explicitly declines to accept it as final since 'stable identity' is ambiguous.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate A: Atma(K)=Identity(A) ... A-identity alone is insufficient
a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate definition A (Atma(K)=Identity(assertion)) is rejected: two knowledge records with the same proposition but different evidence would become identical, losing epistemic distinction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate B: Atma(K)=Identity(E) ... E-identity alone is insufficient
a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate definition B (Atma(K)=Identity(evidence)) is rejected: two independent evidence items for the same knowledge would become different Atmas, useful for evidence but not for knowledge identity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate C: K=(A,C,V,P,S) ... much closer ... but provenance may change without changing the underlying knowledge proposition
a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate definition C: K=(Assertion,Context,Validity,Provenance,Status) is 'much closer' but still conflates identity with mutable provenance, motivating a further split into CoreKnowledgeIdentity vs KnowledgeRecordIdentity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeMeaningIdentity and KnowledgeRecordIdentity ... this solves many problems
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends a two-level identity model: Meaning identity (what proposition/context does this knowledge represent?) and Record identity (which concrete epistemic record/version is this?).

a_rows_sample.anchor: E_1 and E_2 both support A ... MeaningIdentity(K_1)=MeaningIdentity(K_2) but RecordIdentity(K_1)\neq RecordIdentity(K_2) ... exactly what we need for evidence aggregation
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: two independently-supported knowledge records of the same proposition share MeaningIdentity but differ in RecordIdentity — 'exactly what we need for evidence aggregation,' letting KnowledgeOS recognize 'two independently supported instances of the same proposition.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: A=(S,P,O,C,T) ... A_1=(Nexus,HasVersion,3.69.0,Production,t_1)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the canonical assertion representation A=(Subject,Predicate,Object/value,Context,TemporalQualification), worked example A1=(Nexus,HasVersion,3.69.0,Production,t1), called 'computationally manageable.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: ExactEqual(A_1,A_2)=True ... canonical serialization plus hash ... No AI is required
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines deterministic ExactEqual(A1,A2), implementable via canonical serialization plus hash, worked with an identical-tuple example requiring no AI.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Normalize(A_1)=Normalize(A_2) ... SemanticEquivalent(A_1,A_2)=True ... this normalization is where semantic technology enters
b_rows_sample.statement: Shows two differently-phrased natural-language sentences normalize to the same canonical assertion, defining SemanticEquivalent(A1,A2)=True via Normalize() — 'this normalization is where semantic technology enters.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: E_{exact}\Rightarrow E_{structural}\Rightarrow? E_{semantic} ... not necessarily the reverse
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a three-level equivalence hierarchy E_exact => E_structural =>? E_semantic (implication not guaranteed reversible) — 'semantic equivalence does not imply byte-level equality,' extending S0901's three identity relations to an ordered hierarchy.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SemanticEquivalent(A_1,A_2,C,t) must include context and reference time ... CurrentVersion(2026)=3.70 ... SemanticEquivalent_{2025}\neq SemanticEquivalent_{2026}
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires SemanticEquivalent(A1,A2,C,t) to include context and reference time (not optional); worked example shows 'Nexus is current' equivalence to a fixed version differs between 2025 and 2026, reinforcing the temporal model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A_2\succeq A_1 ... A_2\succ A_1 ... not equivalence
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines refinement A2⪰A1 (A2 is a refinement of A1, e.g. a build-qualified version string refining a bare version), explicitly distinguished from equivalence — should be written A2≻A1, not A1=A2.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A_1\preceq A_2 if every situation satisfying A_2 also satisfies A_1 ... A_{specific}\Rightarrow A_{general}
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes refinement as a partial information order: A1⪯A2 iff every situation satisfying A2 also satisfies A1 (A_specific => A_general), worked with Version=3.69.0-build123 implying Version=3.69, computable 'if the version ontology defines the relationship.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: HasVersion(x,v_1)\land HasVersion(x,v_2)\Rightarrow v_1=v_2 ... A_1\perp A_2 ... genuine contradiction
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines contradiction A1⊥A2 for same subject/context/overlapping-time assertions under a functionally-exclusive predicate (HasVersion(x,v1) and HasVersion(x,v2) imply v1=v2) — 'a genuine contradiction.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: HasIPAddress(Server,10.0.0.1) and HasIPAddress(Server,10.0.0.2) ... Not necessarily [contradictory] ... server could have two interfaces ... Functional(HasIPAddress)=?
b_rows_sample.statement: Counterexample showing apparent contradiction (two IP addresses for one server) may not be contradictory since a server can have multiple interfaces; contradiction requires knowing whether the predicate is domain-functional (e.g. Functional(PrimaryIPAddress)=True but Functional(HasIPAddress)=False) — 'extremely important.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Contradiction(A_1,A_2,\Omega,C,T) ... a computed relation under a model
b_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes contradiction to Contradiction(A1,A2,Omega,C,T) where Omega is domain ontology/rules, C context, T temporal relation — contradiction is 'a computed relation under a model,' not purely semantic.

type_signature.domain: Assertion x Assertion x Ontology x Context x Temporal

b_rows_sample.anchor: LLM semantic difference \neq domain contradiction. The domain rules decide
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against a common AI error: an LLM seeing two differing IP-address facts and declaring 'contradiction' without consulting the domain model — 'LLM semantic difference ≠ domain contradiction. The domain rules decide.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: A_1: Version=3.69,t_1 ... A_2: Version=3.70,t_2 ... A_1\rightarrow A_2 ... TemporalEvolution\neq Contradiction
b_rows_sample.statement: Two differently-valued assertions ordered in time (t1<t2) may represent a state transition A1->A2 rather than a contradiction — 'TemporalEvolution ≠ Contradiction,' with both remaining historically valid and the current knowledge state selecting A2 as current.

b_rows_sample.anchor: we do not delete A_1 ... Status(A_1)=Historical ... preserves the knowledge trajectory
b_rows_sample.statement: When A2 supersedes A1 under temporal evolution, A1 is not deleted but marked Status(A1)=Historical — 'preserves the knowledge trajectory,' consistent with earlier non-destructive versioning principles.

b_rows_sample.anchor: M(K_1,K_2,\Omega,C,T)\rightarrow K_3 ... preserves identity, provenance, contradictions, temporal distinctions, confidence/assessment, source independence
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a first merge operator M(K1,K2,Omega,C,T)->K3 required to preserve identity, provenance, contradictions, temporal distinctions, confidence/assessment, and source independence — 'merging everything blindly would be dangerous.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Merge experiment 1: K_1=K_2=NexusVersion=3.69, different evidence, same context/time ... Merge does not duplicate the assertion. It aggregates support
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked Merge Experiment 1: two differently-evidenced knowledge items asserting the same value, same context/time, merge to one assertion with two supporting evidence paths — 'Merge does not duplicate the assertion. It aggregates support.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Merge experiment 2: K_1=3.69, K_2=3.70, same context/time ... must not arbitrarily select ... K_3: Conflict(A_1,A_2)
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked Merge Experiment 2: contradictory same-context/time values must not be arbitrarily resolved — merge preserves the conflict as K3:Conflict(A1,A2).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Merge experiment 3: K_1=3.69,2025, K_2=3.70,2026 ... History: 3.69->3.70. No conflict
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked Merge Experiment 3: time-ordered differing values merge into a history 3.69->3.70 with no conflict.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Merge experiment 4: K_1=3.69, K_2=3.69.0-build123 ... Refinement ... retain the more specific assertion while preserving the original
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked Merge Experiment 4: a general and a more specific value merge as Refinement, retaining the more specific assertion while preserving the original.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Merge(A_1,A_2)={Equivalent, Refinement, Refinement, Evolution, Conflict, Separate} ... a powerful computational classification
b_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates the four merge experiments into a six-branch conditional classification: Merge(A1,A2) = Equivalent | Refinement (A1⪯A2) | Refinement (A2⪯A1) | Evolution (temporal transition) | Conflict (A1⊥A2) | Separate (none of the above).

b_rows_sample.anchor: A_1: NexusVersion=3.69 and A_2: NexusCPU=8 ... Relation(A_1,A_2)=Independent
b_rows_sample.statement: 'Separate'/Independent is itself important: unrelated assertions about different predicates (version vs CPU count) need no relation beyond Relation(A1,A2)=Independent.

b_aliases: Semantic Equivalence / Refinement / Contradiction / Merge Algebra

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'semantic-equivalence-refinement-contradiction-merge-algebra' POSSIBLY relates to 'knowledge-identity-atma-algebra' (batch B0022). Note: S0902's Step 25J: attacks the one open semantic boundary left by S0901/Step 25I via a concrete relation algebra (Equal/Equivalent/Refines/RefinedBy/Contradicts/EvolvesTo/Independent), domain-relative contradiction, and a formal knowledge-merge operator with idempotence/commutativity/associativity questioned as open algebraic properties.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We now consolidate the previous experiments. The objective is to identify the smallest set of invariants whose violation would fundamentally change the nature of KnowledgeOS. Provenance+Authority+EpistemicStatus+TemporalValidity+DeterministicVerification+Traceability+Feedback.
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames Step 120's objective: identifying the smallest invariant set whose violation would fundamentally change KnowledgeOS, starting from a seven-part candidate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.1 — What makes an invariant constitutional? A constitutional invariant says: if this property is violated, the system no longer has the intended semantic character. ConstitutionalInvariant≠CodingConvention. 'Use PostgreSQL' is not necessarily constitutional. 'Authoritative knowledge must have id
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines ConstitutionalInvariant≠CodingConvention: a constitutional invariant's violation changes the system's intended semantic character, illustrated by contrasting a technology preference with a provenance requirement.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.2 — Invariant K1: Provenance ... Every authoritative knowledge object MUST have provenance. Provenance should answer where did it originate, when, through which process, who/what produced it, from which source material.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K1: every authoritative knowledge object must have provenance answering five questions (origin/when/process/producer/source material).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.3 — Why provenance is constitutional ... Without provenance, Knowledge becomes indistinguishable from GeneratedText. That destroys the ability to answer: Why should I trust this?
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues without provenance, Knowledge becomes indistinguishable from GeneratedText, destroying trust justification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.4 — Experiment K1.1 ... KnowledgeOS contains 'The architecture requires rootless containers.' No source, author, decision, timestamp or provenance exists. Can the system establish that it is authoritative? No. Verdict: K1 VIOLATED
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K1.1: a sourceless/authorless/timestampless architecture statement cannot be established as authoritative; verdict K1 VIOLATED.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.5 — Provenance does not equal source URL ... SourceURL does not tell us WhoApproved or WhenDidItBecomeValid. Source≠CompleteProvenance.
a_rows_sample.statement: States Source≠CompleteProvenance: a URL alone does not establish approval or validity onset.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.6 — Invariant K2: Authority ... Every authoritative governance change MUST have identifiable authority. Decision→Authority.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K2: every authoritative governance change must have identifiable authority (Decision->Authority).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.7 — Why authority is constitutional ... Without authority, Recommendation can silently become Decision. And AgentOutput can silently become OrganizationalTruth. That is unacceptable.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues without authority, Recommendation can silently become Decision and AgentOutput can silently become OrganizationalTruth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.8 — Experiment K2.1 ... Agent generates 'Architecture standard changed to X.' No authorized decision exists. Expected: Status=Proposed. Not Status=Authoritative. Verdict: K2 VIOLATION if promoted
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K2.1: an unauthorized agent-declared standard change must remain Status=Proposed; K2 VIOLATION if promoted to Authoritative.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.9 — Authority is not identity ... Actor≠Authority. Credential≠Authority. Role≠Authority unless the governance model explicitly establishes the mapping.
a_rows_sample.statement: States Actor≠Authority, Credential≠Authority, Role≠Authority unless the governance model explicitly maps them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.10 — Invariant K3: Epistemic status ... KnowledgeOS MUST distinguish observed, verified, inferred, proposed and authoritative information. This is perhaps the most important AI-specific invariant.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K3, called perhaps the most important AI-specific invariant: distinguishing observed/verified/inferred/proposed/authoritative information.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.11 — Why epistemic status matters ... 'The service probably owns this database' versus 'The Architecture Board decided that this service owns this database.' The textual similarity may be high. Their epistemic status is radically different.
a_rows_sample.statement: Illustrates why epistemic status matters via a textually-similar but epistemically-radically-different sentence pair.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.12 — Experiment K3.1 ... LLM generates Inference(X). System stores it identically to AuthoritativeDecision(X). Expected: K3 VIOLATION
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K3.1: storing an LLM inference identically to an authoritative decision is K3 VIOLATION.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.13 — Candidate epistemic states ... Observed, Imported, Asserted, Inferred, Proposed, Verified, Approved, Superseded. But we should only implement states that have real semantic value.
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists an eight-value candidate epistemic vocabulary, cautioning only states with real semantic value should be implemented.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.14 — Invariant K4: Temporal validity ... Authoritative knowledge MUST have determinable temporal validity. At minimum Current versus Superseded.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K4: authoritative knowledge must have determinable temporal validity, at minimum Current vs Superseded.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.15 — Why time is constitutional ... An architecture decision from 2024 may not represent the current architecture in 2026. Therefore HistoricalTruth≠CurrentTruth.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues HistoricalTruth≠CurrentTruth, illustrated by a 2024 decision potentially not representing 2026's current architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.16 — Experiment K4.1 ... Two decisions exist: D1 use architecture A, D2 use architecture B. No relationship identifies which supersedes which. Expected: agent cannot safely determine current architecture. Verdict: K4 VIOLATION
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K4.1: two competing, unlinked decisions leave an agent unable to safely determine current architecture; verdict K4 VIOLATION.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.17 — Creation time versus validity ... We must explicitly distinguish CreatedAt from ValidFrom. And potentially ValidUntil.
a_rows_sample.statement: States CreatedAt must be distinguished from ValidFrom (and potentially ValidUntil).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.18 — Experiment K4.2 ... Decision created 2026-08-01 but effective 2026-09-01. If the system only knows created_at, it cannot correctly answer is this decision currently effective. Verdict: K4 PARTIAL
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K4.2: a decision created before its effective date cannot be correctly evaluated by a created_at-only system; verdict K4 PARTIAL.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.19 — Invariant K5: Deterministic verification ... Where a claim is deterministically testable, authoritative assurance MUST be based on reproducible verification evidence. This does not eliminate human judgment. It prevents LLMConfidence from becoming Verification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K5: deterministically testable claims must be assured via reproducible evidence, preventing LLMConfidence from becoming Verification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Architecture Principles → Architecture Constitution → Architecture Decision Records → Implementation Standards → Code → Automated Assurance. A lower layer must not silently contradict a higher layer.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the constitutional hierarchy and the overall pipeline Architecture->Constitution->Deterministic Checks->Evidence; distinguishes Constitution (what architectural properties must be true) from Coding Standard (how developers write code, e.g. constructor injection) and from AGENTS.md (agent operating instructions that may explain compliance but never redefine the architecture).

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-001: Each authoritative domain concept has exactly one bounded-context owner. C-002: A bounded context must not depend directly on another bounded context's internal domain model (Assurance→DecisionReference, not Assurance→GovernanceDecisionEntity). C-003: An Aggregate is a consistency boundary, not a container for all related concepts. C-004: Authoritative state may not change through arbitrary field mutation (decision.activate(), not entity.status=EFFECTIVE). C-005: Command=Intent, Event=Fact; a command must not be named as an event (ApproveDecision producing DecisionApproved, not DecisionApproved as a command). C-006: Query → no authoritative state mutation, especially for the Context API.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines constitutional clauses C-001 through C-006 covering domain ownership, cross-context isolation, aggregate boundaries, explicit state transitions, command/event naming discipline, and query non-mutation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-007: External DTO must not cross into the domain — External API → Adapter DTO → Translator → Domain/Port Model. C-008: Dependency direction is Adapters→Ports→Application→Domain, never Domain→Nexus SDK or Domain→PostgreSQL driver. C-009: Domain purity — no HTTP, REST DTOs, database entities, message-broker classes, LLM SDKs, CLI frameworks, or vendor-specific infrastructure in the domain. C-010: The API is a capability boundary (ActivateDecision, RequestVerification) not arbitrary persistence operations (PATCH arbitrary entity).
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines constitutional clauses C-007 through C-010 covering external model isolation, infrastructure dependency direction, domain purity, and capability-oriented API design.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-011: Projection ↛ Authority — graph/search/cache may inform but never become the master domain-state source. C-012: Every derived projection must have a defined rebuild strategy (Authoritative State + Events/Change History → Projection Rebuild); an unrebuildable projection's authority status must be explicitly justified.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines constitutional clauses C-011 and C-012 on projection non-authority and rebuildability.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-013: Evidence used for assurance must be historically reconstructable (EvidenceID+Source+ObservedAt+Provenance, plus ContentHash where appropriate). C-014: A Verification must reference RuleID+RuleVersion, never a bare label like 'security rule.' C-015: A completed Verification is immutable historical fact — VerificationCompleted must never become VerificationModified; a new evaluation creates Verification_new. C-016: Where a rule is designated deterministic, Verify(E,R) must be reproducible for the same inputs; the LLM may interpret/explain but must not silently replace the deterministic checker.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines constitutional clauses C-013 through C-016 on evidence integrity, rule-version referencing, verification immutability, and deterministic assurance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-017: An AI recommendation is always distinct from a governance decision, authorization, verification, or execution — Recommendation ≠ Authorization. C-018: Agent cannot self-authorize — the path Agent→RequestAction→'Agent says approved'→Execute is constitutionally forbidden; the required path is Agent→RequestAction→Authorization→Execute. C-019: Authorization must not depend exclusively on AGENTS.md, prompt instructions, system messages, or agent goodwill — the platform must enforce it. C-020: For sensitive actions, Authorization→ActionID and, where required, Authorization→ActionFingerprint, preventing authorization from detaching from the exact operation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines constitutional clauses C-017 through C-020 on recommendation/authorization separation, self-authorization prohibition, server-enforced authorization, and action-binding.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-021: Context must have an explicit validity boundary (validUntil) for freshness-sensitive actions — a stale context must not automatically authorize a high-risk action. C-022: Material operations must be correlatable via TraceID, and where useful RequestID/CausationID. C-023: Retryable material commands need a stable idempotency mechanism (IdempotencyKey / ActionID) so duplicate delivery does not produce unintended duplicate effects. C-024: A state transition producing an integration event must persist the state change and event-publication intent atomically (transactional outbox), publishing only afterward. C-025: An event consumer must tolerate repeated delivery without duplicate semantic effects.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines constitutional clauses C-021 through C-025 on context freshness, trace identity, idempotency, transactional outbox, and idempotent event consumers.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-026: Published integration contracts must have explicit version semantics (VerificationCompleted.v1), with compatibility assessed on change. C-027: Contexts may reference one another by identifiers/contracts but must not form a giant shared cross-context transactional object graph (Decision→Policy→Rule→Verification→Evidence→Action as one object is forbidden). C-028: A ContextPackage is assembled from authoritative sources and is a Projection/Composition, not a new authority. C-029: Material Context items must retain enough provenance (source, sourceType, reference, validity, authority) to answer where information came from. C-030: The Context Service should provide minimum sufficient governed context, not indiscriminately expose the entire dataset.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines constitutional clauses C-026 through C-030 on event versioning, no shared cross-context object graph, context-as-projection, context provenance, and context minimization.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-031: Agent memory is explicitly non-authoritative unless promoted through the governed knowledge process (Memory→Candidate Claim→Evidence→Verification→Governed Knowledge). C-032: Engineering knowledge must not be hidden exclusively in .claude/.codex/AGENTS.md — those may point to and locally enforce, but KnowledgeOS remains the governed semantic authority. C-033: Claude and Codex must consume the same KnowledgeOS semantic contract (Contract_Claude=Contract_Codex); only the harness adapter may differ. C-034: The domain must not contain vendor-specific concepts (ClaudeDecision, CodexVerification, OpenAIClaim, AnthropicPolicy) unless they genuinely exist as business concepts — vendor-specific behavior belongs at the integration boundary.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines constitutional clauses C-031 through C-034 on memory non-authority, repository knowledge boundary, agent symmetry, and no vendor-specific domain semantics.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-035: KnowledgeOS must not claim operational state owned by an external engineering system without evidence — e.g. Nexus is authoritative for its own runtime/config state; KnowledgeOS records Observation+Evidence+Provenance. C-036: An agent must never represent an assertion as externally observed evidence without an actual source — AgentAssertion ≠ Observation. C-037: A caller must not submit a verdict directly as though it were a completed assurance operation; the checker produces the verdict. C-038: Failures must preserve semantic meaning (AUTHORIZATION_DENIED, CONTEXT_EXPIRED, INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, RULE_NOT_APPLICABLE, INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION, EXECUTION_FAILED), never collapsed into generic technical errors. C-039: HighRiskAction+UnknownAuthorization ⇒ BLOCK, enforced independently of agent instructions. C-040: The first KnowledgeOS vertical slice must use read-only engineering operations, a temporary implementation constraint, not necessarily a permanent platform rule.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines constitutional clauses C-035 through C-040 on external operational authority, no fabricated evidence/verification, semantically meaningful failures, fail-closed high-risk actions, and the read-only-first implementation constraint — completing the forty-clause Constitution.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Constitution = the machine-checkable set of architectural invariants that every KnowledgeOS implementation must satisfy unless an explicitly governed exception applies.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives the Constitution's formal definition; specifies a 20-section constitution-document outline (Purpose, Scope, Normative language, Architectural principles, Bounded contexts, Dependency/Aggregate/API/Event/Persistence/Evidence/Assurance/Authorization/Agent/Adapter/Projection/Traceability rules, Exception process, Automated conformance, Definition of Done); adopts MUST/MUST NOT/SHOULD/SHOULD NOT/MAY normative language suitable for both humans and tooling; gives a worked constitutional clause example (ARCH-AUTH-001: the Action domain MUST NOT transition to an executable state unless a valid Authorization exists, Severity=BLOCKING, Verification=ActionAuthorizationChecker), stronger than prose like 'actions should normally be authorized.'

b_rows_sample.statement: Step 152 verdict: presents the constitutional loop and states the central transformation Architecture Documentation -> Architecture Constitution -> Machine-Checkable Invariants, bridging the conceptual architecture to the existing implementation philosophy (deterministic assurance, registry, hooks, session/change logging, Claude/Codex symmetry, governance).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The kernel creates the ecosystem; the company creates value around the ecosystem.
a_rows_sample.statement: Uses the Linux/Red Hat precedent to argue KnowledgeOS's moat is the kernel plus governance plus evidence model (not the AI model, which is commoditized), proposing a Community/Professional/Enterprise revenue-tier structure and a 10-year IPO roadmap.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel = the minimal system responsible for creating, identifying, relating, governing, and preserving organizational knowledge objects.
a_rows_sample.statement: The proposed load-bearing definition of the 'KnowledgeOS Kernel', explicitly modeled after the Linux kernel's separation from applications: the kernel provides knowledge primitives (Identity, Lifecycle, Evidence, Authority) and must not know about specific technologies (SAP, Kubernetes, Jira).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Linus did not start by designing 'the operating system of the world.' He started by solving a concrete problem, created a small working kernel ... 'Can we create a trusted kernel that allows digitalization robots to operate safely?'
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues KnowledgeOS should not start with an AI-driven Digitalization Robot ambition; the correct starting question is the smallest trusted kernel that later allows robots to operate safely, mirroring Linux's incremental 0.01-kernel-first history.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Open-source the KnowledgeOS Kernel. Commercialize the Digitalization Robot Platform.
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends an open-core business model (open KnowledgeOS Kernel for trust/ecosystem, commercial Digitalization Robot/Enterprise Platform for revenue), by analogy with Linux Kernel vs Red Hat Enterprise Linux.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Linux manages computer resources. KnowledgeOS manages organizational intelligence resources ... which knowledge is valid, who owns it, and how can it be trusted?
a_rows_sample.statement: States the deepest claimed difference between the Linux and KnowledgeOS kernel analogies: Linux answers 'which process can access which resource', while KnowledgeOS must answer 'which knowledge is valid, who owns it, and how can it be trusted.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rust for the KnowledgeOS Kernel, Kotlin/Spring for the Enterprise Runtime, Python for Intelligence, TypeScript for Experience.
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends a multi-language technology stack (Rust kernel for memory-safety/correctness, Kotlin+Spring Boot enterprise runtime, Python intelligence layer, TypeScript studio/frontend) with an estimated 12-18 month timeline for a first Kernel v1.0 with a small expert team.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If you want IPO potential, do not position KnowledgeOS as 'AI chatbot' ... nor 'Documentation tool' ... Position as: The operating system for enterprise knowledge and digital transformation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues the commercial positioning category determines addressable market size; 'AI chatbot' is too easy to copy, 'documentation tool' is too small a category for IPO ambitions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel scope: 'minimal kernel, no AI' (S0167) vs the platform vision where an AI-driven Digitalization Robot is the top layer (S0171) — the corpus itself frames the robot as a distribution, keeping the kernel AI-free, so the tension is scope of the 'core' vs the 'product'.
a_rows_sample.statement: Surfaces T1: a minimal AI-free kernel proposal versus an AI-driven robot as the platform's top execution layer, resolved by the corpus's own framing (robot = distribution, kernel stays AI-free) but not formally decided.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rust · Spring Boot · Gradle/Cargo · microservices · plugin architecture · Event Sourcing · Kafka are recommendations/hypotheses in the corpus, never adopted KnowledgeOS technology.
