b_rows_sample.statement: Formally separates three notions that must not be collapsed -- observational-neutrality Zero, adverse contribution (Neg), and supporting contribution (Pos), all relative to (T,Pi,Q) -- and distinguishes two different reasons Zero could arise: genuinely no contribution at all, versus contributions that cancel, a crucial distinction for interpreting any observed Zero result.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R4 = T4(R5); R3 = T3(R4); R2 = T2(R3) ... data-processing inequality gives H(Q|R_{n-1}) >= H(Q|R_n) ... adequacy cannot recover later in a deterministic sequential chain.
a_rows_sample.statement: Derives, via the data-processing inequality applied to the deterministic chain Q->R_n->R_{n-1} (each R_{n-1}=T_n(R_n)), that H(Q|R_5)<=H(Q|R_4)<=H(Q|R_3)<=H(Q|R_2), i.e. adequacy cannot recover later in a deterministic sequential chain; reclassifies the original hypothesis H-C (that adequacy could become non-monotone, e.g. R3 adequate again after R4 inadequate) not as empirically falsified by the data but as structurally ill-posed/a priori inapplicable to this experiment class, recommending the frozen label read '[THEORY/NEG] H-C was ill-posed for the specified sequential deterministic chain; the data-processing inequality makes non-monotone conditional-entropy adequacy impossible' rather than 'H-C refuted a priori', on the ground that a priori impossibility and empirical falsification are epistemically distinct.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sequential family: D -> R5 -> R4 -> R3 -> R2 ... No recovery is possible. Parallel family: D -> R_A, D -> R_B, D -> R_C ... Non-monotone comparative behavior is possible here.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a distinction proposed to become part of the theory: a 'sequential family' of representations (each derived deterministically from the previous one) where H(Q|R) is provably monotone with no recovery possible, versus a 'parallel family' of independently constructed representations from the same source D, where one representation can destroy a distinction while another independently preserves it, so non-monotone comparative adequacy is possible; frames this as the difference between monotonicity along a sequential information-reducing chain and comparative adequacy across independently constructed representations, expected to matter when investigating alternative knowledge representations later.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Hhat(Q)=5.0098 ... R5=15.042, R4=12.307, R3=11.097, R2=7.170 ... Hhat(R_n) > Hhat(Q) at every level ... empirical consistency with the theoretical bound.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports hypothesis H-E's result that empirical Hhat(R_n) exceeds Hhat(Q) at every level of the chain (R5=15.042 through R2=7.170, versus Hhat(Q)=5.0098), matching the expected theoretical lower-bound relationship under the relevant assumptions, and endorses treating this as empirical consistency with the theoretical bound rather than as a proof.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R5 -> R4 Zero rate 3.77% / R4 -> R3 Zero rate 4.26% / R3 -> R2 Zero rate 0.00% ... does not show a Zero/boundary relationship ... we should not make Zero the fundamental preservation criterion.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports hypothesis H-RR2's negative result: measured Zero rates across the chain (3.77%, 4.26%, 0.00%) show no association between Zero and the observed preservation boundary, refuting the original suspicion that Zero -> preservation boundary; concludes Zero should not be treated as the fundamental preservation criterion but as one possible mechanism within a broader architecture that separately includes eliminability/Zero, preservation/adequacy, realization, and reduction cost.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SOURCE -> Transformation / Representation / Inquiry Q / Preservation contract Pi / Decoder O -> Recoverability/Adequacy -> Preservation boundary -> Eliminability(Zero) / Reduction measures
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a revised overall theory architecture diagram superseding the prior linear trajectory (Vedic transformations -> Zero/eliminability -> relationality -> representation reduction -> preservation): SOURCE branches into Transformation, Representation, Inquiry Q, Preservation contract Pi, and Decoder O, which jointly determine Recoverability/Adequacy, which locates a Preservation boundary, which in turn splits into Eliminability (Zero) and Reduction measures as two downstream, non-foundational consequences.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A. Mathematical theory: H(Q|R)=0 ... H(R)=H(Q)+H(R|Q) ... R_{n-1}=T_n(R_n) => H(Q|R_{n-1}) >= H(Q|R_n). B. KR-ZERO empirical evidence [list]. C. KR-REP-REDUCTION empirical evidence [list].
a_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates the current state of knowledge into three tiers: (A) the mathematical theory -- H(Q|R)=0 as the sufficiency/adequacy criterion, the decomposition H(R)=H(Q)+H(R|Q) for adequate deterministic representations, and the monotonicity consequence H(Q|R_{n-1})>=H(Q|R_n); (B) a nine-point list of KR-ZERO empirical findings (Zero is context/transformation/contract-relative, group Zero can differ from member Zero, higher-order determination exists but is not universal, interaction order is not globally monotonic, the phenomenon is transformation-dependent, Zero gives no simple universal kernel/algebra); (C) a ten-point list of KR-REP-REDUCTION empirical findings (observable preservation boundary in a sequential chain, boundary detectable via Q-recoverability, first loss at T4 in this run, reduction is multidimensional, adequacy and realization can diverge, a purely representational recoding can leave recoverability unchanged while altering a fixed decoder, Zero did not correlate with the boundary, contract failure and operator-only failure did not occur, non-monotone adequacy was structurally impossible for this chain).

a_rows_sample.anchor: At which transformation does the representation cease to preserve the inquiry we care about? ... Given inquiry Q and preservation contract Pi, does representation R still contain enough information to recover Q? ... a potentially powerful foundation for a KnowledgeOS extraction engine.
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames the practical KnowledgeOS payoff of the representation-reduction results: given a progressive construction chain from raw document through structured representation, claims, relations, normalized claims, knowledge representation, to compressed knowledge representation, the rigorous question 'at which transformation does the representation cease to preserve inquiry Q' can be answered by measuring H(Q|R_n), N_viol(R_n), H(R_n|Q), and representation cost -- proposed as a more rigorous foundation for a KnowledgeOS extraction engine than an informal judgment that summarized information 'still looks present'.

a_rows_sample.statement: States explicitly that the current results do not amount to a general knowledge-extraction theory: they were tested only on a small numerical carrier r=(value, source, timestamp) with a specific Q=(argmax_source, decile(total)) and one particular transformation chain, and transferring the theory to richer carriers (documents, claims, entities, relations, provenance, contradictions, temporal states, evidence) remains an open research question, characterized as 'perfectly fine' rather than a defect.

a_rows_sample.statement: Issues an overall verdict: keep/freeze the old KR-ZERO result (with mechanistic wording narrowed) whose major contribution is that eliminability can be relational, contextual, transformation-dependent, and sometimes higher-order; accept the new KR-REP-REDUCTION result as a successful first representation-reduction experiment whose major contributions are that a specified representation chain can be experimentally tested for preservation with a boundary located without assuming it in advance, that adequacy (what a representation makes recoverable) is distinct from realization (what a particular decoder actually recovers), and that sequential reduction and parallel representation comparison are different mathematical regimes that should become a permanent theoretical distinction.

a_rows_sample.statement: Re-derives from R_{n-1}=T_n(R_n) with deterministic T_n that H(Q|R_{n-1})>=H(Q|R_n), boxing the consequence 'once sufficiency is lost in this chain, it cannot be recovered downstream', and formally classifies this as '[THEORY] Sequential data-processing constraint' with the accompanying '[NEG] H-C is structurally inapplicable to deterministic sequential reduction' rather than retaining H-C as an empirical hypothesis for this experiment class.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sequential reduction: D->R5->R4->R3->R2 ... information sufficiency is monotone. Parallel alternatives: D-> R_A/R_B/R_C ... H(Q|R_A)<H(Q|R_B) is perfectly possible ... we should preserve it permanently.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes and endorses permanently preserving the distinction between Sequential Reduction (D->R5->R4->R3->R2, where information sufficiency is monotone by data processing) and Alternative/Parallel Representation Comparison (D branching into R_A, R_B, R_C with no data-processing ordering between them, so H(Q|R_A)<H(Q|R_B) is perfectly possible), naming these two distinct research regimes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Representation != Recoverability != Realization, where Representation = what is encoded; Recoverability = what can in principle be reconstructed; Realization = what a particular decoder actually reconstructs.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a three-way conceptual distinction -- Representation (what is encoded), Recoverability (what can in principle be reconstructed), and Realization (what a particular decoder actually reconstructs) -- as strictly non-identical properties, proposed to become a major concept in the future KnowledgeOS extraction architecture, sharper than a mere two-way adequacy-vs-realization split.

a_rows_sample.statement: Sharpens the KR-REP-REDUCTION-2026-09 headline claim: the key result is not yet 'representation reduction' but more precisely that the experiment demonstrates contract-relative recoverability loss under a deterministic sequential representation chain D->R5->R4->R3->R2, with the preservation-boundary claim properly restricted to the specified carrier, inquiry, contract, transformation chain, and value alphabet.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R_{n-1}=T_n(R_n) with deterministic T_n ... H(Q|R_{n-1}) >= H(Q|R_n) ... Once sufficiency is lost in this chain, it cannot be recovered downstream. [THEORY] Sequential data-processing constraint. [NEG] H-C is structurally inapplicable to deterministic sequential reduction.
a_rows_sample.statement: Re-derives from R_{n-1}=T_n(R_n) with deterministic T_n that H(Q|R_{n-1})>=H(Q|R_n), boxing the consequence 'once sufficiency is lost in this chain, it cannot be recovered downstream', and formally classifies this as '[THEORY] Sequential data-processing constraint' with the accompanying '[NEG] H-C is structurally inapplicable to deterministic sequential reduction' rather than retaining H-C as an empirical hypothesis for this experiment class.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sequential reduction: D->R5->R4->R3->R2 ... information sufficiency is monotone. Parallel alternatives: D-> R_A/R_B/R_C ... H(Q|R_A)<H(Q|R_B) is perfectly possible ... we should preserve it permanently.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes and endorses permanently preserving the distinction between Sequential Reduction (D->R5->R4->R3->R2, where information sufficiency is monotone by data processing) and Alternative/Parallel Representation Comparison (D branching into R_A, R_B, R_C with no data-processing ordering between them, so H(Q|R_A)<H(Q|R_B) is perfectly possible), naming these two distinct research regimes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Representation != Recoverability != Realization, where Representation = what is encoded; Recoverability = what can in principle be reconstructed; Realization = what a particular decoder actually reconstructs.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a three-way conceptual distinction -- Representation (what is encoded), Recoverability (what can in principle be reconstructed), and Realization (what a particular decoder actually reconstructs) -- as strictly non-identical properties, proposed to become a major concept in the future KnowledgeOS extraction architecture, sharper than a mere two-way adequacy-vs-realization split.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R_up =~enc R_down if and only if the implementation demonstrates a bijection between them ... exists f,g: f(R_up)=R_down, g(R_down)=R_up with g o f = id, f o g = id. Only then should we connect this experiment strongly to the existing Q-equivalence research.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires that the ascending/descending rank representations only be called equivalent (R_up cong_enc R_down) once the implementation demonstrates an actual bijection f,g between them satisfying g.f=id and f.g=id, and that any residual measured difference in H(Q|R) absent such a bijection be attributed to sampling/estimation or implementation effects rather than treated as evidence of non-equivalence; only a confirmed bijection should connect this result to the existing Q-equivalence research.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero -> PreservationBoundary. The experiment did not demonstrate that. ... Zero != definition of preservation ... This is good news, because it prevents the KnowledgeOS theory from becoming circular: Zero -> something can be removed -> therefore preservation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues that the negative finding Zero != definition of preservation (observed Zero rates 3.77%, 4.26%, 0% showing no demonstrated correspondence with the R5->R4 preservation boundary) is good news because it prevents the KnowledgeOS theory from becoming circular (Zero -> something can be removed -> therefore preservation), providing evidence that Zero, preservation, realization, and reduction are separate research concerns.

a_rows_sample.anchor: (D,Q,Pi) -> R -> {Adequacy, Realization, Eliminability, Cost}. This is significantly better than trying to make Zero the central algebra from which everything else follows.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a cleaner research architecture where (D,Q,Pi) determines a representation R, which is then evaluated along four independent axes -- Adequacy, Realization, Eliminability, Cost -- explicitly rejecting the earlier framing that tried to make Zero the central algebra from which everything else follows.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The tested carrier is still very small: r=(value,source,timestamp) ... We have not yet demonstrated preservation over semantic claims, entities, relations, provenance, contradictions, temporal claims, evidence, hypotheses, epistemic standards. So the proper abstraction is currently Contract-relative
a_rows_sample.statement: Insists the current abstraction be called 'contract-relative representation preservation', not 'knowledge extraction calculus', because the tested carrier remains a small numerical tuple r=(value,source,timestamp) and preservation has not yet been demonstrated over semantic claims, entities, relations, provenance, contradictions, temporal claims, evidence, hypotheses, or epistemic standards.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The next audit should explicitly test target leakage. Q not-in Inputs(T), Q not-in Inputs(O), Q not-in Inputs(C), except for the evaluator. ... D --T--> R --O--> Qhat ... evaluator independently computes Q(D). Then compare Qhat =? Q(D).
a_rows_sample.statement: Adds a new required audit check for target leakage: the inquiry target Q must not appear in the inputs of the transformation T, the decoder O, or the constraint C except as the evaluator's independent target, specifying the clean experimental architecture D--T-->R--O-->Qhat with an evaluator independently computing Q(D) and comparing Qhat against Q(D), to guard against the answer being indirectly encoded into the transformation or decoder.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Eliminability, Preservation and Realization are three distinct questions. None implies another.
b_rows_sample.statement: The load-bearing result of the Theory 00-14 programme: Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))) [Zero/eliminability], Hhat(Q|T(D))=0 [Adequacy/preservation] and O(T(D))=Q(D) [Realization] are shown to differ in every system tested, by independent mechanisms; tagged [EXP] deliberately rather than [THM] because necessity of the separation in general is unproven.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Eliminability does not predict Preservation
b_rows_sample.statement: Four experiments of increasing power (H-RR2 boundary-crossing Zero rate 0.0377 vs 0.0426; KR-BRIDGE-01 marginal RD=-0.363 fully explained by redundancy confounding; KR-BRIDGE-02 H1 not refuted; KR-BRIDGE-03 at 13x informative strata, H1 still not refuted, surviving cells 14->1) converge on the same negative finding, stable under a 13-fold power increase.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Preservation does not give Realization
b_rows_sample.statement: Hhat(Q|R5)=0 (adequate) is a separate fact from O(R5)=Q(D) (realized): a fixed decoder can fail on information-theoretically adequate data because it was fixed in advance and not refit; flagged as a design defect that the KR-REP-REDUCTION chain never operationalized this separation (no dropped record/source ever made constraint C fail), so 'the separation is real; that experiment could not exhibit it.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Eliminability does not give Realization
b_rows_sample.statement: Not derivable merely from the other two separations (explicitly not a corollary): Zero is defined via Pi, which is read-disjoint from Q by construction, so it carries no information about Q's recoverability 'by design' — verified rather than assumed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Realization ⟹ Adequacy
b_rows_sample.statement: Standing conjecture that if a fixed decoder recovers Q from R on every observed case, R determines Q on the realized cases; refutable by a decoder that is right by luck (correct on every observed case while the fiber is Q-heterogeneous); explicitly 'not tested.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do the separations survive a non-synthetic carrier?
b_rows_sample.statement: Flagged as the central transfer problem: whether eliminability/preservation/realization separations generalize beyond the tested synthetic carrier is explicitly open.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The estimand for any bridge claim is the within-stratum effect.
b_rows_sample.statement: The programme's central methodological error was estimating the wrong quantity competently — the marginal P(A|Z)-P(A|not Z) was already known to be confounded before KR-BRIDGE-02 ran; re-estimating it produced a false 'H2 SUPPORTED'; the correct estimand is the Mantel-Haenszel within-stratum effect.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A stratum is informative iff (a_k+b_k)>0 ∧ (c_k+d_k)>0 ∧ (a_k+c_k)>0 ∧ (b_k+d_k)>0
b_rows_sample.statement: Both Zero and non-Zero must occur and both Adequate and Inadequate must occur for a stratum to be informative; strata at deterministic extremes contribute nothing, explaining why flattening the redundancy distribution failed (balance is not power) and why choosing a finer stratification variable (multiplicity partition, then partition x |S|) gave 13x the informative strata.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sign agreement alone is not replication.
b_rows_sample.statement: Under a sign-only replication rule, 14 cells 'replicated' with |RD|~0.001 and 12 of 14 had no stratum CI excluding zero; all 14 collapsed at higher power. Replication requires sign agreement AND clearing a substantive floor on both splits AND at least one stratum's 95% CI excluding zero; per-stratum RDs must be reported, not only the pooled MH estimate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If the floor is declared after first inspection, record that fact in the artifact
b_rows_sample.statement: Effect-size floors must be declared and used as a reporting tier rather than a filter (publish every surviving cell at both tiers) since at n~10^5 statistical significance is not evidence of anything; a post-inspection floor must be disclosed as such.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Bootstrap CI on Ĥ ... [DEFECT] invalid here
b_rows_sample.statement: Estimator hygiene register: N_viol is exact and bias-free (authoritative for combinatorial adequacy questions), the Miller-Madow correction is used for Hhat, Haldane+0.5/Woolf CI is used for sparse odds-ratio tables, and bootstrap CI on Hhat is invalid because resampling duplicates cases and depresses conditional entropy.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Within the tested deduplication regime, redundancy behaves as a common cause of Zero occurrence and of inadequacy.
b_rows_sample.statement: Standard formalized here: never state a regime-specific empirical finding as a general causal law; a single-mechanism explanation of the KR-BRIDGE-01 confound was itself withdrawn once the Zero-count was found constant at r=1 but varying at r=2, showing the exact RD=0 had two different causes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Power is a property of the informative region, not of n.
b_rows_sample.statement: Measured across four candidate power levers: population size (no effect, 73/74/70 across n=1500/4000/8000) and flattening the confounder distribution (73->75, no effect) both do nothing, while record count (73->233) and finer stratification variable (~30->388) are the effective levers; when power stops responding to sampling, the constraint has moved into the design (the 67 dead cells are invariant across nine generator regimes because the adequacy definition itself saturates).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Everything in this set is built from six objects and one operator.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theory 01 fixes the six-object signature of the KnowledgeOS transformation carrier: D (data, a finite multiset of records), T (transformation D->R), R=T(D) (representation), Q (inquiry D->Y), Pi (observable R->O), O (decoder R->Y), and C (constraint predicate on R), plus the inquiry frame Pi_frame=(Q,C,O) with O fixed in advance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: a record r = (value, source, tag, timestamp)
b_rows_sample.statement: A record in the tested carriers is r=(value,source,tag,timestamp), optionally a derived rank; explicitly flagged as an experimental carrier, not declared to be the mathematical carrier of KnowledgeOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Set subtraction D \ S is INVALID wherever a field is relative.
b_rows_sample.statement: The elimination operator E_S must be typed to the level it acts at and must recompute relative fields (e.g. within-group rank) after removing S; naive set subtraction D\S leaves stale relative values and produces a representation the level's own rules forbid.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero is indexed by (T,Π) and by the subset S; adequacy by (T,Q) and the population; realization by (T,Q,O) and the case.
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero, Adequacy and Realization are defined with different index sets and are not three readings of one quantity: Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) <=> Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))); Adequate(T,Q) <=> Hhat(Q|T(D))=0; Realized(T,Q,O) <=> O(T(D))=Q(D).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Π and Q must read disjoint fields, and disjointness must be discharged on the triple (Π, Q, T), not the pair (Π, Q).
b_rows_sample.statement: An anti-circularity requirement (candidate FR-003) is proposed: read-disjointness of Pi and Q must be verified on the triple (Pi,Q,T) because T can derive an output field Pi reads from sources Pi never declared; two concrete KR-BRIDGE-02 failures (a rank field secretly shared with Q's tag field, and an arity observable secretly reading value via deduplication survivorship) show declaration is not verification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS has no declared mathematical carrier.
b_rows_sample.statement: Every experiment used a deliberately small numerical carrier (|D|<=6) so fibers would collide and adequacy would be measurable; this is a calibration choice, not an ontological one, and the move to documents/claims/entities/relations/provenance/contradictions/temporal states/evidence is the open research problem.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A transformation family is either sequential (Rk+1 = Tk(Rk)) or parallel (Rk = Tk(D)) — never silently mixed
b_rows_sample.statement: Sequential vs parallel transformation families is a permanent type-discipline rule, load-bearing because the data-processing inequality (document 04) applies to sequential families and not to parallel ones.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 4 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: 0_i != empty != Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) unless a later experiment establishes a structure-preserving correspondence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that algebraic zero (0_i in D_i with x (+)_i 0_i = x), epistemic absence/omission (k_i=empty or not represented), and preservation-relative Zero (Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) iff Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D)))) are three distinct notions that must not be identified unless a structure-preserving correspondence is demonstrated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P_S^restrict(K): a dimension-truncating operation ... P_S^0(K): an ambient-preserving projection mapping ... k_i -> 0_i for i not in S.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes restriction P_S^restrict(K): product_i D_i -> product_{i in S} D_i (changes ambient dimensionality) from zero projection P_S^0(K): product_i D_i -> product_i D_i (ambient-preserving, mapping k_i to 0_i for i not in S); testing whether P_S^restrict(K) equiv P_S^0(K) under an observational query Q determines whether epistemic silence can be faithfully modeled by an algebraic zero element.

a_rows_sample.anchor: HZ_1 (Identity Law) ... HZ_2 (Projection Idempotence) ... HZ_3 (Projection Intersection) ... HZ_4 (Restriction Equivalence) ... HZ_5 (Resolution Atomicity) ... HZ_6 (Emergent Observational Relevance)
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the original six hypotheses for the initial 'KR-ZOOM-01 (Algebraic Zero & Recursive Zoom)' protocol: HZ1 identity law x(+)_i 0_i=x; HZ2 idempotence P_S^0(P_S^0(K))=P_S^0(K); HZ3 intersection P_S^0(P_T^0(K))=P_{S∩T}^0(K); HZ4 restriction equivalence Obs_Q(P_S^0(K)) equiv Obs_Q(P_S^restrict(K)); HZ5 resolution atomicity (an irreducible x_r expands to a nested space with k>1 dimensions on zoom); HZ6 emergent observational relevance (a dimension Zero under query Q_r maps to a nested dimension non-Zero under Q_{r+1}).

a_rows_sample.anchor: HZ1 should become: HZ1 -- Domain Algebra Existence ... Does a tested knowledge-domain representation admit a composition operation (+)_i and distinguished element 0_i satisfying an empirically and semantically justified identity law?
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects HZ1 from an assumed identity law x(+)_i0_i=x to an open existence question: does a tested knowledge-domain representation admit a composition operation and distinguished element satisfying an empirically and semantically justified identity law, since algebra must be discovered from behaviour, not imposed on the problem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P_S^0P_T^0 =? P_T^0P_S^0. Do not assume commutativity merely because the notation suggests it.
a_rows_sample.statement: HZ2/HZ3 are corrected to be recognized as properties of a specific constructed coordinate-zeroing operator rather than discovered KnowledgeOS properties (risk of circularity), and the intersection test HZ3 must also explicitly test order (P_S^0 P_T^0 =? P_T^0 P_S^0) rather than assuming commutativity from notation, especially given the corpus's existing order-sensitivity findings.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Atomic_r(x) does not imply Atomic_{r+1}(Z_r(x)). ... x_r in D^(r) is representation-atomic under the current resolution, while a refinement map Z_r ... may expose a richer structure.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects HZ5 to avoid conflating atomicity of representation with atomicity of knowledge: x_r is representation-atomic under the current resolution, while a refinement map Z_r:D^(r)->K^(r+1) may expose a richer structure, giving Atomic_r(x) does not imply Atomic_{r+1}(Z_r(x)).

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would call this: Resolution-relative eliminability rather than "Zero alteration." Because nothing has changed about Zero itself. The carrier and inquiry have changed
a_rows_sample.statement: Renames HZ6's phenomenon from 'Zero alteration' to 'resolution-relative eliminability': Zero itself is unchanged, only the carrier and inquiry have changed ((D^(r),Q_r,Pi_r) -> (D^(r+1),Q_{r+1},Pi_{r+1})), giving Zero_r(x) does not imply Zero_{r+1}(x').

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero Algebra <-> Zoom/Resolution <-> Biological Reciprocal Communication ... none of the three gets to dictate the others.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a triangle of three mutually-informing but non-dictating research programmes: Zero Algebra (eliminability tests), Zoom/Resolution (resolution changes), and Biological Reciprocal Communication (relational sequences), all evaluated through Knowledge Theory's epistemic semantics and contracts, with none entitled to define the KnowledgeOS kernel.

a_rows_sample.anchor: HZ1-HZ6 should be treated as candidate hypotheses, not as a package whose truth is expected to converge toward an algebra. ... HZ4 should be the first experiment
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the framing of HZ1-HZ6: they are candidate hypotheses, not a package expected to converge toward a proven algebra; HZ4 (does P_S^0 faithfully mimic P_S^restrict under O_{Q,Pi}) is designated the first, gating experiment because it tests the bridge between representational omission and algebraic zeroing -- if it fails, HZ1-HZ3 may still hold for some domain but cannot model KnowledgeOS omission without additional structure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ZERO-RESOLUTION-2026-09 ... Status [PROP][OPEN][RESEARCH ARTIFACT] ... Objective: Test whether three notions can be related: AlgebraicZero <-> RepresentationalOmission <-> PreservationZero without assuming their equivalence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Names the artifact KR-ZERO-RESOLUTION-2026-09 (status [PROP][OPEN][RESEARCH ARTIFACT], Theory v1.2 frozen, kernel untouched, no new algebraic axioms), replacing the earlier draft's reuse of the 'KR-ZOOM-01' ID which collided with the pre-existing distinct KR-ZOOM-01 experiment; its objective is to test whether AlgebraicZero, RepresentationalOmission, and PreservationZero can be related without assuming their equivalence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Phase 1 -- HZ4 first ... Phase 2 -- test the projection algebra ... Phase 3 -- domain algebra ... Phase 4 -- recursive resolution
a_rows_sample.statement: Lays out a four-phase execution architecture: Phase 1 tests HZ4 (O_{Q,Pi}(P_S^0(K)) =? O_{Q,Pi}(P_S^restr(K))), proceeding to Phase 2 (HZ2 idempotence, HZ3 intersection AND order P_S^0 P_T^0 =? P_T^0 P_S^0) only if Phase 1 survives; Phase 3 tests HZ1 domain-algebra existence as a control independent of KnowledgeOS (could show domain algebra valid while Algebraic Zero != KnowledgeOS Zero); Phase 4 tests the recursive Zoom hypothesis x^(r) -Z-> K_x^(r+1), asking whether Zero_r(x)=1 can coexist with exists x' in K_x^(r+1): Zero_{r+1}(x')=0, correctly interpreted as 'a preservation judgment at resolution r does not necessarily determine preservation judgments over the refined carrier at resolution r+1', not 'Zero becoming non-Zero.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: At coarse resolution C^(r)=[sigma_1,rho_1,sigma_2,rho_2] might be eliminable ... Zooming in ... can expose distinctions that were invisible at the coarse level. Therefore Zero^(r)(C)=1 does not imply Zero^(r+1)(C)=1
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies the resolution-relative-eliminability idea to a concrete courtship-sequence example: at coarse resolution the sequence [sigma1,rho1,sigma2,rho2] might be eliminable with respect to a terminal-state inquiry, while a finer resolution exposing orientation/distance/timing/repeated-approach/avoidance can reveal distinctions invisible at the coarse level, giving both Zero^(r)(C)=1 does not imply Zero^(r+1)(C)=1 and its converse Zero^(r)(C)=0 does not imply Zero^(r+1)(C)=0.

a_rows_sample.anchor: HZ6 tests whether eliminability changes across resolution levels under explicitly paired carriers and preservation contracts. Because the experiment can falsify HZ6. It cannot start by saying it proves it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the document's assertive framing ('HZ6 proves eliminability changes with carrier & contract scale') to a testable, falsifiable framing ('HZ6 tests whether eliminability changes across resolution levels under explicitly paired carriers and preservation contracts'), and similarly corrects HZ4's framing from a universal determination claim to a claim relative to the tested carrier/transformation/observation/inquiry/contract.

b_rows_sample.anchor: fractal, resolution-dependent topology ... What we currently have evidence for is: resolution-dependent, recursively refinable knowledge structure
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects 'fractal topology' as too strong (implies unestablished self-similarity/topology/infinite recursion), replacing it with the weaker, testable claim that a point at one resolution may correspond to a structured subspace at a finer resolution.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero and Focus are currently conflated ... Zero concerns influence: Influence_i(K|Q,C)=0. Focus concerns what we choose to make operative/observable: Focus_S(K).
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates Zero (a claim about influence) from Focus/projection (a choice about what to observe), stating 'Projection may instantiate a Zero assumption' but Projection != Zero, and warning that a projected P_{1}(K)=(d_1,0,0) view must not be read as proving d_2=d_3=0 in the underlying state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: generally C \circ Z \neq Id and Z \circ C \neq Id. Why? Because compression can lose information.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects an assumed Compression(Zoom(x))=x inverse relationship: compression is lossy in general, so Compression should be called re-abstraction, not an inverse, unless a lossless condition is established; proposes Q-lossless compression Obs_Q(K_x)=Obs_Q(Compress(K_x)) as the testable property instead.

b_rows_sample.anchor: query forces a resolution zoom event ... ExpansionNecessary(Q,x) iff the relevant contract-observable determination cannot be obtained from the parent representation but can be obtained from the admissible expanded representation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Replaces causal language ('query forces a zoom') with a testable necessity condition ExpansionNecessary(Q,x), and redesigns Axis D around D1 (resolution dependence), D2 (expansion necessity), D3 (compression adequacy), D4 (recursive re-basing).

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would not yet call the four things "operational primitives." Zero, Focus, Zoom, and Surface may turn out to be primitives, derived operations, or different views of a smaller underlying mechanism.
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against calling Zero/Focus/Zoom/Surface 'operational primitives' before irreducibility/derivability is tested, echoing the earlier kernel-minimization lesson that implementation components must not be mistaken for semantic capabilities.

b_rows_sample.anchor: x \longrightarrow K_x ... what appeared as d_1=x at one level becomes x=(x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_m) at the next level.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the founding recursive-zoom operation: a value x observed via Focus_{d_1}(K) can be re-based on (Zoom(K,x)=K_x) into a new knowledge state with its own dimensions, recursively repeatable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero at one level does not imply zero at a deeper level. ... Atomicity is representation-relative.
b_rows_sample.statement: States that neutralizing dimensions at one level (K=(d1,0,0)) says nothing about whether those dimensions' finer-resolution structure (revealed by zooming into d_1=x) is likewise zero, giving resolution-relative atomicity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: "The problem is inflation." ... Inflation=f(MoneySupply,Energy,SupplyChain,Wages,Demand,Expectations,...) ... "What determines energy prices?"
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example illustrating recursive re-basing in ordinary reasoning: a single named factor (inflation) becomes the object of inquiry, decomposing into further factors, one of which (energy price) becomes the next object of inquiry.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A value observed as atomic at one representational resolution may admit further dimensions, relations, causes, or explanatory structure under a finer resolution. Whether that refinement is actually infinite is a separate question.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly holds the claim of infinite recursive refinement as an open, separately-testable hypothesis rather than a mathematical fact, to avoid turning philosophical intuition into an untestable axiom.

b_rows_sample.anchor: An observed value is not necessarily an atomic knowledge object. It can be a compressed observation of another, potentially much richer knowledge state.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the central Recursive Epistemic Zoom hypothesis and the Compression/Zoom operator pair (C_Q(K)=x versus Z(x)=K_x), posing Z(C_Q(K)) =?= K as a research question rather than an assumed identity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: suppressed_zero_dimensions ... That silently turns projection into Zero. ... Better: excluded_dimensions ... or epistemically_silent_dimensions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a data-schema field name that would silently equate projection/exclusion with Zero; renames it and requires a separately recorded, independently tested Zero verdict.

b_rows_sample.anchor: exposure is not necessarily influence. A dimension can become visible without affecting the contract observable. ... Exposed \neq Relevant.
b_rows_sample.statement: Strengthens H3 (Zero-instability-across-resolution) to require an operative-relevance test (Obs_Q(T(K)) != Obs_Q(T(E^-_{d_j}(K)))) rather than accepting mere visibility of a previously silent dimension as evidence of relevance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_{r+1} successfully grounds subsequent inference cycles without referencing K_r ... That is not necessarily what recursive intelligence requires.
b_rows_sample.statement: Weakens H5 (recursive re-basing): the expanded state need not be independent of its parent context; the real test is whether K_{r+1} functions as an effective substrate for the next inquiry cycle, not whether K_r disappears.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Resolution transition ... Z_{Q,\tau}^{r\rightarrow r+1}: x_r \mapsto K_{r+1} ... Z_i Z_j \stackrel{?}{\equiv} Z_j Z_i
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces resolution-transition operators as the candidate central mathematical object, and explicitly connects Axis E's traversal-commutativity question to the Information Algebra extraction operators' idempotence/commutativity as an external baseline.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do NOT modify or ratify the KnowledgeOS constitutional kernel. Do NOT modify Theory v1.2. Do NOT promote any experimental hypothesis into a law, primitive, axiom, algebraic identity or kernel capability.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the governance boundary for KR-ZOOM-01: experimental/non-adjudicated status only, with an explicit prohibition on modifying the constitutional kernel or Theory v1.2.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do NOT represent excluded dimensions as algebraic zero. ... Therefore: Projection != Zero must remain an explicit methodological constraint.
b_rows_sample.statement: Hard-codes 'Projection != Zero' as an explicit methodological constraint of the experimental protocol itself, not merely a design note.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H1 Recursive Refinement ... H2 Resolution-Relative Atomicity ... H3 Zero Instability Across Resolution ... H4 Resolution-Dependent Determination ... H5 Recursive Re-basing ... H6 Q-Reconstruction
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the six KR-ZOOM-01 hypotheses with precise, falsifiable operational conditions, each explicitly requiring an intervention-based test rather than mere observation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The following statements are FORBIDDEN unless separately proven: "All observations have infinite dimensions." ... "Zoom is a topological operator." ... "Recursive Zoom is a kernel primitive."
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists ten specific overclaim statements the experiment execution is forbidden from asserting even if suggestive results appear, protecting the discovery-before-ratification discipline.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Use fixed independent random seeds. ... Do not tune the generator until hypotheses pass. ... If a generator defect is discovered: document it, repair it, regenerate, preserve the defect record. Do not silently replace results.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies reproducibility requirements (fixed seeds, train/test separation, no post-hoc generator tuning, defect preservation) and a 16-item mandatory audit checklist covering schema validity, replay determinism, hidden information, and correct application of typed elimination.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AUDIT-2 shows that anchoring zoom to a single dimension makes the counterfactual untestable by construction -- the exposed structure cannot differ when a non-anchor dimension is removed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports an executed KR-ZOOM-01 audit finding (AUDIT-2): anchoring the zoom operator to a single dominant dimension makes the retain/delete counterfactual test untestable by construction, since the exposed structure cannot vary when a non-anchor dimension is removed -- found by perturbing the operator's own definition, not by the Gita lens.
