a_rows_sample.anchor: STATISTICAL VERDICT: STRONG on framing, WEAK on inference; MEASUREMENT VERDICT: FAILS on the information measure
a_rows_sample.statement: Statistically, Section 208.6's sufficient-statistic analogy is immediately and correctly fenced ('this is an analogy, not a claim that DDD contracts are literally sufficient statistics') but left un-cashed (no Fisher-Neyman factorization or formal criterion transposed), and Section 208.23's handling of conflicting estimates is sound but uncited against prior statistical steps (025N, 082). Measurement-wise: I(.) has no declared scale type yet is compared (<) and subtracted (-) -- arithmetic NOT justified; result=0.91 in one block silently becomes confidence=0.91 in the very next (unjustified type conversion between a point estimate and a degree of belief); uncertainty=0.08 is silently converted into a symmetric +/-0.08 interval half-width in Step 210 Section 210.12, presupposing an unstated symmetric error distribution and coverage level; epistemic strength S(x) is compared with > (Section 208.9 forward) while Step 209 Section 209.21 later explicitly retracts any universal total ordering on the same kind of quantity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DDD VERDICT: STRONG — the best DDD content in the band; UBIQUITOUS-LANGUAGE: Evidence != Claim boxed, then violated two files later
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208's sufficiency-relative-to-responsibility (Section 208.4) is a correct, non-obvious Published-Language/conformist-boundary formulation; S_B ⊆ I(C(A)) ≪ I(A) (Section 208.5) is precisely the anti-Shared-Kernel constraint; Booleanization (Section 208.16) is a genuinely useful named anti-pattern; the four-layer split (Section 208.36) is a defensible strategic decomposition -- but none of it is mapped to Step 206's bounded contexts or Step 207's actual context contracts. Section 208.28 rules 'we should not collapse [Data/Information/Evidence/Assessment/KnowledgeClaim] into one generic object called Knowledge' -- a ruling violated two files later (Contradiction #1). Section 208.30 promotes Proposition to a first-class term; Section 208.29 boxes Evidence != Claim but gives it no owning context ('term without an owner').

a_rows_sample.anchor: ASSUMPTIONS / HIDDEN ASSUMPTIONS; UNDEFINED SYMBOLS in Step 208
a_rows_sample.statement: Stated assumptions: a contract is total and deterministic; information is set-like so subset applies; S_B is knowable a priori. Hidden assumptions: that an information measure exists at all (Section 208.10 defers it and nothing in the band supplies one); that provenance sets are finite and mergeable (required by P(A)∪P(E), never stated); that Valid(C) (Section 208.2) and SI(C,B) (Section 208.12) are different predicates, though the text slides between them; that 'legitimate responsibility' (Section 208.4) is externally given, smuggling the governance model into the definition of sufficiency. Undefined symbols: I(.) (deferred), S_B (depends on undefined 'legitimate'), T_1, A_I/G_I/D_I, Preserve(.), RequiredProvenance(R_C), Knowledge(E).

a_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT SURVIVES / WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE — Step 208
a_rows_sample.statement: Survives: Booleanization as a named anti-pattern; Suff(C,B,Task) (purpose-relative sufficiency); the four-layer split; Evidence != Claim; probability-of-proposition != truth-value-of-proposition; the explicit refusal to claim contracts are sufficient statistics; non-monotonicity as a requirement; the boxed claim 'the objective is not zero information loss, the objective is zero loss of relevant meaning' (the band's clearest and most durable architectural statement). Does not survive: L(C) as any quantity; I(A)<I(E) as a comparison; P(G)=P(A)∪P(E); the Section 208.37 'provisional architectural theorem' (Sufficiency+Provenance+Temporal Validity ⇒ Contract Safety), which is a definition dressed as an implication since Contract Safety is not independently defined -- not a theorem in any sense, a naming convention.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The symbol I is silently rebound between Step 208 (information measure) and Step 209 onward (invariant) with no announcement
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 uses I exclusively for an information measure (I(E), I(A), I_required, I_preserved); Step 209 onward uses I exclusively for invariants (I_L, I_C, I_S, I_i, I_identity, I1-I15, I(s)). The rebinding is never announced -- a reader comparing I(C(A)) (Section 208.4, information) to I(s)=True (Section 210.32, an invariant predicate) is reading two different symbols under one glyph.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A and Gap: eight bindings of A, four bindings of Gap with two different ordinal category sets
a_rows_sample.statement: A denotes: Assessment (208-212, throughout), an aggregate state A_t (209.13), the architecture-as-CSP set A (209.34), an assurance vector (211.9), an AI-artifact 7-tuple (211.21), a statistical-result 8-tuple (210.13), an architecture snapshot A_t (213.16-18), and an artifact A_j (213.4) -- eight bindings, with Section 209.13's aggregate-state A_t formally indistinguishable in notation from Section 213.17-18's architecture-state A_t (delta(A_t,c)=A_{t+1} vs A_0->A_1->...). Gap denotes: a numeric difference (211.4, 212.10), an ordinal category (211.4's {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical} vs 212.10's different {None,Partial,Significant,Critical,Unknown}), a class (212.11 G1-G5), and a register row (212.31 G-01-G-15) -- four bindings, with the two ordinal category sets differing from each other.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #1 — Knowledge as a generic object: forbidden in 208, used as an Owner in 210
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.28 boxes a prohibition: the Data->Information->Evidence->Assessment->KnowledgeClaim transformations of semantic status 'should not [be collapsed] into one generic object called Knowledge.' Step 210 Section 210.25's matrix row I11 nonetheless assigns Owner='Knowledge' (and row I3 compounds it with 'Knowledge infrastructure'), the exact generic object Step 208 boxed a prohibition against two files earlier in the same band. Severity HIGH; neither Step-206 bounded context, and neither file notices.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #2 — Provenance composition (208) excludes the authority Step 209 requires
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.25 asserts as an equality P(G)=P(A)∪P(E), boxed as 'provenance must be closed under semantic transformation.' Step 209 Section 209.4 requires Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D). Since Authority(D), the governance grant that made a decision final, is in neither P(A) nor P(E), a governed decision's provenance under Section 208.25 cannot contain its own authority, yet Step 209's own traceability requirement (Basis(D) including authority) demands that it does -- the two cannot both hold. Independently checked, the equality is additionally vacuous if closure holds (P(A)⊇P(E) implies the union is just P(A)) and self-refuting if it does not. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #14 — Subtraction on an undefined information measure, forbidden in Step 208 and performed anyway in Step 212
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.10 writes L(C)=I_required-I_preserved and immediately cautions 'we should not treat this as a literal numeric quantity until we define an information measure.' Step 212 Section 212.19 writes L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C) without that caveat and without citing 208.10 -- no information measure is defined anywhere in the intervening four files. This is the fourth occurrence of the pattern in the band (208.3's I(A)<I(E), 208.10, 212.19, and 214.7's SemanticLoss(A)>0). Severity MEDIUM-HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: STEP 208 load-bearing boxed claims: Semantic Sufficiency, the provisional Contract-Safety theorem, and the survivor 'zero loss of relevant meaning'
a_rows_sample.statement: Three load-bearing boxed claims of Step 208, adjudicated: (1) 'Semantic Sufficiency: S_B⊆I(C(A))' -- the file's central definition, resting on the undefined I(.) and the undefined 'legitimate responsibility' in S_B. (2) 'Semantic Sufficiency + Provenance Preservation + Temporal Validity ⇒ Contract Safety' -- self-labelled 'a provisional architectural theorem, not a mathematically proven theorem'; verifier judges it a stipulative definition of Contract Safety rather than an implication, since the consequent is not independently defined. (3) 'The objective is not zero information loss. The objective is zero loss of relevant meaning.' -- survives; the band's clearest and most durable architectural statement.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EL_i=(Step,Artifact,Observation,Fact,Derivation,Decision,Architecture,Invariant,Evidence,Status) ... EL=∪_i EL_i
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Evidence Ledger as a per-step 10-field record EL_i=(Step,Artifact,Observation,Fact,Derivation,Decision,Architecture,Invariant,Evidence,Status), with the overall ledger EL as the union across all steps, turning step 213's F/D/P/U discipline into a working data structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observation -> Fact -> Derivation -> Architectural Principle -> Invariant ... Invariant -> Implementation -> Test -> Evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: States the ledger's two-directional fundamental chain (forward: Observation->Fact->Derivation->Architectural Principle->Invariant; feedback: Invariant->Implementation->Test->Evidence->New Knowledge), diagrammed as the architecture's epistemic feedback loop.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge_t != Knowledge_{t+1} ... The fact that H_2 is better does not mean H_1 never existed
b_rows_sample.statement: States that the ledger must preserve chronology (when a belief was held), not only its content, since a later, better hypothesis H2 does not erase the historical fact that an earlier hypothesis H1 was held -- essential to reconstructing the real engineering journey rather than a retrospectively idealized one.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Calendar chronology ... Engineering chronology ... Epistemic chronology ... The code may exist before the architectural concept has been named
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three non-identical chronologies (calendar: when it happened; engineering: what was built before what; epistemic: when it was understood), illustrated by Implementation->Observation->Understanding, where code can precede the naming of its own underlying architectural concept.

b_rows_sample.anchor: implementation -> repeated problem -> experiment -> pattern recognized -> concept named ... The later name should not be projected backward as though it had been consciously designed from the beginning
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the 'late naming' phenomenon: a pattern can exist implicitly in the implementation before it is given a formal concept name, and warns against projecting the later name backward as if it had been consciously designed from the start, since that would distort the history.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | Field | Purpose | ... Rejected alternative | What was not chosen |
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives a practical 15-field Evidence Ledger schema (Step ID, Artifact, Date/sequence, Observation, Fact, Interpretation, Derived principle, Decision, Rejected alternative, Architectural consequence, Invariant, Verification, Evidence status F/D/P/U, Confidence, Open question).

b_rows_sample.anchor: What we rejected ... as by: What we selected ... That rejection itself is architectural knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues architecture is defined as much by what was rejected as by what was selected (e.g. Alternative A rejected because SemanticLoss(A)>0), justifying a dedicated 'Rejected alternative' ledger field as architectural knowledge in its own right.

b_rows_sample.anchor: NegativeKnowledge ... knowledge about approaches, assumptions, transitions or interpretations that have been demonstrated to be unsuitable under specified conditions ... different from failure
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces NegativeKnowledge as knowledge about approaches/assumptions/transitions/interpretations demonstrated unsuitable under specified conditions, distinguished from mere failure -- a failure becomes useful (negative) knowledge only once its cause ('why it failed') is understood.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment=(Hypothesis,Setup,Observation,Result,Interpretation,Consequence) ... Result -> Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-field experimental-lineage record (Hypothesis, Setup, Observation, Result, Interpretation, Consequence) intended to let the eventual book demonstrate the scientific/engineering nature of the work.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A hypothesis says: X may be true ... An invariant says: X must remain true ... Hypothesis -[evidence]-> Pattern -[validation]-> Invariant. Not every hypothesis becomes an invariant
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes hypothesis (X may be true) from invariant (X must remain true) and defines the promotion pipeline Hypothesis->(evidence)->Pattern->(validation)->Invariant, explicitly noting not every hypothesis is promoted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observed(H) does not imply Universal(H) ... AllAI -> InconsistentCode [is unwarranted from one tested workflow]
b_rows_sample.statement: States a statistical-discipline guardrail: evidence for H under tested conditions (Observed(H)) must not be generalized to Universal(H), illustrated by a prompt-strategy-specific inconsistency finding that must not be generalized to all AI.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Claim=(Proposition,Context,Conditions) ... Valid(C) should really mean: Valid(C | Context,Conditions)
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes representing every conclusion as Claim=(Proposition,Context,Conditions) so that validity is always conditioned (Valid(C|Context,Conditions) rather than bare Valid(C)), framed as a connection between DDD and statistical reasoning; extends this to bounded knowledge (Knowledge_A != Knowledge_B across DDD bounded contexts, requiring an explicit ubiquitous-language-guarded translation when a concept crosses a context boundary).

b_rows_sample.anchor: p(C_A) => p'(C_B) ... where p' is the explicitly defined interpretation in the target context. If that implication does not hold, the contract may introduce semantic loss
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a semantic-preservation condition for cross-context evidence transfer: a property p holding in context C_A after transformation T to C_B must imply the target-context-defined interpretation p' holds in C_B, or the contract introduces semantic loss; states evidence for a claim in one context does not automatically establish it in another without an explicit Mapping and evidence the property survives translation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ELG=(V,E) ... V=Artifacts∪Facts∪Observations∪Hypotheses∪Decisions∪Principles∪Invariants ... substantially richer than a conventional requirements traceability matrix
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Evidence Ledger as a graph ELG=(V,E) with seven node types (artifacts, facts, observations, hypotheses, decisions, principles, invariants) and seven edge types (supports, contradicts, derives, motivates, rejects, implements, verifies), explicitly positioned as richer than a conventional requirements traceability matrix.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C_1 <-[contradicts]-> C_2 ... We should not immediately delete one. Instead record: Contradiction(C_1,C_2) ... Sometimes the contradiction disappears once context is made explicit
b_rows_sample.statement: Treats contradiction as a first-class graph edge to be recorded rather than resolved by deletion; investigating Context(C_1) vs Context(C_2) can dissolve an apparent contradiction, and more generally an apparent contradiction (ModelA accurate vs inaccurate) can resolve into conditional coherence once Context/Population/Time/Purpose dimensions are introduced -- framed as contradiction potentially revealing a missing dimension.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Generation != Adjudication ... Candidates -> Evidence -> Adjudication -> AcceptedKnowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies the contradiction-as-evidence principle to AI-generated competing interpretations: rather than declaring one AI output true and another false, treats {AI_1,AI_2} as an explicit candidate knowledge set requiring adjudication, architecturally separating Generation from Adjudication via Candidates->Evidence->Adjudication->AcceptedKnowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KState in {Observed,Hypothesized,Derived,Corroborated,Contested,Rejected,Accepted,Deprecated} ... should not automatically be treated as a single linear lifecycle ... Accepted + Contested
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an eight-value knowledge-item epistemic state (Observed/Hypothesized/Derived/Corroborated/Contested/Rejected/Accepted/Deprecated), explicitly not a single linear lifecycle -- states may coexist, e.g. Accepted+Contested when knowledge is operationally accepted but still scientifically disputed; reiterates the anti-Boolean discipline (verified=true is insufficient; use KnowledgeState+Evidence+Context+Time).

b_rows_sample.anchor: UnderlyingPrinciple != CurrentManifestation ... The analogy helps us ask better architecture questions. It does not prove them
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies a Gita chapter-4 analogy (enduring knowledge vs changing manifestation) to DomainInvariant!=CurrentRuntimeState and HistoricalKnowledge!=CurrentRepresentation, explicitly bounding the analogy as interpretive/heuristic ('helps us ask better questions, does not prove them').

b_rows_sample.anchor: S_{t+1} does not contain all information about S_t ... S_{t+1} ⊉ S_t ... CurrentState + HistoricalRecord -> HistoricalUnderstanding
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the 'new state does not know old state' principle as S_{t+1} not-superset-of S_t in general, requiring an additional historical mechanism H_t; concludes CurrentState alone is insufficient and CurrentState+HistoricalRecord is needed for HistoricalUnderstanding, distinguishing CurrentState, HistoricalRecord, and HistoricalInterpretation as three different things.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t=(CurrentKnowledge_t,HistoricalKnowledge,Uncertainty_t) ... Update does not necessarily erase prior knowledge ... KnowledgeVersion [distinct from] KnowledgeState ... Git commit != current working tree
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a knowledge-continuity model K_t=(CurrentKnowledge_t,HistoricalKnowledge,Uncertainty_t) with K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E_{t+1}), where Update may supersede/qualify/contradict/preserve/deprecate rather than erase prior knowledge; proposes distinguishing KnowledgeVersion from KnowledgeState by analogy to a git commit vs the current working tree, again explicitly flagged as analogy not proof.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 3 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: each file's tail contains the agenda for the next step
a_rows_sample.statement: Structural observation, load-bearing for the whole verification: each file in the 208-215 band ends with the agenda section for the *next* step (e.g. the file titled 'Step 208' ends with a '# Step 209' section at line 1423 onward), so the band is a chain of overlapping documents and every 'Step N' agenda exists in two places (as the prior file's tail and the next file's own opening).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Cardinality drift: the 8-set I_KOS is silently superseded by a 15-list I1-I15 without amendment
a_rows_sample.statement: Probe (c-iii): Step 209 Section 209.42 boxes and freezes an 8-member invariant set I_KOS = {I_identity, I_version, I_provenance, I_temporal, I_epistemic, I_authority, I_decision, I_execution}. Step 210 Section 210.25 then tabulates 15 invariants I1-I15 with no mapping given between the 8 and the 15. Independently checked: I13 (illegal transitions rejected) and I14 (preconditions/postconditions) have no member of I_KOS to belong to, and I15 (no semantic strengthening) is likewise unhoused unless forced into I_epistemic. The 8-set is silently superseded by the 15-list without amendment; only Step 209's own caveat ('we should not freeze this yet') prevents this from being an outright contradiction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: POPULATED. 60 of 60 cells filled. ZERO '?', ZERO TBD. THE ALL-'?' PATTERN IS BROKEN.
a_rows_sample.statement: Probe (d): Step 210's 15-row invariant-verification matrix (lines 809-825) has 60 of 60 cells filled with zero placeholders -- a real, material departure from the corpus's prior pattern (Steps 108, 112, 114, 116, 121 all used all-'?' matrices), credited as a genuine corpus-level improvement.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The matrix realizes 3 of the 6 tuple components it is supposed to instantiate
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.1 boxes V_i = (I_i, O_i, E_i, M_i, T_i, F_i) (invariant, owner, enforcement mechanism, monitoring mechanism, test/verification, failure behaviour) but the rendered matrix has only 4 columns (ID, Invariant, Owner, Verification) realizing I_i, O_i, T_i -- E_i (enforcement), M_i (monitoring), and F_i (failure behaviour) are absent for all 15 invariants: 45 of the declared tuple components are unrealized. Enforcement is the one component that would distinguish an architectural property from an architectural principle, the exact distinction Step 210's own boxed opening claim rests on.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Verification column contains test NAMES, not test RESULTS
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210's Verification column lists 15 test names verbatim (identity transition test, version reconstruction, lineage traversal, semantic contract test, negative inference test, payload/semantic test, reproducibility test, privilege-path test, failure simulation, outcome verification, conflict test, historical replay, state-machine test, invariant test, transformation test) with zero results, zero of the fifteen tests existing as code, and none run (confirmed by Part 2's zero-executable-fences finding). Under TEST SPECIFIED != TEST EXECUTED: 15/15 specified, 0/15 executed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DDD CATEGORY ERROR IN THE 'Owner' COLUMN
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 206 Section 206.15 derives the candidate bounded-context set as Observation, Evidence, Assessment, Governance, Decision, Execution. Step 210's Owner column instead contains values like 'Domain' (a layer), 'Persistence/Domain' (two layers), 'Knowledge infrastructure' (a layer), 'Assessment/Contracts' (half artifact-kind), 'Aggregate' (a tactical pattern, not a party), and 'Contracts' (an artifact kind). Only 4 of 15 invariants (I5, I7, I8, I12) have a single, named bounded-context owner; seven (I1, I2, I3, I11, I13, I14, I15) have an owner entirely outside the derived context set, making them ownerless invariants under Step 212's own Section 212.15 criterion; five (I2, I4, I6, I9, I10) have slash-shared owners, Step 212's own Section 212.16 shared-ownership problem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 210's matrix instantiates, in 12 of its 15 rows, the two failure modes Step 212 names two files later — and neither file notices
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 212 Section 212.15 warns explicitly against 'Ownerless Invariants' (I exists but Owner(I) = empty set), yet Step 212 Section 212.4 reprints the same 15 invariants from Step 210 with the Owner column deleted entirely, and performs no such search -- discarding the exact data (Step 210's Owner column, with 7/15 ownerless and 5/15 shared) that would have triggered Step 212's own diagnosis.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Further arithmetic checks: 0.87>=0.80 correct; 0.91+/-0.08 within range at 1 sigma but 2-sigma bound exceeds 1; ratio checks disclaimed
a_rows_sample.statement: Additional independently-verified arithmetic in the band: Step 209 Section 209.15's 0.87 >= 0.80 evaluates to True (correct). Step 208 Section 208.14 / Step 210 Section 210.12's 0.91 +/- 0.08 gives [0.83, 0.99], within [0,1] at 1-sigma, but at 2-sigma the upper bound is 1.07 > 1 -- out of range for a quantity called 'confidence', though the corpus never commits this specific error since the interval's coverage level is left unlabelled. Step 215 Section 215.24's ratios (182/43=4.233, 43/17=2.529, 17/8=2.125, 8/4=2.0, total 45.5x) make no arithmetic claim and are correctly disclaimed as unknown. Step 209 Section 209.42 vs Step 210 Section 210.25: |I_KOS|=8 vs |{I1..I15}|=15, difference 7, mapping absent (unreconciled).

a_rows_sample.anchor: PREVIOUS DEPENDENCY: 1 (Step 208 only); LATER RESPONSE: Step 210 replaces I_KOS with I1-I15 without amendment
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 cites exactly one prior step (Step 208) and zero prior invariant families. Later response in scope: Step 210 Section 210.25 replaces the 8-member I_KOS with a 15-row I1-I15 without amendment; Step 210 Section 210.9 restates Step 209's Section 209.25 semantic-strength principle as Strength(T(x))>Strength(x) requires Justified(T); Step 212 Section 212.4 reprints I1-I15.

a_rows_sample.anchor: FORMAL OBJECTS: Architectural Principle != Architectural Property; V_i=(I_i,O_i,E_i,M_i,T_i,F_i); Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 ('Invariant Verification Matrix') defines a 6-tuple V_i=(I_i,O_i,E_i,M_i,T_i,F_i) per invariant; boxes 'Architectural Principle != Architectural Property' and 'No claim of architectural compliance without identifiable evidence'; defines Reachable(D,E)!=empty; boxes 'Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity' and 'Epistemic state cannot be silently strengthened'; states Strength(T(x))>Strength(x) requires Justified(T); boxes 'Quantitative value without relevant uncertainty may constitute semantic loss'; defines a statistical-result 8-tuple A=(theta-hat,Estimator,Sample,Population,Model,Assumptions,Uncertainty,Validity); boxes 'Documentation < ExecutableEvidence < FormalProof'; a conceptual Assurance(I)=f(Evidence,Coverage,Independence,Repeatability,Criticality); an E_1..E_5 evidence hierarchy (documentation..formal verification); the target for-all-s-in-S_reachable: I(s)=True; and boxes 'AI may assist assurance; AI should not be the sole source of assurance', plus the 15-row invariant-verification matrix itself (60/60 cells filled).

a_rows_sample.anchor: LATER RESPONSE IN SCOPE: Step 211 reverses Test/Evidence order; Step 212 drops the Owner column and recalibrates E_n
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 cites only Step 209 by number ('up to Step 209, we have asked...'). Later response: Step 211 Section 211.2 restates the assurance chain with Test before Evidence, contradicting Step 210's own Section 210.40; Step 212 Section 212.4 reprints I1-I15 minus the Owner column; Step 212 Section 212.6 re-mints an E_0..E_5 scale with different rung definitions than Step 210 Section 210.30's E_1..E_5.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EVOLUTION/DEFINITION VERDICT: CLEAR on the principle/property distinction, CONTRADICTORY on E_1..E_5 (twice)
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 answers 'where' (role names) and 'how proven' (test names) but not 'is it true' for any invariant. CLEAR: the principle/property distinction (its best contribution), Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity, the three assurance levels. INCOMPLETE: V_i is 6-ary, only 3 components ever instantiated. AMBIGUOUS: 'Owner' is used as bounded context, layer, pattern, and team interchangeably. CONTRADICTORY: E_1..E_5 vs Step 212's E_0..E_5 (Contradiction #3), and E_1 bound to two incompatible types within Step 210 itself (Contradiction #4: Section 210.20's evidence-item E_1 vs Section 210.30's documentation-rung E_1).

a_rows_sample.anchor: FIRST INVALID INFERENCE: Section 210.30 vs 210.20 (E_n ambiguity); honest gaps in 210.26/210.28/210.29
a_rows_sample.statement: Section 210.20 uses E_1⇒P and E_2⇒¬P as evidence items; Section 210.30, ten sections later, binds E_1=documentation...E_5=formal verification as evidence-strength levels -- the same subscripted symbol carries two incompatible types with no disambiguation, and every downstream use of E_n in Steps 212-214 inherits the ambiguity. Section 210.29 honestly declines to scalarize Assurance and names fake precision (Assurance=97.3%) as a hazard, yet Section 210.28 immediately prior writes Critical(I)⇒HigherAssurance(I), a comparison requiring the very ordering Section 210.29 declines. Section 210.26 correctly concedes a test provides evidence, not proof (Test(I_8)=PASS does not prove I_8=True in all states), then Section 210.32's target for-all s in S_reachable: I(s)=True leaves S_reachable undetermined (Section 210.33 concedes this openly) -- an honest, correctly-labelled gap, not an invalidity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: COMPUTABILITY: highest rung reached is INPUTS_KNOWN, for I_i/O_i as strings only; 15 tests specified, 0 run
a_rows_sample.statement: V_i is DEFINED with 3/6 components at INPUTS_KNOWN (role-name granularity); the I1-I15 matrix is DEFINED->INPUTS_KNOWN (names) but not CONSTRUCTIBLE (no mechanism/code/test); Assurance(I) is DEFINED but explicitly barred from numeric evaluation; S_reachable is DEFINED but conceded as the open challenge, not CONSTRUCTIBLE. The highest rung reached anywhere in Step 210 is INPUTS_KNOWN, and only for I_i and O_i as strings. TEST VERDICT NOT_EXECUTED: 15 tests specified by name, 0 written, 0 run; Section 210.16's negative test ('can an AI-generated Assessment directly invoke an execution command? Expected: False') is designed in prose and never run against anything.

a_rows_sample.anchor: STATISTICAL VERDICT: STRONG (the 8-tuple A=(theta-hat,...,Validity) is the best statistical section in the band); two correct refusals and two measurement violations
a_rows_sample.statement: Section 210.13's 8-tuple statistical result A=(theta-hat,Estimator,Sample,Population,Model,Assumptions,Uncertainty,Validity) is correct and genuinely good statistical practice, rarely done in architecture documents, but never carried into the matrix (which collapses all eight back into one row) and never connected to the corpus's prior statistical steps (025N, 074, 082, uncited). Correct refusals: Section 210.29 declines to scalarize Assurance (names fake precision explicitly); Section 210.27's Documentation<ExecutableEvidence<FormalProof is a properly-used ordinal. Violations: Section 210.28's Critical(I)⇒HigherAssurance(I) compares assurance levels the same file declines to scale; the E_1<...<E_5 ladder (Section 210.30) is re-issued by Step 212 Section 212.6 with different rung contents and an added E_0 -- the same ordinal scale has two incompatible calibrations in the band, making any statement 'we have E_2 evidence' uninterpretable without knowing which file it was written under -- a scale-integrity failure that silently corrupts later aggregation. The 15-row matrix itself carries no scale at all (purely nominal, no arithmetic attempted -- correct).

a_rows_sample.anchor: DDD VERDICT: MIXED — strong distinctions (Architectural Principle != Property; Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity; Memory/Identity/History split), weak ownership
a_rows_sample.statement: Architectural Principle != Architectural Property is exactly the right DDD-governance move; Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity (Section 210.5, a foreign key proves existence not that this version was the artifact used) is a real and useful insight; Section 210.39's Memory/Identity/History separation, concluding the current domain object need not carry all history internally, is correct DDD (event sourcing / separate read model), well argued. Against this, the Owner column's category error means only 4/15 invariants have a single bounded-context owner, 7/15 are owned by a layer or pattern (which cannot be accountable), 5/15 are slash-shared, and I13/I14 are owned by 'Aggregate' -- a tactical pattern name is never the answer to 'who is accountable' in DDD.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ASSUMPTIONS / HIDDEN ASSUMPTIONS / UNDEFINED SYMBOLS — Step 210
a_rows_sample.statement: Stated: each invariant has exactly one owner; a test name determines a test; enforcement can be located by inspection. Hidden: that the 15 invariants are the right 15 (no derivation from I_KOS's 8, no completeness claim); that S_reachable is finite or tractable (required by the for-all quantifier, false for unbounded state); that Owner and Enforcement are separable -- the matrix drops Enforcement and keeps Owner, implicitly assuming Owner=Enforcement, which Step 211 Section 211.29 later denies ('Invariant->Owner present but Enforcement missing = a design gap'), meaning by Step 211's own criterion all 15 rows of Step 210's matrix are design gaps. Undefined symbols: Justified(T), Strength(x), Critical(I), HigherAssurance(I), Coverage/Independence/Repeatability, S_reachable, Estimator/Sample/Population/Validity, DA's codomain Result.

a_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT SURVIVES / WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE — Step 210, including the word 'Matrix' itself
a_rows_sample.statement: Survives: Architectural Principle != Architectural Property; Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity; Documentation<ExecutableEvidence<FormalProof; the 8-component statistical result tuple; the refusal of test-as-proof; the refusal to scalarize assurance; the Memory/Identity/History split; the 15 invariant names as a working checklist. Does not survive: the Owner column (11/15 rows unusable); the Verification column as evidence of anything (0/15 executed); V_i as a realized 6-tuple (3/6 realized); E_1..E_5 as a stable scale; and the word 'Matrix' in the title -- a 4-column table realizing 3 of 6 declared dimensions, with no status and no results, is a checklist.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The most damaging collision is E-binding #2 vs #5, which occurs INSIDE ONE FILE (Step 210)
a_rows_sample.statement: Of the twelve distinct bindings of the glyph E catalogued across the band, the most damaging collision is internal to a single file: Step 210 Section 210.20 writes E_1⇒P (an evidence item entailing a proposition), and Step 210 Section 210.30, ten sections later, writes E_1=documentation (the weakest rung of an assurance ladder) -- same symbol, same file, incompatible types, no disambiguation, no notice.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The symbol I is silently rebound between Step 208 (information measure) and Step 209 onward (invariant) with no announcement
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 uses I exclusively for an information measure (I(E), I(A), I_required, I_preserved); Step 209 onward uses I exclusively for invariants (I_L, I_C, I_S, I_i, I_identity, I1-I15, I(s)). The rebinding is never announced -- a reader comparing I(C(A)) (Section 208.4, information) to I(s)=True (Section 210.32, an invariant predicate) is reading two different symbols under one glyph.

b_rows_sample.anchor: F | D | P | U ... F = Fact ... D = Derived ... P = Proposed ... U = Unknown
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a four-way epistemic classification for every architectural statement: F=Fact (directly supported by engineering evidence), D=Derived (logically derived from facts/observations), P=Proposed (a recommendation or future design), U=Unknown (insufficient evidence).

b_rows_sample.anchor: We designed the system according to this architecture from the beginning ... That would be misleading. The intellectually stronger story is: Experience -> Problem -> Observation -> Experiment -> Pattern -> Abstraction -> Theory -> Architecture
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against retrospectively rewriting the book's history as if the system had been designed according to the derived architecture from the beginning, calling this misleading; proposes instead the causal chain Experience->Problem->Observation->Experiment->Pattern->Abstraction->Theory->Architecture as the intellectually stronger and more honest narrative.

b_rows_sample.anchor: How can this artifact support our current theory? We should ask: What does this artifact actually establish?
b_rows_sample.statement: States the archaeological method's central mindset shift: treat prior artifacts (prompts, AI outputs, architecture docs, ADRs, code, tests, rejected ideas, contradictions, revisions) as evidence to be asked 'what does this actually establish', never 'how does this support our current theory'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: E(A_j)={Facts,Observations,Decisions,Assumptions,Experiments,Failures,Questions} ... Artifact -> Evidence -> Interpretation. Not: Theory -> selective evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines evidence extraction per artifact E(A_j) as the set {Facts,Observations,Decisions,Assumptions,Experiments,Failures,Questions}, to be connected to architectural concepts only afterward (Artifact->Evidence->Interpretation), explicitly rejecting the reverse flow Theory->selective evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance enforcement could not yet be established from the available evidence ... unless we have evidence of absence
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires that absence of knowledge about whether a property (e.g. provenance) exists in an implementation be written as Unknown ('could not yet be established from the available evidence'), never as an assertion of absence ('is missing') unless positive evidence of absence exists.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Prov(C)={A_1,A_2,...,A_n} ... provenance of architecture itself
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes giving architectural claims themselves a provenance set Prov(C)={A_1,...,A_n} of supporting artifacts, so a reader can trace Claim->Evidence -- termed 'provenance of architecture itself'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ADL = Decision -> Problem -> Evidence -> Alternatives -> Rationale -> Consequence
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an Architecture Decision Lineage ADL = Decision->Problem->Evidence->Alternatives->Rationale->Consequence, proposed to eventually become part of the KnowledgeOS architecture itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Failure -> Knowledge ... some of the strongest architectural principles may originate from failed approaches ... What did not work ... alongside ... What eventually worked. Otherwise the final architecture looks inevitable
b_rows_sample.statement: States the negative-result principle: a failed experiment (Hypothesis H tested, Result=not-H) is Failure->Knowledge, not useless, and some of the strongest architectural principles may originate from failed approaches; the book should explicitly record what did not work alongside what eventually worked, because otherwise the final architecture looks falsely inevitable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ChosenPattern ... RejectedPattern ... ReasonForRejection
b_rows_sample.statement: Connects the negative-result principle to the corpus's Chapter 4 theme: knowledge includes discrimination between Valid and Invalid, so the architecture should preserve not only the ChosenPattern but sometimes the RejectedPattern and ReasonForRejection.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A_{t+1}=E(A_t, Evidence_t) ... Architecture is not merely documentation growth. It is knowledge evolution
b_rows_sample.statement: Models architecture evolution as A_{t+1}=E(A_t,Evidence_t) driven by new evidence, explicitly rejecting the weaker model A_{t+1}=A_t+more documentation; calls architecture 'knowledge evolution', not documentation growth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ΔA=(Trigger,Evidence,Decision,Rationale,Impact)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an architecture-evolution tuple DeltaA=(Trigger,Evidence,Decision,Rationale,Impact) as the architecture's evolutionary provenance record for each change.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Stage 1 ... What problem was first recognized? ... Stage 7 What remains unverified?
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes reconstructing an 'epistemic chronology' (not necessarily calendar chronology) in seven stages: problem recognized, assumptions made, experiments challenging them, patterns emerged, abstractions introduced, resulting architecture, and what remains unverified -- proposed as the backbone of the eventual book.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observed Reality ... Architectural Interpretation ... Normative Design
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates three reconstruction layers: Observed Reality (what happened), Architectural Interpretation (what it means), and Normative Design (what should be built), illustrated with an AI-code-inconsistency example running observation->derived-knowledge->proposal.

b_rows_sample.anchor: O=observations ... D=g(O)=derived knowledge ... P=h(D)=proposed architecture ... P ⇏ O
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes O->D->P (observations, derived knowledge via D=g(O), proposed architecture via P=h(D)) with the explicit non-implication P does-not-imply O: a proposal cannot retroactively become evidence for the observation that motivated it, protecting the book from circular reasoning (e.g. avoiding 'we need deterministic assurance because KnowledgeOS is a deterministic assurance platform').

b_rows_sample.anchor: C_fact=High if directly supported by primary implementation evidence ... C_derived=Medium if the inference depends on assumptions ... avoid false numerical precision
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a qualitative confidence label (e.g. C_fact=High, C_derived=Medium) attached to F/D/P/U claims only when justified, again warning against false numerical precision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Primary ... source code; configuration; database schema; test result; runtime behavior; direct experiment ... Secondary ... AI analysis; architecture summary; meeting notes; retrospective explanation. Secondary evidence ... should not silently override primary evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Primary evidence (source code, configuration, database schema, test result, runtime behavior, direct experiment) from Secondary evidence (AI analysis, architecture summary, meeting notes, retrospective explanation), warning that secondary evidence must not silently override primary evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AIClaim -> Hypothesis. Then: ImplementationEvidence -> Fact ... AI Interpretation != Engineering Evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: States that an AI-generated statement (e.g. Claude or DeepSeek claiming 'the system uses invariant-driven architecture') is not itself proof but a hypothesis, only becoming Fact once corroborated by implementation evidence; boxes the AI epistemic boundary AI Interpretation != Engineering Evidence as one of the book's strongest intended methodological principles.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We are using AI to reconstruct an architecture for an AI engineering platform ... The architecture is therefore being used to validate the method by which it is being reconstructed ... The method is correct because it follows the architecture [is circular]
b_rows_sample.statement: Notes the self-referential situation of using AI to reconstruct the architecture of an AI engineering platform (a useful meta-level experiment), then explicitly warns against circular validation ('the method is correct because it follows the architecture'); the reconstruction method must independently satisfy Evidence+Reproducibility+Traceability before it can be said to exemplify the architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EAG=(Evidence,Claims,Decisions,Invariants,Architecture) ... Invariant -> Test -> Evidence. This creates a closed assurance loop
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Architecture Assurance Graph into an Evidence-Architecture-Graph EAG=(Evidence,Claims,Decisions,Invariants,Architecture) with edges Evidence->Claim->Decision->Architecture->Invariant and potentially Invariant->Test->Evidence, closing the assurance loop, then generalizes to the full cycle Observation->Knowledge->Architecture->Invariant->Implementation->Test->Evidence->NewKnowledge, calling architecture 'a learning system'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Learning -> ArchitectureDrift ... Architecture evolution must itself be governed
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns that ungoverned architectural learning becomes ArchitectureDrift, boxing the principle that architecture evolution must itself be governed, and lists six questions a software change should answer (what changed, why, which invariant is affected, which bounded context owns it, what evidence justifies it, how was it verified) as a stronger Software Change Governance model.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 3 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: Subject: Shipment S ... Decision: RELEASE ... Authorization: APPROVED ... Action: EXECUTED ... Outcome: CARRIER ACCEPTED ... RELEASE SHIPMENT S ... SHIPMENT S WAS RELEASED SUCCESSFULLY. ... this outcome is not produced directly from an AI answer, a retrieved document, or a rule match. It is the resu
a_rows_sample.statement: 21A.33 (new): presents a structured Final Decision Record (Subject, Determination, Determination Status, Decision, Authorization, Action, Shipment Status, Outcome, Rule Version, Proof, Release Gap) summarizing the entire worked example, concluding with the explicit outcomes 'RELEASE SHIPMENT S' and 'SHIPMENT S WAS RELEASED SUCCESSFULLY', and stressing this outcome is the product of the entire controlled Evidence->Premises->Reasoning->Proof->Verification->Determination->Decision->Authorization->Action->Outcome chain, not of an AI answer, retrieved document, or rule match alone.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Never store only the answer when the system is expected to preserve why the answer was justified. ... Every consequential conclusion should be traceable backward to its evidence and forward to its consequences. ... A KnowledgeOS reasoning engine must preserve the derivation, not merely the conclusio
b_rows_sample.statement: 21A.31: closes with the rule 'never store only the answer when the system is expected to preserve why the answer was justified'; restates the canonical Evidence->Premise->Rule->Derivation->Proof->Verification->Determination->Decision->Authorization->Action chain alongside an 11-row table of the distinct question each layer answers (Evidence: what supports this? ... Observation: what happened afterward?); concludes with the boxed traceability principle (every consequential conclusion traceable backward to evidence and forward to consequences) and the deepest architectural requirement of Part XXI: 'a KnowledgeOS reasoning engine must preserve the derivation, not merely the conclusion.'
